Renting in Maryland
Facing an eviction

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides zero percent interest loans or grants to help seniors make their homes more accessible and functional, allowing them to remain independent in their homes as they age. Funding addresses critical accessibility improvements for owner-occupied primary residences.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years to finance accessibility improvements, or grants up to $25,000. Loans may cover up to 110 percent of the property value and must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans generally do not exceed $50,000. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on applicant's ability to pay. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their primary residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements such as widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, lever handles, and first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms. Also covers access for disabled and seniors, inclusive of chair lifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, and doors, as well as fall and injury prevention items like handrails, rubber treads, and bathroom grab bars.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, including Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) and rest of state
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one resident age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered case by case)
Reside in a home that is structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
Not have outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure

Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington DC MSA median (for interest rates 4.5%-6%) or 60 percent of median (for interest rates 0%-4.5%). Income limits vary by household size and location
Provide proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement)
Provide photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant
Provide current property tax bill and homeowners insurance policy declaration page
Provide flood insurance policy if applicable
Provide contractor bid(s) from licensed Maryland tradesperson or company documenting repairs; bid should not be more than 60 days old and grand total should not exceed $50,000
Contractor must provide current MHIC License or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with minimum $1M per occurrence limits, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain completed application form available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. 2. Complete all required sections of the application including income, assets, liabilities, and applicant information. 3. Gather required supporting documentation including income verification (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, award letters as applicable), proof of home ownership, photo IDs, property and insurance documentation, and contractor bid(s) with required contractor documentation. 4. Submit completed application with all documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 5. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency or through an in-home appointment. 6. The application is processed by the department and the applicant will be contacted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) provides strategic investment in local housing and businesses to support healthy, sustainable communities with growing tax bases and improved quality of life. The program focuses on areas where coordinated investment and strategy will have meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact, targeting designated Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City and the inner beltway areas of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for community development projects that support neighborhood revitalization, including down payment assistance for home buyers, property acquisition or rehabilitation programs, energy efficiency improvements through weatherization and retrofits, mixed-use development combining housing and retail space, community open space or public infrastructure development, workforce and employment development, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.contact_email: jessica.degaine@maryland.gov, katherine.howard@maryland.gov, sarah.kim1@maryland.gov, erin.lavitt@maryland.gov, sara.jackson@maryland.gov, jean.cannon@maryland.gov, maria.mougridis@maryland.gov, jessica.argueta@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support various activities, including: down payment assistance to attract home buyers; acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties; improvement of residential and business properties; energy efficiency through weatherization and retrofits; mixed-use development combining housing, retail, and office space; community open space or public infrastructure development; workforce and employment development; strategic demolition; and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to view BRNI boundaries. Contact your Regional Project Manager to confirm specific address eligibility.
requirements_list: Community Development Organization must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
If organization does not have an approved plan, it must submit one at time of application
Strategic neighborhood revitalization plan must be approved by the Department prior to any funding awards
Projects must be part of the approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
Projects should capitalize on community strengths and be targeted to specific neighborhoods
Applying with partner organizations, like Community Development Financial Institutions and cross-jurisdictional partners, is strongly recommended
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan submit applications for projects in eligible areas. Organizations without an approved plan must submit the plan along with project requests at time of application. Organizations are encouraged to apply with partner organizations including Community Development Financial Institutions and cross-jurisdictional partners. For more information on how to apply, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Contact your Regional Project Manager to confirm specific address eligibility. Regional Project Managers are organized by region: Region 1 (Northwest Baltimore City and County), Region 2 (Northeast Baltimore City and County), Region 3 (Southeast Baltimore City and County), Region 4 (Southwest Baltimore City and County and Northern Anne Arundel), Region 5 (Western Maryland), Region 6 (Southern Maryland), Region 7 (Eastern Shore), and Region 8 (Central Maryland).

The program supports revitalization of vacant properties to increase housing supply and neighborhood stability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to public and nonprofit partners for acquisition, stabilization, demolition, and pre-development activities on vacant properties to support affordable housing, green space, and mixed-use development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and nonprofit partners in Baltimore City working to address vacant properties and rehabilitate vacant residential properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, demolition, and pre-development activities on vacant properties to create green space or support affordable housing and mixed-use developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Project must be located in Baltimore

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest financing to help homeowners improve the energy efficiency and comfort of their homes by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating and cooling systems, insulation, and other energy-saving measures. Homeowners can save on utility bills and improve home livability and safety through these improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% APR for up to $30,000 in financing available for energy efficiency measures with a term up to 10 years (borrower can choose term length). Minimum loan amount is $5,000. The loan cannot finance projects or upgrades that have already been purchased or completed. Initial disbursement is a 30% down payment check (2-Party check with borrower and contractor names, or 1-Party check for retail purchases). Final 70% is disbursed after project completion and submission of Certificate of Completion. There are no pre-payment penalties, and borrowers can avoid interest by paying off the loan early. Solar photovoltaic projects can only be financed up to 50% of the total loan amount (1:1 match to other energy efficiency costs). Health and safety costs related to energy improvements (such as mold remediation or radon mitigation) can be included up to 25% of the total loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who want to improve energy efficiency and comfort in their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances (note: no ENERGY STAR compliant stoves, ovens, or microwave ovens are available), windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installation (capped at 50% of total loan or 1:1 match to other energy efficiency costs), health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan amount), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
Unsecured loan based on verification of credit and ability to pay
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland (proof of license and insurance required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online BeSMART Loan Application and provide a copy of your Driver's License, 30 days of pay stubs, and a recent mortgage statement. You will receive a DocuSign document to securely provide your Social Security number and authorize a credit report check. Submit an estimate or proposal from your contractor or retailer for the work or appliances you wish to finance. Once approved, sign and return the loan documents sent by DHCD. DHCD sends you an initial 30% down payment check (2-Party check with your name and contractor's name for contracted work, or 1-Party check to you for retail purchases only). Upon project completion, you and your contractor sign Certificates of Completion and submit photos. DHCD then issues the remaining 70% payment check. After receiving funds, you begin making loan payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant is a microgrant program offered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program that provides funding to support small businesses seeking capital for growth and expansion opportunities. The program particularly supports home-based businesses looking to establish their first commercial location outside the home. Microgrants range from $20,000 to $50,000, with a total of up to $2,000,000 available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 are provided to support small businesses seeking capital for growth and expansion opportunities. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024 to March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. However, only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses are not. The total program offers up to $2,000,000 in funding. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Businesses must have more than 2 employees and no more than 50 employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024, annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million, and be located in a Sustainable Communities area. Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025, with grant payments expected in February-March 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application round is projected to close on Monday, October 14th, 2024, at 5 PM EST. The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses with growth and expansion plans, particularly home-based businesses looking to establish a first commercial location outside the home. New and expanding small businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities with more than 2 employees and 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees, annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Funds must be used for new expenses only (increased rent, increased payroll for new hires, new equipment, marketing boosts). Existing expenses such as current rent and payroll are not eligible unless they represent increases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a designated Sustainable Communities area in Maryland. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify if a business location qualifies. Enter your business address in the incentive look-up tool to confirm eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit business demonstrating plans for growth
Must be a new or expanding small business located in a designated Sustainable Community
Must be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland
Must have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Must have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Must have annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must be in good financial and legal standing with no past due amounts, liens, or judgments
Professional services and sales-based businesses (including Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, Finance) are not eligible

Non-profit organizations, cannabis-based businesses, pawn shops, gun shops, massage parlors, adult video/book shops, adult entertainment facilities, tanning salons, check-cashing facilities, gambling facilities, tattoo parlors, and liquor stores are not eligible
Previous award winners of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant and an NBW Business Boost grant are not eligible
Must provide Articles of Organization
Must provide By-laws
Must provide most recent annual tax return (Tax year 2023)
Must provide financial statements as of August 31, 2024
Must provide screenshot showing business is in an eligible location
Must provide proof of matching funds (bank statement as of August 31, 2024 or fully executed loan statement from financial institution)
Must provide screenshot of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must provide IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
Business name on application and W-9 must exactly match SDAT's Good Standing Certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application round opens Monday, September 23, 2024 at 12:00 noon and closes Monday, October 14, 2024 at 5 PM EST (may close sooner if funding is exhausted). Applicants create an account and submit applications online at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. Only fully completed applications at the time of submission will be considered; incomplete applications will be returned. Applications are evaluated based on eligibility requirements, business financials, and supporting documents. Priority funding is based on: (1) business location, (2) impact of business expansion (new employees, capital investment, additional square footage), (3) presentation of financials and supporting documents, and (4) priority impact attributes including innovative businesses, businesses in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBE). Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. If awarded, DHCD will seek local governing body approval via resolution. Grant payments are expected February-March 2025. Awardees must submit a final report by March 31, 2026 and complete a questionnaire nine months after receiving funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Hurricane Sandy
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provided funding to help Somerset County and other affected Maryland counties recover from the damage caused by Hurricane Sandy, which struck the eastern seaboard on October 28, 2012. The state received a total of $28.64 million from Congress through the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development through the Community Development Block Grant Program. Funds were designated for housing recovery, economic recovery, infrastructure improvements, and other community development and disaster recovery activities in the most impacted and distressed areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state received $28.64 million in federal CDBG-DR funding for community development and disaster recovery activities related to Hurricane Sandy and other eligible storm events in 2011-2013. The first allocation of $8.64 million (Disaster Grant #1) was targeted entirely to Somerset County. A second allocation of $20 million (Disaster Grant #2) was distributed across multiple counties with at least 80% going to Somerset County. Funds were used for: Housing recovery programs providing deferred loans to rehabilitate or replace homes damaged by the hurricane (for homeowners with household income not exceeding 80% of area median income); Economic recovery activities including grants to watermen (up to $2,500), facade improvement grants (up to $5,000), and business loans (up to $60,000 interest-free for up to 10 years); Public services including job training activities; Infrastructure improvements including waterway improvements, drainage projects, water/sewer system improvements, street repairs, and broadband extension; Public facilities reconstruction including homeless shelters and Head Start facilities; and Planning activities including housing studies, strategic economic analyses, drainage studies, and feasibility studies. Housing assistance was provided as deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property after the grant was closed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program window closed; distribution period extended to October 1, 2022 for expenditure of remaining funds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and organizations in affected Maryland counties (Somerset, Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, and Garrett) recovering from Hurricane Sandy damage, particularly low and moderate income persons, watermen, small businesses, and non-profit organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing recovery (rehabilitation and replacement of hurricane-damaged homes); Economic recovery (grants and loans for impacted businesses and watermen); Job training; Public facilities reconstruction (homeless shelters, Head Start facilities); Infrastructure improvements (waterway stabilization, drainage systems, water/sewer systems, streets, broadband); Planning and feasibility studies; and State administrative costs. Funds could only be used for unmet recovery needs not covered by FEMA, SBA, private insurance, or other sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All funds were targeted to the most impacted and distressed areas. Disaster Grant #1 ($8.64 million) was used entirely for Somerset County, which was the only Maryland county declared eligible for FEMA Individual Assistance. Disaster Grant #2 ($20 million) required that 80% be spent in Somerset County, with remaining funds available to Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, and Garrett Counties through a competitive process, with the majority going to infrastructure projects. Somerset County experienced unprecedented 7-foot storm surges and the most significant damage from Hurricane Sandy in Maryland.
requirements_list: Proof of storm damage to property or business
Proof of homeownership or business ownership
Household income not exceeding 80% of area median income for Somerset County (for housing assistance)
Residence in affected county
No duplication of benefits from other federal, state, or private sources
Compliance with floodplain management and future sea level rise considerations for mitigation and resilience
For business loans: demonstrated need and ability to repay
For housing assistance: property must be brought to livability code standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This was a retrospective program distributed through established recovery processes managed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development in coordination with Somerset County and other affected counties. Recovery activities were implemented through multiple phases of action plans approved by HUD between 2013 and 2018. Applications for specific assistance (housing rehabilitation, business loans, etc.) were processed by Somerset County on a first-come, first-served basis. Housing assistance applicants needed to document storm damage, prove homeownership, and verify income eligibility. Business applicants needed to document business damage and income eligibility. The County worked with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on infrastructure projects. Program amendments were made through HUD-approved Action Plan amendments with public comment periods.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds help strengthen Maryland communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods and improving overall quality of life. The program is designed to assist county and municipal governments with activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, housing opportunities, economic development and improved public facilities and services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State receives annual Congressional allocations and distributes federal funds to non-entitlement counties, small cities, and towns through two competitive categories: Community Development (accepted once per year) and Special Projects (submitted anytime after written approval). The state must cumulatively use at least 70% of its allocation to benefit low-income and moderate-income persons over a three-year period. For SFY 2026/FFY 2025, the State allocated $7,416,560 distributed as follows: State Administration (2% + $100,000) = $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%) = $74,165; Community Development (82% - $100,000) = $6,000,000; Special Projects (15%) = $1,094,064. Funds are provided primarily as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions to meet their needs. Grantees must use CDBG funds for reasonable and necessary costs only.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development Applications accepted once each year; Special Projects accepted anytime after written approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Public or private entities may be sub-recipients of eligible local government. Eligible subrecipients include governmental agencies, non-profit organizations with IRS Section 501(c)(3) status, Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs), Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and for-profit businesses in good standing for economic development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing (single-family rehabilitation, rental housing construction, acquisition/renovation/resale programs, homeownership assistance); public facilities (water/sewer systems, streets, childcare centers, senior centers, community centers, shelters); economic development projects; and public services. All funded projects must benefit persons of low-to-moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety. Maximum CDBG funds per house for acquisition, renovation and resale programs is $200,000. Maximum grant per house for single-family owner-occupied rehabilitation is $40,000 (no maximum loan amount). Grantees may use up to 25% of award for emergency repairs in housing rehabilitation programs if approved.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-entitlement counties and municipalities. Ineligible entitlement counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's. Ineligible cities: Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, Salisbury. Municipalities in ineligible entitlement counties cannot apply. Project location must be in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services; single family housing rehabilitation; acquisition, renovation and sale of existing houses; downpayment assistance; or where the Secretary of DHCD determines that the project is necessary to protect public health, to alleviate personal economic hardship in an emergency situation, to promote economically integrated housing, is consistent with an overall economic development strategy, or where an exception is necessary and has been granted through the Maryland Department of Planning exception process. Towns with over 51% low and moderate income population are eligible for area benefit activities.
requirements_list: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population of less than 200,000
Non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000
Project must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low- and moderate-income persons; eliminate slum and blight; or meet urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety
Project must be eligible activity under HUD Program regulations (24 CFR Part 570)
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible
All projects must support the primary objectives of developing viable communities by funding activities that result in decent housing, improved and expanded infrastructure, and access to facilities
Projects must comply with fair housing, equal opportunity, and non-discrimination requirements
Projects must comply with environmental review requirements (National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 and 24 CFR Part 58)
Projects with $200,000 or more of HUD funding must comply with Section 3 requirements for job creation/retention
Infrastructure projects must comply with Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements for domestic procurement preferences on iron, steel, and manufactured products
Housing rehabilitation programs must meet local livability code requirements or housing quality standards
For rental housing assisted with CDBG funding, rents must comply with fair market rent standards and remain affordable for defined terms (10-20 years depending on funding amount)
For homeownership assistance, mortgages must be fixed-rate for minimum 30 years with no subprime or adjustable-rate mortgages allowed, and minimum 8 hours of HUD-approved housing counseling required
All procurement activities must allow for full and open competition
Single Audit required if grantee spends more than $750,000 of federal funds in a fiscal year
Grantees must have written Conflict of Interest policies and procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions on application development. Community Development applications are competitive and accepted once per year through a formal application process. Special Projects and Planning applications can be submitted anytime after receiving written approval from CDBG program staff. Applicants seeking funds for urgent need projects must contact CDBG program staff first to determine if their proposed project qualifies. Applications must include a Local Resolution, Citizen Participation Plan, Public Hearing Notice, Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan, and Program Income Re-Use Plan as applicable. All applications are evaluated against established criteria and rating systems. The State conducts monitoring of awarded projects throughout implementation to ensure compliance with all federal and state requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Investment Tax Credits support 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits for use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services. Businesses and individuals that donate $500 or more to a qualified organization's approved project can earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of the money, goods or real property contribution.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors that make contributions of $500 or more to qualified nonprofit organizations' approved projects receive Community Investment Tax Credits equal to 50% of the value of the money, goods or real property contribution. Tax credits can be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made and may not be used retroactively. These tax credits are in addition to deductions on both Federal and State taxes as a result of the charitable contribution. The maximum award of tax credits available through the program is $50,000 per application. Awardees must raise double the amount of tax credits requested; for example, a $50,000 tax credit award requires raising $100,000 in eligible donations. All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life. For FY26 awards, the contract period runs from January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2027. Credits must be used within this two-year period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Thursday, June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations applying for tax credit allocations, and individuals and businesses making charitable contributions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating and typically involve activities such as education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, enhancing neighborhoods and business districts, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible budget line items may include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Projects may also receive additional consideration if they are located in designated Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households (ENOUGH) areas or designated Just Communities. For capital projects, the project site must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations may be eligible if they document that clients served reside within a PFA boundary.
requirements_list: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations are eligible applicants
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Office of the Maryland Secretary of State
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Donors must make contributions of $500 or more
Donors must obtain a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
Individuals and businesses must use tax credits against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made
Donors must be individuals with personal tax liability in Maryland or businesses conducting trade or business in Maryland and subject to income tax, franchise tax or insurance premiums tax
For capital projects, organization must document site control via deed, executed lease with owner's permission, or real estate settlement documents
Maximum request for tax credits is $50,000 per application
Applicant must be registered in the DHCD IGX Project Portal
All required organizational documents must be submitted in PDF format
Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws must include all amendments and be current and in force at time of upload
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations apply annually and competitively to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for tax credit allocations. The FY26 CITC application round opens on Monday, May 19, 2025, and closes on Thursday, June 19, 2025, at 5:00 PM. Applications must be completed and submitted through the Department's IGX Project Portal online grants management system. To access the application, applicants must be registered users in the Portal. New users must complete a registration request form by clicking the 'New User? Register Here' link on the login page and indicating interest in the FY26 CITC application round; registration requests typically take up to 72 hours to be approved. Organization records and legal document uploads must be completed in the account's Profile before creating an application. Applications must include: Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, List of Current Board of Directors and Officers, Current Charitable Registration Letter or Exemption Letter from Maryland Secretary of State, current SDAT Good Standing status screenshot, Executed Corporate Resolution/Authorized Officers, Priority Funding Area (PFA) maps for all project addresses, and evidence of site control (if requesting capital funding). Applicants must provide a detailed project description, tasks and timeline table covering the entire 24-month award period, and a budget table with narrative. Award announcements will be made in Fall 2025. The FY26 award contract period begins January 1, 2026, and ends December 31, 2027. Awardees must submit electronic Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation and submit four Semi-Annual Reports (due July 10 and January 10 of each year) throughout the award period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that provides local governments and community development organizations with money for projects that strengthen communities. Projects focus on business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership, and commercial revitalization in areas targeted for recovery.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided to local governments, community development organizations, and groups of local governments for revitalization projects in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones in specific counties. The grant supports activities such as mixed-use development, business retention and expansion, streetscape improvements, homeownership programs, façade improvements, and real estate acquisition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community development organizations, and groups of local governments working on revitalization projects in designated Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that strengthen communities including mixed-use development, business retention and attraction, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation, residential and commercial façade improvements, real estate acquisition, land banking, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones specifically in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must capitalize on community strengths while addressing revitalization challenges
Project should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects should aim to stabilize a community, reverse social/economic/physical decline, or encourage sustainable growth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For application instructions and more information, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible student households enrolled in Maryland community schools who are experiencing housing instability and homelessness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency rental assistance provided to eligible student households experiencing housing instability and homelessness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student households enrolled in Maryland community schools experiencing housing instability or homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rental assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland community schools.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a Maryland community school
Must be experiencing housing instability or homelessness

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funds to seventeen Community Action Agencies and other non-profit organizations across Maryland to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. These agencies use the money to offer direct services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, as well as training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies. The state uses the other 5% for discretionary funding to support activities that fight poverty. Funding supports programs and activities to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization, plus training and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units that serve low-income individuals and families, focused on poverty elimination and community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support direct services for low-income individuals to help them become self-sufficient, including programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Funds can also support training, technical assistance, coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies, and community revitalization projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period for fiscal year 2025 has closed. You should check the program's webpage for information about future application opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions create or upgrade computer labs and centers. These labs provide public computer access for individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 covering 100% of costs for computer equipment purchases. Additionally, up to $10,000 available for internet service subscription costs for up to three years. Majority (50% or higher) of those served must fall into covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026. Eligible uses include: computers and laptops, networking equipment, internet service subscription, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses (up to 15% of budget), administrative expenses (up to 15% of budget), software, audiovisual equipment, and assistive technology. Total program funding is $2 million from American Rescue Plan Act State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 29, 2024 by 11:59 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions serving targeted populations (individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, incarcerated or returning citizens)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers providing public computer access. Eligible uses include computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones), networking equipment (routers, switches, network cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls), internet service subscription (up to 3 years of wired internet connection), marketing and outreach (up to 10% of total budget), operational expenses including staff salaries and lab maintenance (up to 15% of budget), administrative expenses including training and security monitoring (up to 15% of budget), software (operating systems, productivity suites, educational/training software, antivirus), audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards for training, speakers), and assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards/mice).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Grant up to $65,000 per application for computer equipment purchase
Internet service subscription funding up to $10,000 per application
Majority (50% or higher) of those served must be from covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens

Applicant must be legally organized as one of: Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated municipality, local government agency delegated by local jurisdiction, not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or Community Anchor Institution within Maryland
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026
Application must be complete in its entirety with all required documentation
Must submit proof of non-profit status (501(c) documents) or local jurisdiction documentation
Must provide Executive Summary and Scope of Work including timeline
Must provide detailed itemized budget
Must provide federal W-9 form
Must provide Certificate of Good Standing (if applicable)
Computers must come with standard manufacturer warranty or extended warranty
Marketing and outreach expenses limited to 10% of total project budget
Operational expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
Administrative expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET. Submission methods: (1) Electronic submission via email to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application – Organizational Applicant name' (files should be converted to PDFs); (2) Paper submission postmarked, shipped, or hand-delivered to Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 (must show proof of mailing via USPS postmark, mail receipt, or commercial carrier shipping label dated on or before deadline); (3) Hand delivery accepted daily 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and state/federal holidays) with proper identification. Application includes: completed application form, executive summary, scope of work with timeline, project narrative (barriers, partners, outcomes/metrics, statement of experience), detailed itemized budget, federal W-9 form, 501(c) documentation for nonprofits (if applicable), and Certificate of Good Standing (if applicable). Technical assistance available prior to November 22, 2024. The OSB intends to award funds beginning December 2024 and successful applicants must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU).

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. The program covers significant capital construction costs for deploying broadband service at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds), with the applicant providing a required match based on service area density.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $800,000 and $4,500,000 covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for broadband networks serving unserved homes and businesses. Match requirements are 10% to 30% of eligible capital construction costs, determined by service area density: For wired infrastructure: Fewer than 8 premises per mile (10% match), 8-14 premises per mile (20% match), 15+ premises per mile (30% match). For wireless infrastructure: Fewer than 40 premises per tower (10% match), 40-69 premises per tower (20% match), 70+ premises per tower (30% match). Match must be in cash and available at time of award. Eligible capital expenses include outside plant construction (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets/shelters), and customer drops to individual premises. Ineligible expenses include operating costs, leases, bandwidth and spectrum expenses, salaries not directly related to construction, tower or land purchases, building construction/renovation, customer devices (laptops, tablets, handsets), and video or telephone service expenses not necessary for broadband delivery. Grant funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis as the project progresses. At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by the second anniversary of the grant agreement effective date. All grant funds must be expended by August 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners, including incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, private corporations, limited liability companies organized on a for-profit or not-for-profit basis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks including middle mile transport, interconnection plant, service drops to individual homes and businesses in unserved areas, electronic equipment necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), and other capital assets directly necessary to provide broadband service to end users at the Broadband Grant Speed of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in unserved areas of Maryland where broadband service does not currently exist; areas having received state grant funding in the past are ineligible for additional funding; must serve all unserved premises in the Proposed Funded Service Area at the Broadband Grant Speed; service area may be within a single or multiple jurisdictions and does not need to be contiguous
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, cooperative, private corporation, or limited liability company (for-profit or non-profit) - not an individual or partnership
Grant request range: $800,000 to $4,500,000
Required match: 10% to 30% of eligible capital construction costs depending on service area density (wired or wireless)
Service area must contain only unserved households and businesses with no existing broadband service at 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up speeds
Must demonstrate legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal and state statutes and regulations
Must have legal existence verified by Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (good standing status)
Must provide IRS Form W-9 and DUNS Number
Must obtain Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
If partnering with another entity, must provide partnership agreement addressing financial terms and entity qualifications
If local jurisdiction partner, must provide letter from sponsoring jurisdiction documenting partnership extent and support
Match must be cash available or shown to be available upon execution of grant agreement; in-kind contributions are not eligible
Areas with past state broadband funding are ineligible
All grant-eligible capital expenditures must be for new, non-depreciated items
Project must achieve minimum network requirements of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable, with certification) with maximum 50 millisecond latency
Federal funds may be used as match only if expressly allowed by federal funding source
If receiving federal funding for match, federal award must be confirmed before state funds disbursed
Must comply with American Rescue Plan Act requirements and all applicable federal and state rules
Must commence project on or prior to September 1, 2023
Must complete project prior to August 31, 2026
Applicant not eligible to submit another application under this program for the same jurisdiction until construction is complete and grant is fully closed out, or two years, whichever is later
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application package by December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET via mail (postmarked), commercial shipping (receipt dated), or email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov. Application must include: (A) Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, and evidence of legal existence and good standing; (B) Executive Summary describing the service area, project need, applicant qualifications, partnership details, and project benefits; (C) Scoring Criteria Documentation; (D) System Design including network diagram; (E) Service Area Demographics and map in .shp or .kml/.kmz format showing properties to receive service; (F) Scope of Work including construction build-out/project milestones (Schedule F-1) and detailed project budget (Schedule F-2) by category; (G) Financial Information and Sustainability including historical financial statements and pro forma financial statements (Schedule G-1); (H) Statement of Experience; (I) Evidence of Funding Commitments from Other Sources; (J) Reporting and Compliance documentation. All files except specified formats should be converted to PDF. If mailing, must provide proof of mailing via USPS postmark, USPS receipt with date, or dated commercial carrier shipping label. Applications delivered after the deadline will not be considered. Prior to submission, technical assistance available until November 18, 2022. Applications will be scored competitively and reviewed for completeness and eligibility. If selected for award, applicant must enter into grant agreement with Department and comply with all grant terms, conditions, and procedures outlined in the Network Infrastructure Grant Program Agreement and Contracting and Procedures Guide. Grant funds disbursed on reimbursement basis as project progresses upon submission of request with supporting documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding specifically for Smith Island to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. The program covers up to 90% of capital construction costs with a required local match of at least 10%.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $1,000,000 to $3,000,000 covering up to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband networks serving unserved homes and businesses on Smith Island. Required match of at least 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of requested grant amount). Funds must be used for eligible capital expenses including outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets/shelters), and customer premises equipment necessary to deliver broadband service at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream (100x100) with maximum 50 millisecond latency. Operating expenses are not eligible. Match must be in cash and cannot fund operational costs. Matching funds exceptions: (1) eligible federal funding may be used as match if clearly requested; (2) up to 3 years of Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul service costs may be included as match; (3) tower construction/structural improvements may be treated as match. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis as the project progresses. At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by the second anniversary of the agreement's effective date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners on Smith Island seeking to expand broadband infrastructure to unserved areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks on Smith Island including: outside plant infrastructure (fiber optic cabling, conduit, poles, support structures); middle mile infrastructure; electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters, cabinets); customer premises equipment (CPE) up to and including the ONT or fixed wireless modem; and engineering costs tied to funded capital assets. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated. Ineligible uses include: duplication of existing broadband service, operating expenses, tower/land/building purchases, building renovations, telephone or video service expenses not necessary for broadband delivery, customer devices (laptops, handsets, tablets), and expenses incurred prior to application submission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Maryland (all locations on Smith Island as identified by latitude/longitude coordinates in Appendix A of the application guide). The Identified Service Area (ISA) must be unserved with no locations currently receiving broadband service at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be legally organized as: a Maryland local jurisdiction; an incorporated organization recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction; a cooperative legally formed in Maryland and recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction; a limited liability company recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction; or other legal entity recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction. Partnerships and sole proprietors are not eligible.
Grant request range: minimum $1,000,000; maximum $3,000,000
Required match: minimum 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of requested grant amount)
Service area must include all unserved premises on Smith Island with no existing broadband service at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal and state statutes and regulations

Project must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream (100x100) with maximum 50 millisecond latency at served subscriber locations. Exception: 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up with 50 millisecond latency is acceptable only if network is scalable to 100x100 and applicant submits certification of circumstances (geography, topography, or excessive cost) preventing minimum connectivity
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Match must be in cash available or shown to be available at time of grant agreement execution. In-kind contributions are not eligible for match.
Applicant must not have been debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity in the past four years, nor subject to civil claims for non-payment of $30,000 or more
Applicant must have good standing with The State of Maryland (documented for corporations/LLCs)
Applicant must have Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9 and DUNS Number
If applying with federal funding as match, must clearly request this exception in Executive Summary and Application Form
If partnering with another entity, must provide draft agreement addressing financial terms and partner qualifications
Applicant must have obtained or will obtain all necessary federal, state, and local government approvals, permits, and licenses prior to project commencement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request technical assistance from OSB prior to January 19, 2024 if needed (technical assistance requests must be made prior to application submission). 2. Complete all required application sections: (A) Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, and evidence of good standing/legal existence; (B) Executive Summary covering project description, applicant description, total project costs, and system overview; (C) Scoring Criteria documentation addressing project strength, contribution above match, and other evaluation factors; (D) System Design including network diagram; (E) Scope of Work including Service Area Demographics, construction build-out/project milestones, and project budget; (F) Financial Information and Sustainability including historical financial statements and pro forma financial statement with assumptions; (G) Statement of Experience; (H) Evidence of funding commitments from other sources; (I) Reporting and Compliance certifications. 3. Prepare all required worksheets and supporting documents including: network diagram, pro forma financial statement assumptions, construction build-out schedule, project budget on Schedule F-2, historical financial statements, and pro forma financial statement on Schedule G-1. 4. Submit completed application package by 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024 via one of three methods: (a) Paper copy with original signatures and electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 with proof of mailing/shipping; (b) Email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line "Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – [your company name]" with files as zipped attachment; or (c) by certified mail. 5. Applications received after deadline will not be considered. 6. OSB may contact applicants for clarification information on submitted materials. 7. Upon grant award, applicant must execute grant agreement with Department. 8. Post-award: applicant must submit interim progress reports on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1 of each year; commence project by September 1, 2024; complete project by August 31, 2027; expend at least 50% of grant funds by second anniversary of effective date; maintain records for 5 years after final report approval; and submit final report within 45 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions create gap networks and community networks to provide affordable or free broadband internet access. These networks address affordability challenges that prevent low- and moderate-income households and other covered populations from subscribing to internet service.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $25,000 to $250,000 covering up to 100% of construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation costs for community-based broadband gap networks. Funding covers equipment such as network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters needed to deliver broadband service to end users.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profit organizations, community-based organizations, and anchor institutions serving low- and moderate-income households and covered populations including individuals living at or below 150% of the federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, and digital network technology to provide broadband services to covered populations at low or no cost. Funds can be used to build and deploy new gap networks, upgrade or expand existing networks, or operate and maintain networks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Applicants must be providing services within the State of Maryland and registered in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, non-profit 501(c) entity, community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Applicant must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Projects must reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with limited exceptions
Only complete applications will be considered for funding
Subscriber cost must be low or no cost for covered populations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application submission process opened on February 15, 2022 and closed on March 31, 2022. Applications and supporting documents were submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov. Funding announcements were scheduled for on or before April 15, 2022. Applicants must submit a completed application form, project summary with executive summary and network design, IRS determination letter if applicable, certificate of good standing verification, IRS W-9 form, and DUNS number.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports digital equity and inclusion by providing new, internet-enabled devices to eligible households. The program addresses the need for devices among Marylanders who cannot afford to purchase them, working alongside discounted and free internet services. Funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds, the program aims to procure approximately 145,000 HP Chromebook 14 G7 devices or similar models.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) to county and municipal governments for distribution to eligible households. Each device costs $198.75. A $6 per device stipend is available to help cover storage, security, distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution. Round one awarded 91,300 chromebooks; round two provides remaining devices with priority for new eligible applicants. Jurisdictions have six months from delivery of their first device shipment to complete distribution. Any devices not distributed within six months must be returned to the Department at the awardee's cost. Devices can be received at a maximum rate of one shipment per month over a five-month period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 29, 2023 by 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland county and municipal government entities, in partnership with eligible distribution partners such as libraries, school districts, non-profit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions, who will distribute devices to eligible households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of internet-enabled devices to households with income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, with one device per household address maximum. The $6 per device stipend may be used for cost of securing devices in storage, cost of securing devices during distribution, cost of distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, all Maryland counties and municipalities. Jurisdictions that did not receive devices in round one will receive priority review over returning applicants in round two.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or municipality) as recognized by the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Eligible households must have income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (e.g., family of 4: $55,500 annual income)
Alternatively, households enrolled in the federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) are eligible

Alternatively, households participating in government assistance programs including SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit, Free/Reduced-Price School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program (including USDA Community Eligibility Provision schools), or recipients of Federal Pell Grants in current award year are eligible
One device per household address or recognized MDU unit maximum
Applicant must develop and document an eligibility verification process
Applicant must develop an outreach program to inform the targeted population of the program
Applicant must ensure the bulk shipment receiver has loading/unloading capabilities and secure storage space
Applicant must inspect devices at time of receipt and notify OSB immediately upon discovery of damaged products
Applicant must use the Department Device Tracking Portal for address verification during distribution to ensure multiple devices are not provided to one household
Applicant must maintain records of device distribution and be able to provide household-level data upon request
Applicant must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) before submitting complete application
Applicant must provide a valid DUNS number and unique entity identifier
Applicant must provide a current IRS W-9 Form
If applying in partnership with distribution partner organizations, an agreement or draft agreement must be provided identifying the partner entity, its qualifications, and any financial terms
If a municipal applicant is in a county where the county is also an applicant, entities must coordinate efforts to ensure complementary and not conflicting distribution
Distribution must be completed within six months of delivery of first device shipment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a complete application package by September 29, 2023 at 11:59pm ET. Applications may be submitted electronically via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Connected Devices Program Application – your jurisdictional name,' or via USPS/shipping with postmark or dated shipping receipt. The application package must include: (1) completed Application Form with applicant information, project information, estimated funding, receiver information, and authorized representative signature; (2) written Project Narrative including Executive Summary (up to 2 pages), Verification and Distribution process, Scope of Work, Outreach program, Barriers and solutions, Partners and Local Engagement, and Intended Outcomes and Metrics; (3) Scope of Work detailing establishment of partnerships, data collection, device storage, distribution method, eligibility verification, and methodology to ensure one device per household; (4) Project Schedule outlining milestones; (5) Monthly Device Delivery Request; and (6) Federal Form W-9. Technical assistance is available prior to September 22, 2023. OSB reviews applications for completeness and suitable distribution methodology, may coordinate with other State Agencies for verification, and may contact applicants for clarification. Successful applicants are selected based on qualifications and response evaluation, with possible interviews. Awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Department. If total device requests exceed availability, an equal percentage reduction is made across all applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (Homeowner)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps limited income households with installation of energy conservation materials in their homes at no charge.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Installation of energy conservation materials in homes at no charge to limited income households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income homeowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of energy conservation materials to improve home energy efficiency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Limited income household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an interest form or application. After confirmation of eligibility, receive a letter with an assigned contractor. Contact contractor to schedule in-home energy assessment or wait for contractor to contact within 30 days. Contractor completes recommended work at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides income-eligible homeowners and single-family renters with energy-saving upgrades at no cost, including upgrades to energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, insulation replacement, and other energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost grants for eligible income-qualified participants to make energy-saving upgrades to their homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and single-family renters in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving upgrades including energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, insulation replacement, and other energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Income-eligible

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides low-interest construction loans or helps improve existing loans for building low-energy or net-zero homes. Eligible projects include new construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower, producing as much or more energy than they use.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest construction loans and loan enhancements available to builders, developers, or owners building in Maryland. Interest rates range from 3% to 5% for market-rate projects and 2% to 4% for projects where more than 50% of units are at or below 60% of Area Median Income, depending on HERS score. Administration fee of 1% of total loan, appraisal fee of $290, and title fees apply. Loan-to-value up to 90%. Construction period typically 12 months with 12-month loan repayment period for projects for sale. Loan enhancements available for applicants using private lenders. Additional fees may apply if funding is provided as a loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open until available funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, and investors constructing or retrofitting homes to net-zero energy standards.

requirements_list: Qualified to do business in Maryland
Have legal capacity and all necessary authorization to incur the obligation of the loan
Demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability acceptable to the department
Demonstrate ability to complete the project
New construction or deep energy retrofit of existing home

Submit current financial statements
Provide evidence of ownership (deed or purchase contract)
Obtain zoning letter confirming residential use
Provide Property/Builder's Risk insurance with DHCD as certificate holder and mortgagee/lender loss payable

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan (Net Zero) Program paper application form. Provide contact information for the person completing the application and owner information including legal name, legal structure, and business address.
