Submit the completed application by email to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov and CC Thomas.Walz@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps county jurisdictions pay for capital construction costs to install broadband service in remote or difficult-to-serve properties. The program addresses geographic barriers that discourage internet service providers from delivering service to these locations. Funding supports connections of unserved difficult-to-serve premises to existing broadband networks, with projects required to deliver minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload (or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with certification) with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,100,000 per eligible county jurisdiction for capital construction costs of broadband service installation in difficult-to-serve properties. Maximum funding per location is $8,000. Required match of 25% of eligible capital construction costs (can be provided by local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination). Match must be in cash form; in-kind matches not acceptable. Eligible costs include construction of service delivery facilities, equipment, materials, and electronics (ONTs, routers, switches, wireless equipment, antennae) necessary to serve unserved difficult-to-serve premises. Ineligible uses include middle-mile infrastructure, duplication of existing services, land or tower purchase, building construction, and operating expenses. Funding source: Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (CPF) administered by U.S. Treasury through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due on or before December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions developing sub-grant programs with internet service provider partners to serve unserved difficult-to-serve properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation to premises with difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from infrastructure, or other geographic issues. Eligible uses include construction of service delivery facilities, minor extensions of ISP infrastructure, and equipment such as Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, and modems necessary to deliver service at grant-required speeds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; focus on unserved difficult-to-serve properties. Projects must connect unserved premises lacking terrestrial fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds to existing broadband networks.
requirements_list: Applicant must be county jurisdiction with ISP partner or partners
All partnering ISPs must participate in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Applicant must enter partnership with ISP prior to funding agreement
Maximum grant funding per applicant: $1,100,000
Maximum funding per location: $8,000
Required match: 25% of eligible capital construction costs (match can be from local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination; match must be cash, not in-kind)

Projects must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50ms latency, or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with certification of geographic or topographic constraints and commitment to upgrade when technology available
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant responsible for all non-capital expenses related to state and federal reporting and ongoing administrative costs for duration of project

Applicant must develop jurisdictional-specific funding program with program overview including end user selection, low-income assistance, ISP billing methods, low-income program details, and ACP assistance/promotion
Applicant must address how financially distressed property owners will be treated in program plan
Applicant must include outreach component to promote program
ISP networks must be scalable to minimum 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds based on future technology advances (if using lower-speed option)
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application package to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 22, 2023 with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and local county jurisdiction name. All application materials must be combined into one ZIP file to ensure submission integrity. If application exceeds email size limits, upload files to Google Drive or cloud service and share link. Complete the FY24 Connect Maryland Grant Application Form and provide required documentation including: Executive Summary describing unserved premises, community needs, and project benefits; Application Partnership section naming ISP partner(s); Experience statement of senior team from applicant and ISP partner; Network Discussion describing ISP network, technology, capabilities, and offerings; Subscriber Profile with demographic data; Subscriber Costs and Limitations including pricing and service options; Budget with capital construction cost estimates; Program Overview with sufficient detail on program delivery, end-user selection, low-income assistance, and ACP promotion; Proposed implementation schedule assuming Spring 2024 start with key milestones. Identify any proprietary or confidential information. Applications will be scored based on criteria: Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points); Match Contribution Source and Percentage (up to 15 points); Network Delivery Speed (up to 5 points); Subscriber Options including affordability and service limitations (up to 20 points). Awards made high to low score as funding permits with maximum 45 points total. OSB intends to facilitate award of funding in February 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program designed to help Housing Voucher participants achieve higher education, improve employment status, and work toward self-sufficiency. The program evaluates the skills and determines the needs of families and individuals, guiding them onto a path of economic independence through supportive services including financial literacy, job training, childcare, and other instruments to gain success in the workforce.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides case management, needs assessment, and goal-setting services to help Housing Voucher participants pursue higher education, job training, homeownership, and entrepreneurship. Participants receive supportive services including childcare, education, employment counseling, financial literacy, health services, job training and retention, and transportation. All FSS participants are eligible for an interest-bearing escrow account where increased portions of rent earned through employment wage increases are credited monthly. Participants who successfully complete the program receive all funds in the escrow account plus interest, which are tax-free according to IRS guidelines. The standard contract period is 5 years and can be extended for an additional 2 years with good cause. Participants may graduate early if they accomplish all goals before the allotted time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Voucher participants seeking to improve their employment status, education level, and achieve economic independence and self-sufficiency. Eligible participants include families and individuals, including those with disabilities who can designate another adult household member as head of household.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for pursuing higher education, job training, homeownership, entrepreneurship, financial literacy, childcare, employment counseling, health services, job retention, and transportation. Escrow funds can be used for contract goal-related expenses such as vehicle repair or testing fees, and once the contract is completed, funds can be used for any purpose including down payments on homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; Eastern Shore Regional Office located in Cambridge, Maryland (Dorchester County).
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Voucher participant
Head of household must complete and submit an application
Must sign a Contract of Participation
Must have two required long-term goals: obtaining employment and being free of temporary cash assistance (TANF)
Social Security and assistance for a child or disabled family member do not count toward TANF freedom requirement
Can join at any time after receiving rental assistance
Disabled individuals can participate as long as their goal is to obtain employment/earned income and be free of TANF benefits
To receive escrow funds at contract completion, must be working and free of TANF
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can contact DHCD by phone at (410) 901-4080, email fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, visit dhcd.maryland.gov/CambridgeCEC, ask their case manager at any meeting or redetermination, or complete an online FSS Inquiry Form at dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/family-selfsufficiency-program. Upon initial contact, applicants will meet with an FSS coordinator who will review and discuss the family's strengths, barriers, and goals. The applicant and coordinator will complete a Needs Assessment outlining the rights, goals, and responsibilities of both parties. An individual family plan will be created to meet goals, and a Contract of Participation will be signed. Goals may be set by all family members and can include higher education, job training, homeownership, and entrepreneurship. The FSS case manager will assist with creating realistic and achievable goals and will direct families to supportive services from the community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects. The program is administered in Maryland by the Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis according to the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the Internal Revenue Service and varies annually. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. The credit is claimed by project sponsors or their investor partners on their federal income tax return. Credits are determined using IRS-published eligible basis calculations and applicable percentages. In Maryland, 10% of the annual allocation is set aside for nonprofit sponsors.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a competitive basis; portal opens May 16 and closes June 20 annually for End of Year reporting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit sponsors developing low-income rental housing projects. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Developers, investors, and property management companies seeking to develop or rehabilitate affordable rental housing. Eligible applicants also include county governments and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Funds support the eligible basis of qualified low-income rental housing buildings as determined under IRC Section 42.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland. A residential rental building must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made. Properties in Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) and Difficult Development Areas (DDAs) may receive preferential consideration.
requirements_list: Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy
Owner must rent either 20% of units to households with incomes of 50% or less of area median income (50/20) or 40% of units to households with incomes of 60% or less of area median income (60/40)
Building must comply with requirements regarding tenant income, maximum rent levels, and percentage of low-income occupancy
Building must remain in compliance and is subject to covenant to enforce compliance for minimum of 40 years (or 30 years for projects financed with tax-exempt bonds plus 15-year extended use period)
Household income must not exceed applicable income limits for the area
Gross rent (including utilities and mandatory charges) must not exceed specified limits
Annual income certifications and recertifications required for all tenants in low-income units
Physical property must be maintained in decent, safe, and sanitary condition suitable for occupancy
Owner must not refuse to lease units to applicants with Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8)
Building must be used exclusively for low-income residential rental housing (no owner occupancy)
Initial compliance period of 15 years from placed-in-service date, followed by extended use period of at least 15 additional years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Competitive Application Process: 1) Sponsors prepare comprehensive application including organizational history, financial capability, development experience, and project details consistent with QAP requirements. 2) Applications are submitted through competitive rounds based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). 3) CDA reviews applications for compliance with QAP priorities and scoring criteria. 4) Selected projects receive tax credit reservations. 5) Developers must obtain CPA-prepared cost certification for each building. 6) Upon completion, sponsors must register their property in the LIHTC Tenant Demographic End-of-Year Reporting System. Post-Allocation Process: 1) Upon building completion and occupancy, owners claim tax credits via IRS Form 8609. 2) Annual compliance monitoring conducted by Division of Credit Assurance (DCA) including file reviews and physical inspections at least every five years during extended use period. 3) Owners submit annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance (OCPC). 4) Annual tenant income certifications maintained. Tax-Exempt Bond Financed Projects: May bypass competitive process if project meets specified criteria and receives appropriate bond financing. Contact the program for additional information on how to apply.

Loans may also be used to refinance mortgages on existing group homes.

structured_extraction.program_name: HAF WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Grant helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by providing grants for critical repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. The grant is one-time financial assistance per household.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 standard grant for critical home repairs. Exceptions of up to $15,000 may be made for extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Grant assistance with no deed of trust recorded. Applicants may choose between 33% deposit with 67% at completion or 0% deposit with 100% at completion payment options. There is no minimum credit score requirement. Payments or deposits made by homeowners for work or materials at any point will NOT be reimbursed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners experiencing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic who need critical repairs to avoid displacement from their primary residence. Renters and tenants are not eligible; only owners of primary residences qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs to primary residences including non-functioning heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, roof repair/replacement, mold/mildew remediation, lead paint/asbestos removal, structural and maintenance issues, wells, and trip/slip safety issues. Funds cannot be used for remodeling or non-health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for primary residences. Income limits are based on household size and cannot exceed 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI), with specific limits for each county.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020
Income at or below 150% of County AMI (Area Median Income)
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the primary residence
Must be named on the deed of trust
Must provide a work proposal for the critical repair from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with photos or drawings
Work proposal estimate must be dated within the last 60 days
If other persons are named on the deed but do not live at the property, must provide proof they live elsewhere (copy of driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
Must attest to COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020
Must be a one-time applicant (one-time financial assistance per household)
Contractor must be currently licensed with the State of Maryland as a Home Improvement Contractor
Contractor must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Contractor must have active limited liability insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million
Contractor must provide completed W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application available by emailing Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov. 2. Provide income documentation (recent paystubs, tax returns, award letters, or zero income statement). 3. Attest to financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020. 4. Obtain at least one detailed estimate within the past 60 days from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor that includes photo documentation of critical repairs, contractor phone number, and email address. 5. Contractor must complete the Bid Cover Page and provide current MHIC License (or relevant trade license), Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and executed W-9. 6. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation via email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis until funding is fully reserved. Upon approval, applicant must sign commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor accepting work as completed satisfactorily.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to support affordable housing development. The program helps build, buy, or rehabilitate rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds are targeted to serve very low-income and low-income households, and can be used in conjunction with existing DHCD housing programs or as standalone funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are provided as zero-interest deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years depending on the type of housing financed, or as regular amortized loans. Funds may also be provided as grants or recoverable grants requiring repayment when property is sold or discontinued for low-income housing use. For rental projects, equity sharing may be required when low-income usage is discontinued. Maximum assistance to a single project generally will not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable. For rental housing, HOME funds are targeted to households at or below 80% of area median income. For homeownership projects, HOME funds are targeted to households at or below 80% of area median income. HOME funds can be used for multifamily rental housing, single-family homeownership programs, group homes for special populations, rehabilitation of owner-occupied housing, and tenant-based rental assistance on a limited basis. FFY 2023 allocation was $7,319,907.00 with funds allocated to multifamily housing programs, single family programs, HOME Special Reserve Fund, and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dale Quisgard, HOME Program Manager; Kiaya Nickens, Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and for-profit developers seeking to develop affordable housing for low-income and very low-income residents. Eligible projects serve homeowners, renters, and special populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, buying, or rehabilitating rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. Funds may be used for soft seconds to reduce home costs, land acquisition, development costs, and construction financing. Funds may be used in conjunction with existing DHCD programs including Community Development Programs, Homeownership Programs, and Special Loan Programs. Uses include rehabilitation of owner-occupied housing, lead paint hazard reduction or abatement, accessibility modifications, furnace and roof replacement, group home development, tenant-based rental assistance including security deposit assistance, and disaster relief.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County except Annapolis, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct HUD allocations). State government agencies are automatically eligible for HOME funds and receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater.
requirements_list: For rental housing units, residents' household incomes must be at or below 80% of the area median household income (adjusted for household size, set annually by HUD)
For owner-occupied housing units, the owner's household income must be at or below 80% of the area median household income (adjusted for household size, set annually by HUD)

The number of income-restricted units is usually calculated by dividing the amount of HOME funds by the total cost of the project, then multiplying that result by the total number of units in the project
Projects must meet both DHCD program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements when using HOME funds in conjunction with other DHCD programs
If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with DHCD
Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) must be certified by the State and meet HUD qualification criteria
For CHDO operating assistance, organizations receiving set-aside funds or under written agreement to receive funds within 24 months are eligible
CHDO operating assistance cannot provide more than 50% of a CHDO's operating budget in any fiscal year, or $50,000, whichever is greater
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Project applications may be submitted as part of DHCD's ongoing housing programs or through the HOME Special Reserve Fund process. Applications can include specific requests for HOME funds or DHCD staff may propose HOME funds during project evaluation and underwriting. HOME Special Reserve Fund applications are reviewed and allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs, nonprofits, and local governments applying in conjunction with nonprofits. Rating criteria include readiness to proceed, demonstrated ability, matching contributions, geographic distribution, and performance on prior HOME awards. Applicants should contact the HOME Program Manager for specific application procedures and timelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: This initiative helps families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health, pays for lead removal from homes or apartments where children live or spend time at no cost to the owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and Maryland Department of Health will pay for lead removal and necessary minor home repairs from homes or apartments where eligible children live or spend time, at no cost to the owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under age 19 living in Maryland who have elevated blood lead levels and are eligible for or enrolled in Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in homes or apartments where children live or spend time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Child must be under 19 years old
Child must live in Maryland
Child must have recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL) or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure happened (home, apartment, or other facility)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 (toll-free) or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov to inquire about eligibility and program details. You may also contact your local health department for more information. There is no cost to the property owner or tenant for lead removal services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch - Public Housing Program (Broadband Wiring Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps public housing owners install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units and provides free WiFi in common areas. The program addresses digital equity and inclusion issues by ensuring low-income residents in publicly-owned and non-profit housing can access broadband service. Funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus Capital Projects Funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1 (FY24 Public Housing): Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with required 5% match. Expanded Round (FY24 Affordable Housing for municipally-owned and non-profit MDUs): Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible costs with required 5% match. Total funding for expanded round is $26.9 million. Eligible uses include: (1) installation or extension of wiring to deliver wireless service to public areas; (2) installation of end user facilities including wiring, wireless access points and necessary electronics; (3) educational and technical assistance outreach to support adoption; (4) extension of fiber optic facilities; (5) engineering design services; and (6) community engagement costs (capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000). Match funds must be cash match of capital construction costs and can include other state or federal funds. All equipment must be new and non-depreciated. Projects must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 milliseconds latency at each dwelling unit. Common area WiFi should provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds. Free broadband service via WiFi must be extended through all common areas of housing community. Applicants must maintain and operate the network for minimum 5 years after project completion, with hardware warranty and service agreements required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 22, 2023 (Round 1); January 31, 2025 (Expanded Round)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (county or municipal), housing authorities, municipally-owned and non-profit entities that own and operate publicly supported housing for low- and moderate-income households, and internet service providers serving these communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in public housing; extension of fiber optic facilities; installation of wireless access points for free common area WiFi; building modifications necessary for broadband equipment; engineering and design services; community engagement and ACP registration assistance; network equipment including cabinets, switches, routers, modems, firewalls; low-voltage contracting work; installation labor costs; taxes, shipping and insurance directly related to broadband equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties). Eligible project areas are publicly owned or municipally owned/non-profit housing developments identified as having need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connection reliably meeting or exceeding 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds, lack of affordable access, or lack of reliable broadband.
requirements_list: Applicant must be local jurisdiction, housing authority, or internet service provider serving eligible properties
Must be publicly owned housing development or municipally owned/non-profit low-income multi-dwelling units (MDUs)
Properties must be identified as having need for broadband investment (speeds less than 100/20 Mbps or unreliable service)
Minimum grant range: $500,000 (Round 1) or $250,000 (Expanded Round)
Maximum grant range: $9,000,000 (Round 1) or $5,000,000 (Expanded Round)
Minimum 5% cash match of eligible capital construction costs required (other state or federal funds acceptable)

Must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 milliseconds latency at each dwelling unit (or provide certificate explaining geographic, topographic, or cost barriers)
Must agree to maintain and operate network for minimum 5 years after project completion
Must acquire necessary hardware warranty and service agreements for 5+ years of operation
Must install wireless access points in all public and common areas providing free WiFi service
Internal wiring must be designed as open access to facilitate multiple service providers
For Expanded Round: Must be existing Internet Service Provider actively offering high-speed services over own physical network infrastructure
For Expanded Round: Must provide strong letters of support and commitment from property owners
For Expanded Round: Must offer low-cost plans for low-income residents and affordable pricing for different speed tiers
For Expanded Round: Must demonstrate financial stability and previous successful project experience
All funded projects must comply with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) and Treasury Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (CPF) requirements
Non-capital administrative costs capped at 1% of total project costs (engagement costs capped at 3%, not to exceed $15,000)
Community engagement strategies must include ACP registration assistance and educational outreach during project development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically as PDF via email to osb.md@maryland.gov. Subject line must include 'Broadband for Public Housing', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Complete application package must include: (1) Completed and signed application form; (2) IRS W-9 Form; (3) Executive Summary describing public housing location, selection rationale, resident problems, and project benefits; (4) Statement of Experience demonstrating applicant capability and relevant work experience; (5) Network Design describing technology, speeds, latency, backhaul requirements, and network diagram; (6) Community Profile with demographic data and existing internet service information; (7) Subscriber Cost information if applicable; (8) Barriers and Risk Assessment; (9) Partners and Local Engagement documentation; (10) Detailed implementation schedule with major milestones and dates; (11) Line-item capital construction budget on provided budget form with all work and material quantities and costs; (12) Sustainability and Financial Plan (for Expanded Round). Applications not including all required information will be deemed ineligible. Applications will be scored on project description, technology feasibility, experience, and benefits to community. Awards made on high-to-low score basis as funding permits. For Round 1, awards announced February 2024 with projects to be completed by June 30, 2026. For Expanded Round, awards announced on or before February 28, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and support innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program also allows counties to purchase existing privately owned housing in conjunction with local housing authorities or housing developers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to support rental housing development projects, including new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation. Funds can also be used for purchasing existing privately owned housing. Two loan options are available: (1) Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate, or (2) Longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP loans are subordinate loans; positioning will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum award per project is $2,500,000. Loans follow DHCD's Multifamily Fee Schedule. For FY 2026, $5 million in total funding is available for up to 3 project awards, with a maximum of one award per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments, particularly those partnering with housing developers to create mixed-income rental housing. Sponsors must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing, including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with affordability requirements. Funds may also be used for projects where a county acquires existing private-sector housing in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland counties. Projects must be located in Maryland. Priority consideration given to projects located within ¾ mile of rail stations, within ENOUGH Act approved award locations or Just Communities designations, or within Communities of Opportunity.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government
Projects must partner with a housing developer (except for counties acquiring existing housing with a PHA or developer)
Sponsor must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity, as demonstrated by an organizational chart and/or partnership agreement

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing
Projects must be proposed in Maryland
Project must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of award selection date
Application fee of $2,500 required
Must meet all Threshold Criteria established in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
For projects seeking both HIPP and LIHTC funding, project must meet all threshold requirements of the Multifamily Rental Financing Program
Must comply with fair housing and equal opportunity requirements
Must comply with relocation and displacement requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request pre-application meeting using the Pre-Application Meeting Request Form. 2. Complete the Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package, which includes CDA Form 202 (Multifamily Rental Financing Application), certifications, threshold checklist, and self-scoring sheet. 3. Submit waiver requests if applicable using the Waiver Request Form at least 15 days prior to application deadline (by May 4, 2026). 4. Prepare all required exhibits including project information, certifications, development team information (Forms 203 and 209), organizational chart, letters of intent for all financing sources, and affirmative fair housing marketing plan. 5. Submit complete electronic application via Procorem WorkCenter with all attachments clearly tabbed. 6. Submit application fee of $2,500 separately to Community Development Administration, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784. 7. DHCD staff reviews applications for completeness; incomplete submissions will not be processed. 8. Scoring committee scores all complete proposals based on six criteria: Project Readiness (6 points), Location (6 points), Statutory Preferences (16 points), Innovation (10 points), Affordability (12 points), and Developer/Owner/Partner Capacity (12 points). 9. Highest-scored proposal is recommended for CDA Director approval, then submitted to Secretary for final approval and allocation. 10. DHCD may select only one project per jurisdiction. 11. Virtual information session held March 11, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. for questions about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to homeowners and rental property owners to install or repair indoor plumbing in residential properties, including wells, septic systems, water and sewer connections, and plumbing fixtures. Part of the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program, which aims to provide affordable funding to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. The program serves individuals with limited income by offering flexible loan terms based on ability to pay.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay and household income level. For households at 60% of median income or below, interest rates range from 0% to 4.5%. For households at 80% of median income, interest rates range from 4.5% to 6.0%. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Deferred loans are available for borrowers with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Deferred principal and interest may be available for borrowers with no repayment capability at 30% and 50% of median income levels. Maximum loan amount is $50,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes who are income-eligible, and owners of rental residential properties whose units will be occupied by income-eligible households. Individuals with limited income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into buildings, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications to provide private space for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation test costs, and alternative and innovative septic and water systems. Funds can also pay for connections to public systems and general repairs to water or sewer systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Loan requests are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Income limits vary by household size and location, with higher limits in the Washington, D.C. PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties).
requirements_list: Must be an individual with limited income.
Owner-occupant of single-family home with inoperative, unsafe, or critical plumbing issues or indoor plumbing not in place
Property must be structurally sound
Owner-occupants must have household income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (specific limits by household size available)
For rental properties, residents of assisted units must have income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be primary residence
Photo identification required for applicant and co-applicant
Proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement or proof of ownership)
Current property tax bill and homeowners insurance policy declaration page
Licensed and insured Maryland contractor must provide bid and scope of work with photographs documenting the issue
Contractor must provide current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Bid must be from qualified Maryland tradesperson; grand total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
Bid should not be more than 60 days old
Income verification documentation (two months paystubs, two years federal income tax returns, bank statements, or award letters for benefits)
If person on deed is not applicant, provide proof of different address or death certificate if deceased
If home built before 1978, lead-based paint disclosures and documentation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact your local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, 877-218-8101, or 1-844-369-4150. Step 2: Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application form and gather all required supporting documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration, and photographs documenting the critical plumbing issues. Step 3: Obtain a bid from a licensed and insured Maryland contractor that includes scope of work, photographs, the contractor's MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form. Step 4: Submit completed application and all supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Step 5: Loans are originated, packaged, and closed by the Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies, which includes county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: DHCD provides grants and loans to help Maryland homeowners, landlords, and daycare center operators reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards in residential buildings and childcare facilities, preserve housing stock, and prevent lead poisoning. Grants of up to $25,000 per property are available to fund lead abatement services performed by licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors. The program offers three assistance options: grants, amortizing loans, and deferred loans. The program applies to both single-family homes and multi-family properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 per eligible property for lead abatement services. Available statewide except in the City of Baltimore. Grants require 10-20% match depending on sponsor type: 20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median income, and no match required for owner-occupants with limited income (less than 80% of median). Three loan options available: (1) Amortizing loans at 0%-7% interest for 20 years with up to $25,000 per unit; (2) Deferred loans at 0% interest for 20 years with up to $25,000 per unit, available only when underwriting shows no affordability to repay. Deferred loans may include loan forgiveness if no equity is available upon resale, transfer, or after 20 years. All assistance capped at $100,000 annual sponsor maximum. Funding available until April 1, 2029.

requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied single family home or rental property
For owner-occupants: must be Maryland resident, own and occupy dwelling as principal residence
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Licensed childcare facilities may also be eligible
Clearance testing is required

Grants require 20% match for for-profit sponsors, 10% match for nonprofit sponsors, or 10% match for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median income; no match required for owner-occupants with limited income (less than 80% of median)

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance community infrastructure projects. The program reduces financing costs through economies of scale by pooling local demand and provides expertise in managing the bond issuance process. Local governments borrow the bond proceeds at market rates and repay the debt. The program provides long-term capital financing for projects like streetscape improvements, transportation enhancements, water and sewer treatment facilities, and other public infrastructure.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on local government loans is subject to market conditions at the time of bond sale. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs. The loan term is set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Each participant pledges its full faith and credit to secure repayment. The program can finance projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted on a rolling basis. Bond issuances occur periodically based on volume and frequency of local government participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project, pledge security for and repay the loan, and pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system and may include street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements, public safety vehicles and equipment, water production and treatment, storage and distribution systems, storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities, government office and meeting facilities, police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service-related facilities, and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less
Project must generally range from $150,000 to $10 million or more in financing need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions. The local government completes a formal application that requests information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness, including financial data, project specifications, and legal documentation. Technical assistance is available through the Community Development Administration to help with the application process. The Community Development Administration reviews applications and coordinates bond issuances. Bond issuances occur periodically and are influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Sponsors of eligible housing projects receive tax credits that can be claimed on federal income tax returns. The program is governed by Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code and administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Community Development Administration (CDA).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building, with the applicable percentage determined by the IRS. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside the competitive process. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return over a 10-year credit period. Buildings must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years, consisting of an initial 15-year compliance period followed by a minimum 15-year extended use period. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Owners must maintain tenant income certifications, rent records, utility allowances, and other compliance documentation. Annual monitoring fees are required. The program offers two primary set-aside options: (1) 20-50 test: at least 20% of units affordable to households at or below 50% of area median gross income (AMGI), or (2) 40-60 test: at least 40% of units affordable to households at or below 60% of AMGI. Income-averaging options are also available. Maximum rent limits are established annually based on HUD Multifamily Tax Subsidy Program (MTSP) data and vary by county/metropolitan statistical area and household size. Tenant rent plus utility allowance cannot exceed maximum rent limits. Properties must serve the general public on a non-transient basis and meet all local health, safety, and building codes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Competitive allocations announced annually; properties must submit applications according to the Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP) timeline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible rental housing projects seeking to develop or rehabilitate affordable rental housing. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Project owners and their management agents must comply with all federal and state requirements throughout the compliance and extended use periods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Funds may be used for eligible basis costs including land acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and related professional fees. Projects must serve households with incomes at or below specified area median gross income limits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all 24 counties and Baltimore City. Income and rent limits vary by county or metropolitan statistical area. Properties must be located in Maryland to be eligible for state tax credit allocations.
requirements_list: Residential rental building must be placed in service in or within two years after the year the allocation is made
Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes of 50 percent or less of area median income or 40 percent of units to households with incomes of 60 percent or less of area median income (or meet income-averaging requirements)
Building must comply with requirements regarding tenant income, maximum rent levels, and percentage of low-income occupancy
Building must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years (15-year initial compliance period plus 15-year extended use period minimum)
Residential rental units must be suitable for occupancy and meet local health, safety, and building codes
Owner must receive annual Tenant Income Certifications from each low-income resident with supporting documentation
Owner must maintain utility allowances and update them at least once per calendar year
Owner must document rent restrictions and ensure rent does not exceed maximum limits
Owner must maintain documentation of next available unit assignments when applicable
Owner must comply with fair housing requirements and not refuse to lease to applicants with Section 8 vouchers
Owner must not evict or terminate tenancy of existing tenants except for good cause during extended use period
Owner must not increase gross rent above maximum allowed under Section 42 during extended use period
All tenant facilities included in eligible basis must be provided on comparable basis without charge to all tenants
Owner must maintain proper administrative records and project file with all pertinent documents
Owner must notify CDA of any changes in ownership, management, or other material changes to the project
Owner must submit Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance annually
Owner must comply with extended low-income housing commitment provisions
No finding of discrimination under Fair Housing Act may have occurred
Owner must maintain occupancy records and document vacancies and tenant assignments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owners submit a Notice of Intent after December 31 of the 14th year of compliance period if interested in Qualified Contract process, or during annual application cycles for new allocations. 2. For new allocations: Owners submit competitive applications according to the Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP) which is published annually and outlines scoring criteria, set-aside requirements, and other program rules. Applications are evaluated by CDA based on criteria including project feasibility, development team experience, targeting of low-income households, and community impact. 3. CDA issues preliminary approval and requests a cost certification from a CPA. 4. Upon receipt of cost certification, CDA completes and executes Part I of IRS Form 8609. 5. Owner completes Part II of Form 8609 and submits to IRS when filing personal, partnership, or corporate tax returns for the first year. A copy must be forwarded to CDA. 6. Owner records the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Covenant with local land records before end of calendar year in which credits are first claimed. 7. Throughout compliance and extended use periods, owner must submit annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance (OCPC) by deadline published in CDA notices. 8. CDA conducts on-site monitoring inspections at least once every five years during the extended use period, with file reviews of low-income unit certifications and rent records. 9. Owner must maintain all documentation on-site and available for CDA inspection. For the Qualified Contract process: Owner must submit Notice of Intent, then Qualified Contract Request Part I with proposed price calculation, then Part II with supporting documents and deposits. CDA seeks bona fide offer from qualified purchaser within one year. If successful, owner has 60 days to execute agreement or offer is deemed rejected.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to further Maryland's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. The program funds local jurisdictions, 501(c) non-profit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions to advance digital inclusion through both planning and implementation of digital inclusion programs. It supports broadband adoption for covered populations for educational and employment opportunities, digital literacy training, and public access computing centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for Digital Inclusion Planning: up to 50% of planning costs with a minimum of $5,000 and maximum of $30,000. Grants for Digital Inclusion Implementation/Programming: up to 100% of program costs with a minimum of $10,000 and maximum of $75,000 per application. Total program funding is $2 million. Grant amounts may be reduced based on impact and ability to deploy funds responsibly and quickly. Applicants are highly encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage the available grant funding. Funded projects must comply with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) requirements and all federal rules regarding this funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties or municipalities), 501(c) nonprofits, and community-based anchor institutions committed to digital inclusion. Covered populations include individuals with household income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers or low literacy, racial or ethnic minorities, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To develop digital inclusion plans and implement digital inclusion activities; to facilitate broadband adoption for covered populations for educational and employment opportunities; to implement training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; to construct, upgrade, expand, or operate public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; to research and identify populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers; to enhance understanding of internet service; to assist households with applications for internet service; to enhance community capacity to access jurisdiction services and participate in civic matters. Grant funds may NOT be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Services must be provided within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), a 501(c) nonprofit providing services within Maryland, or a community-based anchor institution
Digital Inclusion Planning: minimum grant request $5,000, maximum $30,000, up to 50% of planning costs
Digital Inclusion Implementation: minimum grant request $10,000, maximum $75,000, up to 100% of implementation costs
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Only fully complete applications will be considered for funding
Application form must be completed in its entirety with all required information

Applications must include: completed and signed application form, executive summary with project overview, population needs, barriers, partners, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience
Scope of work specific to the funding requested must be provided

Simple budget required showing spending in categories: operations (payroll, supplies, materials), contracted services (payments to independent contractors, external organizations), travel (must be related to program deployment), and any other funding sources
IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status required if applicable
Online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation required
IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification required
Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number required for the organization
Federal EIN Number required
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of awardee and State to the Project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: NOFA released February 9, 2022. Application submission opens February 15, 2022 and closes March 31, 2022. Submit all applications and supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization'. Include the applicant's legal name (must match W-9), Federal EIN Number, DUNS Number, office address, and primary contact information. Attach completed application form, executive summary, project budget, and Federal Form W-9. The OSB intends to award funds beginning in May 2022. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interview. Funding announcements to be made on or before April 15, 2022. Grant awards range from $50,000 to $350,000
Funding covers up to 100% of eligible program costs

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants for Main Street improvements. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive allocated funding amounts distributed equally. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive allocated funding amounts distributed equally. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive allocated funding amounts distributed equally. For current allocation amounts, please refer to the program webpage. Funds support operating expenses only, including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. All projects and activities should be completed within one year; a funding match is not required. Awards are contingent upon availability and allocation of sufficient State funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other projects that have been identified in the applicant's work plans as key to its Main Street efforts. Funds support operating expenses only; capital project costs are not supported. All activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the transformation strategy of the community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland's designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities. Designated Sustainable Community areas throughout Maryland, with additional consideration for projects in designated ENOUGH areas and Just Communities.

Projects and activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan
Projects and activities must contribute to the transformation strategy of the community
All projects and activities must be completed within one year
Operating expenses only; capital project costs are not supported
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Current awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State
Awardees must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest
Awardees must maintain all project-related records for a minimum of three years after official close-out of the award
Final report must be submitted no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date
Awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of award execution date; all awarded funds must be drawn down by the award agreement's expiration date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. Register as a new user if needed; approval may take up to 72 hours. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Ensure your organization profile includes all required nonprofit documentation (evidence of nonprofit status, good standing, and charitable registration) before submitting. Contact your project manager to confirm your organization's standing before applying. Application period opens Friday, February 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM EDT and closes Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT. Late applications will not be accepted. All applications must be submitted online; first-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. Applications must align with the Main Street annual work plan. Site visits and/or follow-up discussions with applicants may be conducted prior to award decisions. Award recommendations are subject to review and approval by the Secretary of DHCD. Final authorization of award amounts is contingent upon approval by the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session. Upon approval, DHCD will notify successful applicants through the Project Portal by sending official award letters. Award Agreement execution occurs when both parties have signed and witnessed the document via DocuSign. The authorized signatory must sign and return within five business days of receipt. Funds cannot be drawn down until after execution and all Special Conditions have been met. Following award execution, awardees may begin requesting funds. Progress reports are due at the 6-month mark from grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted. All payment requests must be submitted electronically through the Project Portal and must align with activities and budget outlined in the award agreement. An advance of up to 25% of total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required. Subsequent requests must include evidence of expenditures such as paid invoices, contracts, or itemized receipts. Virtual application training and individual technical assistance sessions are available.

list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for small businesses to cover renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and certain other costs associated with business recovery. The program provides working capital and recovery funding for eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Colleen Cord-Malone, Business Lending Programs Manager II; Aisha K. Taylor, Business Lending Programs Loan Underwriter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces that have been affected by declared disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and certain other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County and must show evidence of damage or loss associated with the May 2018 flooding events.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business or nonprofit organization
Business must be located in a commercial space
Applicant must show proof of insurance status
Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Must show evidence of damage or loss associated with May 2018 flooding events

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses access financing by enabling private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund. The program uses contributions from lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland to reduce lender risk on loans that fall slightly outside normal credit guidelines. The program supports businesses located in Priority Funding Areas across Maryland. Note: No lenders are currently participating in this program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program works through participating lenders who enroll appropriate loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Lender, borrower, and the program each contribute to a reserve account (typically 1.5 percent from lender, 1.5 percent from borrower, and 3 percent match from the program for a total reserve of 6 percent of the original loan amount). In case of loan default, the reserve account covers losses up to 75 percent of the account balance. This effectively provides a loan guarantee/credit enhancement for small businesses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: There are no lenders currently participating.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Priority Funding Areas, including nonprofit organizations, seeking financing that may fall slightly outside traditional lender credit guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business loans for small business growth and expansion. Cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential housing, facilities such as hospitals or universities, adult entertainment, check cashing, gambling, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas as approved by the Maryland Department of Planning.
requirements_list: Business must be a small business located in Maryland
Business must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Loan amount must range from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential housing or transient living facilities
Project cannot be certain restricted business types
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small business applies to a participating lender. Lender underwrites and enrolls the loan. Lender, borrower, and program contribute to a reserve account. Lender submits one-page enrollment form to the program.
