structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Facade Improvement Program provides funding to improve the exteriors of businesses located in Maryland Sustainable Communities. The program supports communities seeking to create consistent, attractive designs for their commercial corridors in order to bolster economic vitality and stimulate new private investments. Local governments and community development organizations apply to capitalize a grants fund and develop an application process for businesses to improve their building facades.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are provided as grants to local governments and community development organizations to capitalize their own local facade improvement programs. These programs then award grants to eligible businesses for capital improvements to the exterior facades of commercial properties. Individual business improvements must range from $1,000 to $50,000 of MFIP funding per award cycle. Eligible uses include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Improvements must prioritize aesthetic improvements on or attached to primary elevations of commercial properties over routine maintenance. Predevelopment and operating expenses including acquisition, permitting, and architectural services are ineligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, counties, and community development organizations located in or serving Sustainable Communities. Final recipients of MFIP funding must be businesses located within the State's designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to exterior facades of commercial properties including signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 per business per award cycle. Interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, and improvements to vacant properties are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland Facade Improvement Program funding can only be used in areas known as Sustainable Communities, which are geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility. All MFIP projects are subject to the Maryland Historical Trust Act and the Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation for properties over 50 years old.
requirements_list: Applicants must be counties, municipalities, or community development organizations
Project should capitalize on the strengths of a community while addressing its challenges to revitalization
Project should help to achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants
Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle
Changes to completed improvements that received MFIP funding within the last 12 months are ineligible
Improvements must comply with all local building codes, zoning ordinances, and Historic Preservation Commission requirements
Work completed prior to receipt of a letter of commitment is ineligible for funding
Applicants must provide evidence of expenditures including receipts or canceled checks
Applicants must maintain valid insurance coverage for property damage and personal injury
Applicants agree to maintain property improvements and return pro-rated grant funds if improvements are removed within two years
All improvements are subject to historic preservation review by DHCD staff and the Maryland Historical Trust
Work must be completed in less than 120 days from date of award to be most competitive
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the MFIP application and submit required attachments including evidence of site control, photographs of existing conditions, written consent from landlord and lessee (if applicable), project description with two cost estimates and detailed sketches, and a screenshot from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation showing the business is in good standing. The application must include general information about the applicant, business name, project address, and property owner information. Property owners or authorized representatives must sign the application. DHCD reviews applications competitively with priority given to projects that contribute to community harmony, support Sustainable Communities Action Plan goals, improve historic features, have timelines under 120 days, support legacy and minority businesses, and demonstrate commitment to excellent design. All projects are subject to historic preservation review before work begins. For more information, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization or local government agency

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides affordable funding through special loan programs to help homeowners preserve and improve their single-family homes. The program addresses critical health and safety issues and brings properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. Low-interest loans are available to help homeowners fix problems such as mold remediation, roof repair, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, structural repairs, and accessibility improvements for seniors and disabled residents. To qualify, a household's income must not exceed 80% of the Adjusted Median Income set by DHCD each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and household income. Interest rates are 4.5%–6.0% for households at 80% of median income, and 0%–4.5% for households at 60% of median income. Maximum loan is generally $50,000 or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage (deed of trust). Households with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may qualify for deferred payments of principal and interest if needed for project feasibility. The maximum initial deposit is 33% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners needing repairs for health, safety, and building code compliance. Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income not exceeding 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Homeowners with incomes at or below 60% of median income are eligible for lower interest rates (0%–4.5%).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs addressing health and safety issues including: mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, gutters, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement (gas ranges, water heaters, space heat), HVAC replacement for end of service life, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage including bulk water mitigation by drain tile, sump pump, and minor grading, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and knob and tube removal including necessary service upgrades, electrical upgrades for future home electrification (100A to 200A upgrades), plumbing issues, water and well repair, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion or security, structural repairs (atrophy, rot, insect, settling, storm-related), accessibility improvements for disabled and seniors and persons with special needs including chair lifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, and doors, fall and injury prevention (handrails, rubber treads, bathroom grab bars), ductwork upgrades and installations (primarily for solid fuel-burning households, mainly in Allegany and Garrett counties), building shell stabilization, and pest treatments (rats, roaches, and mice).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Loans are processed by local government offices for properties within their jurisdiction. Applicants should contact their local housing office by county. Income limits vary by region: Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area (includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) and Rest of State.
requirements_list: Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (detached single family homes, duplexes, townhomes, and condos eligible; mobile homes excluded)
Household income cannot exceed 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Provide a work proposal from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor or other trade professional within the past 60 days
Provide photos documenting the issues requiring repair

Contractor must provide current MHIC license or trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.), Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Proof of home ownership including copy of deed and current mortgage statement
Photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant
Copy of most recent Property Tax Bill
Copy of Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy and Flood Insurance Policy if applicable
No active bankruptcy or foreclosure; both must be dismissed for a minimum of 2 years before assistance can be provided
Lowest qualifying bid should not be more than 60 days old
Grand total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs office at (301) 429-7409 or (877) 218-8101. Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program application and submit the following: (1) Income verification documents (most recent 2 months of paystubs or employment verification letter, 2 years of Federal Income Tax Returns, 2 months of bank statements, award letters for Social Security/disability/pension/public assistance); (2) Documentation of home ownership (photo ID, deed, current mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance policy if applicable); (3) Work proposal and photos from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement contractor or trade professional dated within the past 60 days; (4) Completed Bid Cover Page per contractor with bid attached; (5) Contractor documentation (current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, completed W-9 form). Submit completed application and supporting documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loans are reviewed for verification of work meeting health and safety requirements and contractor qualifications. Once approved, applicants sign commitment letter, rehabilitation contract, construction agreement, and W-9 form. Loans are processed, packaged, and closed by the network of local administering agencies including county offices and nonprofit organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative designed to help certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses reduce the interest rate on loans they obtain from participating banks. Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on their loans to help them access affordable capital for growing and expanding their business.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating lenders offer loans at an interest rate up to 2% lower than the standard rate for similar loans. The state treasurer deposits an amount equal to the loan with the lending bank at a reduced interest rate. The interest rate reduction benefit is available for the full term of the loan, up to 10 years, for term loans only or loans with fixed rates and one disbursement. Loans cannot exceed 10 years and points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount. The program leverages $50 million of state funds. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds must be used for projects located in Maryland. Funds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects and activities must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a certified minority business enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, or a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining the qualifying loan
Must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to maintain the interest rate reduction benefit
Loan must be obtained from a participating bank designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years
Loan proceeds must be for a project or activity located in Maryland
Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. The department verifies eligibility and forwards the application to all enrolled banks, or notifies the lender of the borrower's eligibility if the lender applied on behalf of the borrower. The borrower receives a list of participating banks and contacts them to complete full application requirements. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank. Banks underwrite the loan according to their standard process and offer an interest rate up to 2% less than the standard rate. Upon loan approval and acceptance, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program. The state treasurer then deposits an amount equal to the loan with the bank at a reduced interest rate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program

The program supports small businesses, micro-businesses, and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) businesses with limited opportunities for growth, targeting communities and areas with high concentrations of these business types. It partners with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI provides funding through various small business financing programs including capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs. Funds are issued through lending partners to eligible businesses — no grants. The program also includes the Neighborhood BusinessWorks Loan Participation Program and the Own Your Future Program for property acquisition support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, micro-businesses, and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) businesses with limited opportunities for growth, particularly those in communities with high concentrations of such businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing and growth through capital access, loan participation, loan guarantees, collateral support, venture equity, and property acquisition support (through Own Your Future Program).

County governments, regional government groups, and private organizations can also sponsor a circuit for these municipalities.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Eligible governments are notified when applications are due each year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can only pay for the salary and fringe benefits of circuit rider staff to assist with specific municipal functions and activities for a two-year period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participating municipalities must have populations of 5,000 or less and must be within reasonable proximity to each other. Circuit sponsors must consist of two or more municipalities.
requirements_list: Participating municipalities must have populations of 5,000 or less
Sponsors must be municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations
Circuit must consist of two or more municipalities within reasonable proximity to each other
Funding can only be used for salary and fringe benefits over a two-year period
Applicants are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment
Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance

Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Microenterprise Loan Program provides flexible financing to entrepreneurs for microenterprise start-ups and expansions in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. The program works through partnerships with community-based microlenders (Community Development Financial Institutions/CDFIs) who originate and administer loans and provide training and technical assistance. These CDFIs lend money to small businesses and microenterprises in Maryland communities to support local economies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microenterprise loans up to $50,000 are provided at rates up to 12 percent with loan terms not exceeding 5 years. Additional funds may be added by the intermediary lender. Collateral is required which may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. No prepayment penalties apply. The program also offers loans directly to local CDFIs who then lend to small businesses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs seeking to start or expand microenterprises (small businesses with annual revenue not exceeding $500,000 and no more than 5 employees) located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas, as well as Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning, feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. CDFIs use loan funds to provide financing to small businesses and microenterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in designated Sustainable Communities or Priority Funding Areas. Eligible counties include Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Retail business, manufacturing business, or goods and services related business
Located in designated Sustainable Community area
Annual revenue does not exceed $500,000
No more than 5 employees at time of application

Not a residential or transient living business, multifamily or single-family housing development, nursing home, assisted living facility, crisis care center, group home, transitional housing, or homeless shelter
Not an adult entertainment facility, gambling facility, gun shop, liquor store, massage parlor, pawn shop, tanning salon, or tattoo parlor
Not a home-based business
Collateral is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the intermediary microlender (CDFI) serving your county directly to receive an application. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development has established partnerships with community-based microlenders (intermediaries) that originate and administer microenterprise loans. Each intermediary serves specific counties. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides tax-exempt bonds and notes to increase the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. Financing can be used for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing with at least five units, and can be combined with federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (4% LIHTC) to finance rental housing projects. The program also supports families with limited incomes by expanding the availability of affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing through multiple credit enhancement options including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (Section 542(c)), GNMA MBS (FHA Sections 221(d)(4)), Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, FNMA MBS Collateral, and cash collateral options. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate and vary by financing structure. Construction loan terms typically range from 20-24 months with interest-only or capitalized interest payments. Permanent loan amortization periods range from 35-40 years with permanent rates generally ranging from 5.520% to 6.670% depending on the financing structure (all-in rates ranging from 5.770% to 6.670% as of April 2, 2026). Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years. A first lien position is generally required. Projects may use unallocated 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits if they comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration and Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program. Multiple financing structures are available including public offerings, private placements, and draw-down loans. Unrated private placements and rated bond transactions are both available options.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs; Benedict DuRant; Kristen Musallam
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers seeking to develop or rehabilitate multifamily rental housing for low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing containing a minimum of five units. Loans may also refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance is in conjunction with housing rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located in designated Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Rental housing must contain a minimum of five units
Housing must be for families with limited incomes
Projects using tax-exempt bond financing must contain complete independent dwelling units
Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits
A sponsor must make either 20 units available to households earning 50% or less of area median income, OR make 40% of units available to households earning 60% or less of area median income
All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program
A first lien position is generally required for all bond loans
All loans funded with tax-exempt bonds must comply with federal requirements established for tax-exempt revenue bonds
Bond proceeds must be sufficient to satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits
The full amount of Bonds must be secured 100% by cash collateral (Letter of Credit is not sufficient)
GNMA Loan must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or other similar HUD programs (FHA Risk Sharing with CDA is not eligible)
A MAP Lender must be engaged by the borrower for GNMA financing
For unrated private placements, the entity purchasing the Bonds must be CDA-approved and must retain the Bonds for the entire term without selling, pledging, transferring or disposing of them
For unrated private placements, the interest rate on the Bonds must be approved by CDA to ensure competitiveness in the tax-exempt bond market
For rated bond transactions, a bankruptcy opinion meeting rating agency requirements (such as Moody's) must be obtained at the borrower's expense
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective borrowers should contact the CDA Multifamily staff to discuss financing options and structure. A TEFRA Public Hearing Notice may be required for proposed multifamily rental developments. Borrowers must complete application materials and work with CDA loan underwriters to determine the appropriate financing structure. For projects using Tax/TE Financing with GNMA Loans, borrowers must engage a MAP Lender and structure the transaction as either an unrated private placement or rated bond offering. Projects must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan requirements and fee schedules. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - EmPOWER
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides grants or loans to reduce electric or gas consumption in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Funding can be used for energy efficiency measures and limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects that reduce energy consumption. All building sizes and configurations are eligible, including single family units as group projects, individually metered, or master metered buildings. The program aims to reduce greenhouse gases and keep housing affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides funding through grants or loans with 0% interest and deferred payments. Funding is allocated at $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. Tier 1 funding is available for projects with a minimum of 20% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 5 years. Tier 2 funding is available for projects with a minimum of 20% of households at 80% AMI or less for a minimum of 15 years. Funding covers energy efficiency measures, electrification measures, health and safety work, and incidental repairs necessary for measure installation. The MEEHA Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) provides additional funding for covered buildings under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS), with funding limited to $15,000 per unit and requiring a minimum of 51% of units at or below 80% AMI for a minimum of 15 years. All building sizes and configurations are eligible, including single family units as group projects, individually metered, or master metered buildings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of affordable multifamily rental housing developments, including government bodies, for-profit companies, non-profit organizations, and individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including building shell improvements (air sealing, insulation, fenestration), HVAC system upgrades, domestic hot water system improvements, lighting upgrades, appliance replacements, and renewable energy systems such as solar. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing measures that reduce electric or gas consumption. Electrification measures to replace fossil fuel systems with electric systems. Gas reducing measures are allowed only if the customer is in the Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Gas reducing measures limited to BGE or WGL utility territories.
requirements_list: Project must be an affordable multifamily rental housing development
A minimum of 20% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 5 years (Tier 1) or 15 years (Tier 2)

For GHGRP, a minimum of 51% of households must be at or below 80% AMI for a minimum of 15 years and building must be 35,000+ sq ft or multiple buildings totaling 35,000+ sq ft served by same meter or system
For rehabilitation projects, a Qualified Energy Professional must complete an energy audit in compliance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Energy audit must identify eligible energy conservation and decarbonization measures (ECMs)
Qualified Energy Professional must submit the Funding Request on behalf of the project owner
Property must be affordable or serve low income households
Energy audit must include sampling protocol of at least 10% of dwelling units (minimum 5 units) with at least one representative unit from each unique unit type
Post-retrofit ventilation must meet ASHRAE 62.2 standards
Air sealing is mandatory if feasible; HVAC replacement is mandatory if equipment is past expected useful life; insulation is mandatory in certain conditions
Regulatory agreement or tax covenant must demonstrate affordability compliance for minimum required period
Utility account information and customer consent to release energy use information required
Measure costs must be based on actual contractor bids including materials, equipment, and installation
Health and Safety and Incidental Repair costs combined cannot exceed 10% of total energy efficiency measure funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Property owner obtains energy audit from DHCD Qualified Energy Professional. 2. Qualified Energy Professional completes comprehensive energy audit for rehabilitation projects or energy certification review for new construction in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards and program guidance. 3. Energy Professional recommends eligible energy conservation and decarbonization measures (ECMs) with costs based on contractor bids. 4. Qualified Energy Professional submits MEEHA Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner using DHCD Rehab Funding Request Form (or MINT system when operational in 2026). 5. Owner submits MEEHA Application and required documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov including application form, utility bills, customer consent forms, deed with legal description, SDAT ownership and status checks, Minority Business Enterprise Plan, ACH Direct Deposit Form, proof of affordability, and W-9 form. 6. DHCD reviews and verifies funding request and application materials. 7. DHCD finalizes the Funding Request and determines funding tier and amounts. 8. DHCD creates and sends funding agreement (grant or loan agreement) to project owner for execution. 9. Project owner executes funding agreement and returns to DHCD. 10. Project installs funded energy efficiency measures per approved scope. 11. DHCD performs post-installation inspection to verify equipment installation and compliance. 12. DHCD releases funding after equipment has been installed and inspected. 13. Project enters affordability compliance period with monitoring by DHCD.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that reduces direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Funding also supports building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GHGRP provides grants only with no loan option. Funding is allocated at $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026. The program offers up to $15,000 per dwelling unit, with a project cap of $1.25 million. Projects must maintain a minimum of 51% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years. Eligible projects must be existing buildings with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more, excluding parking garages. Funding is disbursed on a reimbursement basis through a requisition process during the course of construction as work is completed and verified. Eligible measures include replacing fossil fuel-fired equipment with electric equipment, incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure, energy efficiency and conservation improvements, and alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more, housing at least 51% of tenants at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment. Building energy conservation measures and weatherization upgrades to the building shell, HVAC or water heating systems, lighting, appliances, and fenestration. Alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics. Incidental repairs required to allow installation of program-funded energy saving measures. Health and safety measures to prevent issues regarding indoor air quality, mold, etc. Electrification costs associated with installing electrification measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be an affordable multifamily rental housing development

Project must be an existing building with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more, excluding parking garages, OR two or more buildings with a combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more (excluding parking garage area) served in whole or in part by the same electric or gas meter or by the same heating or cooling system(s), which is not a district energy system
A minimum of 51% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years

If no initial regulatory agreement exists or current affordability restrictions have fewer than 15 years remaining, the property must accept regulatory restrictions for a period not less than 15 years
For rehabilitation projects, a Qualified Energy Professional must complete an energy audit in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Energy audit must identify eligible greenhouse gas reduction measures and include ASHRAE ventilation calculations
Qualified Energy Professional must submit the Funding Request on behalf of the project owner using DHCD's Rehab Funding Request Form or MINT (Hancock Mobile Intake Tool) when operational
Projects must set up an Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and follow MDE and/or EPA guidelines for creating a benchmarking report
Third party verification report required
Annual energy use benchmarking reports must be provided to DHCD for a minimum of two (2) years after construction completion
Portfolio Manager must be updated annually with the previous 12 months of utility data after construction is complete
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner sets up an Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and follows MDE and/or EPA guidelines for creating and generating a benchmarking report. 2. Owner submits a completed MEEHA Application and required documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov, including Portfolio Manager baseline report, third party verification report, and other required application documents (or submits 202 application form if also applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs). 3. A Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list completes a comprehensive energy audit for rehabilitation projects or energy certification review for new construction projects, in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards. 4. Qualified Energy Professional submits the Energy Audit Report, recommended scope of work, and Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of the project owner, including greenhouse gas emissions reductions data and estimated costs. 5. DHCD reviews and finalizes the Funding Request. 6. A DHCD Project Manager conducts meetings and visual inspections on a monthly basis to track construction progress. 7. DHCD creates a funding agreement to be executed. 8. Project installs the funded greenhouse gas reduction measures. 9. DHCD disburses funding on a reimbursement basis through a requisition process as work is completed and verified. 10. Project provides annual energy use benchmarking reports to DHCD for a minimum of two years after construction completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) offers competitive funding for business and housing projects in areas chosen for revitalization. The program focuses on places where a small, planned investment can make a big difference in improving the neighborhood, supporting strategic economic development projects in the National Capital region through capital investments and revitalization initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant and loan funding provided for commercial and residential development projects including down payment assistance for homebuyers, property acquisition and rehabilitation, property improvements, energy efficiency upgrades (weatherization and energy retrofits), affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing, retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition. Also supports broader capital projects for strategic economic development and community revitalization in the National Capital region.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community development organizations seeking to revitalize targeted neighborhoods in the National Capital region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquiring or rehabilitating vacant or dilapidated properties, improving existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, developing affordable housing, creating mixed-use projects combining housing, retail and office space, developing or enhancing community open space or public infrastructure, and strategic demolition. Funds must support projects listed in a Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in designated Sustainable Communities within specific boundaries. In Prince George's County, the area must be at least partly inside the Capital Beltway (I-495) and the District of Columbia. In Montgomery County, the area must be within an Enterprise Zone or bounded by Prince George's County, MD-200, I-270, I-495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities
Projects must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be in eligible geographic boundaries as defined for Prince George's or Montgomery County
Project must be located in the National Capital region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through Project Portal after registering as a new user. Registration must be completed by June 11, 2025. Application period closed July 2, 2025. For more information and application procedures, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: An affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The National Housing Trust Fund provides federal funding to increase and preserve affordable housing supply for extremely low-income and very low-income households under guidelines established by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Extremely low-income and very low-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing production and preservation

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects. A business project qualifies if it is located in a priority funding area and is acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business, whether or not for profit. Some qualified business projects are also located in traditionally underserved areas defined as Sustainable Communities. The program, also known as Neighborhood Business Works (NBW), has a 20+ year history of financing small businesses in Maryland and currently manages a portfolio of 158 loans with an aggregate outstanding principal balance exceeding $20 million.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration obtains legislative authority to issue bonds to fund loans for business projects. Project types include: (1) Commercial real estate, including construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; (2) Commercial real estate, including acquisition or refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; (3) Non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy and/or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. Loans are structured as senior or subordinate loans, or a combination of both. For-profit borrowers require minimum 10% equity contribution with maximum 90% CLTV financing. Non-profit borrowers require minimum 5% equity contribution with maximum 95% CLTV financing. Upfront costs include 0.5% to 1% upfront financing fee, $25,000 for DHCD legal counsel, plus normal real estate and loan closing fees. Interest override targets minimum 0.60% annually for portfolio administration and investor reporting, plus 0.40% loan servicing and asset management fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business projects and qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking financing in priority funding areas and sustainable communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy and/or use by qualified nonprofit organizations. Funds support projects in traditionally underserved areas with emphasis on revitalization impact, elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus, and job retention/creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas as defined in Section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article or in Sustainable Communities as defined in Section 6-205 of DHCD's Article, Title 5 Subtitle 13 of the Economic Development Article, or Section 7-101 of the Transportation Article. Some projects are also located in Just Communities.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a priority funding area or sustainable communities
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business
For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost borrower contribution
Non-profit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost borrower contribution
For-profit borrowers: maximum 90% CLTV financing or 100% CLTV with two-loan structure (70% senior, 30% subordinate state-appropriated)
Non-profit borrowers: maximum 95% CLTV financing or 100% CLTV with two-loan structure (70% senior, 30% subordinate state-appropriated)
Loan debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service
Minimum pro-forma 1.50 DSCR throughout the life of the loan for CDA-funded loans; 1.25 DSCR for credit-enhanced non-CDA loans
Industry-standard underwriting criteria including credit worthiness of borrower, market position, adequacy of collateral, and soundness of business plan
Collateral valuation by qualified professional and independent appraiser acceptable to CDA, MHF and debt investors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application to facilitate loan intake and underwriting. CDA business lending underwriters perform comprehensive loan underwriting for all CDA-funded business loans, subject to internal and external credit committee approval. All NBLP CDA business loan underwriting is reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC). All NBLP loans over $250,000 as well as MHF credit enhancement for business loans are reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the NBW Loan Review Committee. All projects are evaluated based on revitalization impact on the community including elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus, and job retention/creation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides financing options for new and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations during all phases of business growth. The program helps finance businesses whose efforts improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers, supporting businesses located in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities across the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct, insured, or guaranteed loans to small businesses and nonprofit organizations. Financing is available through direct business loans and lending partners including banks and community development financial institutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and expansion, revitalization of commercial districts and town centers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities throughout Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can complete a pre-application consultation and then submit a financing application online. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The program covers a significant portion of capital construction costs with a required local match. Funding comes from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARP) administered by the US Treasury.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 covering 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for extending broadband service to unserved areas. Required cash or in-kind match of 10% to 30% of capital construction costs depending on project density. For wired infrastructure: Fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match; 8-15 households per mile requires 20% match; 15+ households per mile requires 30% match. For wireless infrastructure: Fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match; 40-70 households per tower requires 20% match; 70+ households per tower requires 30% match. Match from local jurisdictions must be cash; ISP partners may contribute cash or in-kind capital construction costs. Grant funds may be used for: (1) construction of facilities to deploy service at minimum broadband speeds to all end users; (2) middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service including interconnections between non-contiguous service areas; (3) electronics necessary to deliver service including OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and equipment shelters. Ineligible uses include duplication of existing service, unnecessary middle mile infrastructure, telephone or video service expenses, engineering design services, purchase of land or towers, building construction or renovations, and operating expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 23, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and their internet service provider partners seeking to expand broadband to unserved areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for extending broadband service to unserved areas, including outside plant construction, middle mile infrastructure, electronics and equipment necessary to deliver service at minimum broadband speeds
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; eligible project areas must be unserved with no locations receiving broadband service at 25 Mbps download by 3 Mbps upload speeds with latency at or below 50ms. Areas having received state grant funding in the past are ineligible for additional funding.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a County or Municipality listed on the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Must partner with an established internet service provider (ISP)
Project area must be unserved (lacking terrestrial fixed internet service above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50ms)

Projects must provide minimum connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50ms (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds for geographic/topographic reasons with ISP certification)
Local jurisdiction must have entered into partnership with ISP prior to funding agreement
Required cash or in-kind match based on project density (10-30% of eligible capital construction costs)
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023

Applications must include completed Grant Application Form, Executive Summary, partnership information, experience statements, network design and construction details, subscriber profile, subscriber costs and limitations, detailed line-item capital budget, implementation schedule, graphical maps showing PFSA and infrastructure, and GIS shapefiles (shp, kmz or kml format)
All submitted responses and supporting documents must be combined into one zip file
Project facilities will be owned by the Local Jurisdiction or ISP Partner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete response to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 23, 2021 with subject line including 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Application package must include: completed Grant Application Form, Executive Summary describing unserved area and project benefits, partnership information naming ISP Partner, experience statements from senior team members of both applicant and ISP Partner, detailed network design and construction description, subscriber profile and demographic data, subscriber service options and costs, line-item capital construction budget (submitted as both PDF and Excel spreadsheet), implementation schedule with key milestones, graphical maps of PFSA and infrastructure, and GIS shapefiles on separate layers. All items should be combined into a single zip file. DHCD will review applications for completeness and eligibility. Applications will be scored on up to 25 points based on: Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points). Awards are expected to be facilitated beginning in April 2022. Reimbursement is made on a reimbursement basis after Local Jurisdiction pays eligible Project costs and submits invoices with supporting documentation within 30 days of payment. DHCD will make reimbursements within 60 days after approval of invoice.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides matching grants to support operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations that stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. These organizations partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the State to provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling services, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible Neighborhood Housing Services corporation may apply for a grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Umbrella corporations may apply for grants for each program under their supervision, also up to $50,000 per program without exceeding one-third of the annual operating budget for that program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation that serve low- and moderate-income households in targeted neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations, which support homeownership programs, home rehabilitation, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling services, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Neighborhoods served by certified NHS corporations in Maryland, including multiple neighborhoods in Baltimore City and Baltimore County served by NHS of Baltimore and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center, and the West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods of Salisbury served by Salisbury NHS.
requirements_list: Must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local NHS corporation
Local political subdivision must participate on the NHS corporation's board of directors
State grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions
Grant amount cannot exceed $50,000
Grant amount cannot exceed one-third of the NHS corporation's annual operating budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible NHS corporations apply for grants annually. Contact the Poverty Solutions Team at the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for application instructions and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NourishMD Grant Program expands access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity. It provides direct grants to eligible food retailers to support operations, capital needs, and improvements. Supplemental loan funding is also available through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible projects may receive grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 to support capital-related needs that contribute to business stabilization or expansion. Up to $2 million in total grant funding is available. A $250 processing fee is required for all applications and may be paid directly from the awarded grant funds if the applicant is approved for funding. Supplemental loan funding is also available through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, which undergoes thorough financial review to assess the applicant's capacity to manage debt. Funds support equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), facility upgrades, renovation and build-out, capital costs for inventory expansion, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure for SNAP/EBT acceptance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers serving communities with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Food retailers include but are not limited to grocery stores, corner stores, farm stands and other on-farm markets, farmers' markets, food co-ops, delivery retailers serving populations with low fresh food access, and small retail stores where the majority of inventory or sales are food-related (if no more than 25% of gross sales are derived from alcohol/tobacco products).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of furniture, fixtures, and/or equipment (e.g., refrigeration, shelving); renovation and build-out; facility upgrades; capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods); working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction; and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. For purposes of this program, 'Food Deserts' is defined as any area with a Maryland Community Business Compass fresh food gap score of 60% or higher pursuant to Annotated Code of Maryland - Housing and Community Development Article §6–308. Retailers located in areas with documented food insecurity are prioritized. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Note: Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program. However, if you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Operate at least 5 days per week year-round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year-round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)

Currently or plan to offer a variety of high-quality fresh produce, or a mix of fresh, frozen, and preserved produce, as well as other healthy grocery items (e.g., whole grains, dairy products, fresh meats/proteins)
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items, which may be based on square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory for sale
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
A $250 processing fee is sourced from the award amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications opened on January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closed on February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST through an online portal. Only completed applications that include all required documentation will be eligible for review. Required documentation includes: (1) a detailed written plan describing how grant funds will be used (not exceeding 2 pages), (2) information demonstrating compliance with the 20% healthy food inventory/space requirement including documentation, photos, or store layout, (3) one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation if operating less than one year), and (4) supporting documentation for relocation or expansion projects (lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control). The $250 processing fee must be submitted with the application. Applications are under review during the February-March 2026 review period. DHCD staff will evaluate eligible applications for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities, then refer the final list to the Review Committee for determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April 2026, award announcements occur in May 2026, and Board of Public Works approval and disbursements occur in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program assists nonprofit organizations and local governments with operating costs associated with community and economic revitalization efforts throughout Maryland. The program provides grants to help cover operating expenses for local housing and community revitalization projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Maximum grant award is $50,000 per application. No funding match is required. Grant term is one year from the date the award agreement is signed by DHCD. An advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required; evidence of how advanced funds were spent must be submitted with the next payment request. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. Awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of award execution, and all funds must be drawn down by the award agreement expiration date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, and placemaking initiatives. Capital project costs and ineligible expenses such as alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, fines, or parking tickets are not supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool to verify PFA eligibility. Additional consideration given to projects in designated ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or local government in Maryland
Must be engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Projects or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans and/or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or state agencies
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
Maximum grant award is $50,000
No matching funds are required
Funds cannot be used for capital project costs

Nonprofit applicants must submit: Evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), Evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and Evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State
Current awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting reporting deadlines and submitting required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
For projects involving acquisition, demolition, construction, or rehabilitation, site control must be demonstrated at time of award agreement execution
Organizations must maintain records for minimum of three years after official close-out of the award
Organizations must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register on the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/IGXLogin by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form (approval may take up to 72 hours). 2. First-time applicants should contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access; new organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline. 3. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents (nonprofit status evidence, good standing documentation, and charitable registration) before submitting your application; applications missing documents may be disqualified. 4. Complete the online application through the Project Portal for the TAG program. 5. Submit application through the Project Portal by the deadline. 6. Applications are evaluated using a single 5-point scoring scale (0=Not Evident, 1=Minimally Meets Expectations, 3=Somewhat Meets Expectations, 5=Strongly Meets/Exemplary) reflecting overall strength and readiness. 7. Bonus points are awarded: up to 10 points for ENOUGH areas, 10 points for Just Communities. 8. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants for follow-up discussions prior to award decisions. 9. Upon approval by DHCD leadership and the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session, successful applicants receive official award letters through the Project Portal. 10. Award agreement is drafted and sent via DocuSign; authorized signatory must sign within five business days. 11. Once executed and special conditions met, award moves to active status and management begins.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows businesses to source additional capital and receive federal tax incentives by locating or expanding in designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program enables businesses starting or expanding in Opportunity Zones to source additional capital and receive federal tax incentives.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup or expansion in Opportunity Zones
