structured_extraction.program_description: Own Your Future provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy property they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program is funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) and supports property acquisition and renovation for eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans of at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million for purchasing, constructing, or renovating commercial real estate. Loan terms are flexible with options for up to 30 years, senior or subordinate loan positions, and interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. The program focuses on maximizing community benefit. Borrowers must provide a minimum of 1:1 private capital match (one dollar of private funding for every dollar of DHCD loan), provide adequate collateral, maintain total project costs not exceeding $20 million, and provide personal guarantees from all owners with more than 20% equity interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees seeking to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate, including buying the space where you currently operate, moving to a new location, buying property for the first time if you do not have a storefront such as an e-commerce business or food truck, or buying property as part of an expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Minimum 1:1 private capital match required
Loan amount must be at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity
Adequate collateral must be provided
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion
New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion
Business cannot be an adult entertainment facility, check cashing facility, gambling facility, gun shop, liquor store, massage parlor, pawn shop, tanning salon, tattoo parlor, or cannabis business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Applicants can schedule a consultation before applying by contacting DHCD.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households by providing loans for new construction and rehabilitation of rental properties. It typically involves partnerships between State and local governments. The program also allows non-governmental entities to create housing for people with disabilities or special needs integrated within traditional rental housing developments. Rental units must be occupied by households earning below 50% of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct loans for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million without a per unit cap for small projects (defined as 40 units or fewer). Repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rents it to income-eligible households. Failure to comply with income and use restrictions may result in loan acceleration. Any profits from the sale of the project must be used by the borrower for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on ongoing basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities owned in part by a local government or housing authority, non-governmental entities creating housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs, for-profit and non-profit rental housing developers, county governments, and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings and shared housing facilities for developing and preserving affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Statewide.
requirements_list: Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median
Local governments must make a contribution of the land or a contribution of equal value from non-state resources
The local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage the project
Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50 percent of statewide median income adjusted for family size
Residents must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds or neighborhood
Occupants of Partnership Rental Housing Program-assisted units must provide tenant contributed services as detailed in the program statute and regulations
For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, resident households must have gross income not exceeding 30 percent of Area Median Income adjusted for household size
Projects must be evaluated based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications are evaluated and processed based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. If Partnership Rental Housing Program funding is requested with other department funds, the application requirements and applicable deadlines of the other funding must be met. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that activates vacant buildings, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing financial support to place-based economic development organizations working to improve the vitality of Maryland's commercial corridors. Designated Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other place-based economic development organizations in Sustainable Communities receive grants of up to $300,000 to identify priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts and sub-grant the funding to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment to activate vacant spaces.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $300,000 per applicant organization are provided. These funds are sub-granted to businesses for rental assistance (as determined by grantee within grant term), renovation, and equipment/furniture/fixtures costs to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in business districts. Grant funds are disbursed when the Request for Payment is approved, which is before construction/purchasing begins for the project. Grantees may request up to 15% of the grant for operating costs (staff, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0). Grantees cannot use operating funds for indirect costs or organizational overhead unrelated to the program. All grant funds must be expended and businesses must be operational by December 31, 2025. FY2024 had $8.0 million available. All rounds of Project Restore are funded with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds. Businesses receiving sub-granted funds must open and be operational by December 31, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2024 Closed (April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations such as Main Street organizations (designated Main Street Maryland programs), Arts and Entertainment Districts, local governments (town, city, or county), and other place-based economic development organizations located in designated Sustainable Communities. Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but receive funding as sub-grantees through awarded organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting place-based economic development organizations to activate vacant buildings and improve commercial corridors through: sub-grants to businesses for rental assistance, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in local business districts; and organizational operating costs (staff, professional services, marketing, promotion) directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0. Grant funds cannot be used for acquisition/building purchase, new construction, vehicle purchase, operating costs for sub-grantees, infrastructure upgrades, or reimbursement for costs incurred prior to award.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all counties eligible. Priority for organizations and properties located in designated Sustainable Communities. All awarded properties must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community. Each county in the state has a local government eligible to apply. If no place-based economic development organization exists in an area, the local government (town, city, or county) is eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization (e.g., designated Main Street, Arts and Entertainment District) OR a local government entity (town, city, or county)
Must be located in or serving a designated Sustainable Community
All properties for which funding is requested must be in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community at time of application
Must have identified priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts at time of application
Applicant must have at least 0.5 FTE staff at time of application
Applicant must have IRS-determined nonprofit status at time of application (501c3 not specifically required but nonprofit status required)
Property must be vacant at time of application (no executed lease with tenant at application date)
No minimum time in operation required, but applications scored on demonstrated ability to complete similar projects within grant timeline
Each entity can submit only one application
Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly; must apply through awarded place-based organization
Property must be in a commercial corridor or downtown/historic commercial district (street-level retail focus)
Projects in indoor shopping malls, industrial parks, or office parks are ineligible; shopping centers on commercial corridors may be eligible if they improve walkability and street-level retail
Vacant building does not mean entire building must be vacant; individual tenant spaces within a building can be vacant and eligible
Applicants must demonstrate an open and inclusive process for determining sub-grantees that is not limited to organization members

Past Project Restore awardees are eligible with restrictions: cannot fund same property location as previous rounds; if expanding to new location may be eligible; if previous award was recaptured due to non-compliance may be eligible if demonstrating ability to complete; if business was operational then closed may be eligible if demonstrating project sustainability
Sub-grantee (tenant/small business) must sign executed lease specifying property address, lease term, and lease rate before Request for Payment approval
Any legal business in good standing with the state is eligible as sub-grantee, including cannabis businesses and Airbnb businesses (if owned by business/LLC, not private residence)
Landlords may be sub-grantees if lease specifies how Project Restore funds support tenant with rent, fit-out, etc.
Building owner with vacant area for own new business eligible if building and business owned by separate LLCs and building vacant at application
Project budget must show all funding sources and uses; if other funding sources exist, proof (award letter, loan documents, bank statements) must be provided
Must complete Request for Payment, Completion Report (by property), and Final Report with required documentation
Grant term begins when award agreement is signed (expected by June 2024) and ends December 31, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: FY2024 Application Period (CLOSED): The application period for FY2024 closed on April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST. Applications were submitted through Maryland OneStop system. All applications were reviewed after the deadline on a competitive basis. Applications first reviewed for threshold eligibility, then scored by team of DHCD staff members (100 points available based on organizational readiness, equity considerations, project alignment with strategy, and advancement of Project Restore 2.0 goals). Applications with highest scores recommended for funding. Post-Award Process: (1) Award agreement executed (expected by June 2024, must be by September 30 per ARPA rules); (2) Grantee submits Request for Payment (RFP) per property before project costs are incurred - RFP includes property info, sub-grantee business plan, budget with sources/uses, executed lease, and estimated costs. RFPs are approved and funds released before construction/purchasing begins; (3) Grantee submits Completion Report per property once sub-grantee is operational - includes date business opened, Use & Occupancy permit, interior/exterior photos, Maryland Historic Trust determination document, and paid receipts/invoices for Project Restore funded costs (all by December 31, 2025); (4) Grantee submits Final Report within 30 days of grant term end - includes documentation of operating funds spent, narrative on grant impact, feedback on program, and status of all awarded properties. Both RFPs and Completion Reports can be revised. Grantees strongly encouraged to use ACH (direct deposit) for grant payments. Contact Kristin Dawson (DHCD.ProjectRestore@Maryland.gov) for 1:1 support. Interested parties can sign up for DHCD news and alerts for notification if future rounds of the program are offered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Housing Program provides financing to rehabilitate or create affordable multifamily rental housing. The program allocates funds through a competitive process and may be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other public or private funds. It supports the development and preservation of affordable rental housing across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a term of up to 40 years, bearing interest at 2 percent per annum and repayable from cash flow. The maximum loan amount should not exceed $2 million. Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other development-related costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, limited profit, or nonprofit developers, nonprofit organizations, county governments, municipalities, or local housing authorities developing rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Newly constructed or rehabilitated rental housing including congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters and shared living facilities. Projects may be restricted to elderly residents. In some cases, small commercial rehabilitation housing projects may be considered. Funds may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs.

Applications are accepted at designated times during the year and are evaluated against criteria established by the Department. Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by supporting the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The financing is used in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. Projects must be financed through both the DHCD Multifamily Bond Program and the Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program to qualify.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate loans with a maximum of $2.5 million per project, though this limit may be waived in certain circumstances if funds are available and the project is financially feasible in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code. Loans are offered with a 40-year term at 2% simple interest with no regular interest accruing during the construction period. During the permanent loan period, borrowers make surplus cash payments equal to a specified percentage (typically up to 75% of annual cash flow) applied to reduce the outstanding principal balance. Payments are due on April 1 (or other specified date) annually, commencing in the first April following the construction period. Additional contingent interest payments may be owed upon capital events (sale, refinancing, transfer) or at maturity, up to a maximum contingent interest amount. Prepayment without penalty is allowed, though it does not terminate contingent interest obligations or affect occupancy restrictions if prepayment occurs prior to expiration of affordability restrictions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, for-profit businesses, non-profit organizations, county governments, and municipalities involved in creating or preserving affordable rental housing projects that also qualify for the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Funds cannot exceed the amount necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Required zoning for use and density must be in place at time of application with proper documentation (letter from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution)
Award of any necessary competitive public and private sources of funding must have been made prior to application submission
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent jobs must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (an FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all funding awards
Projects must meet threshold and scoring criteria outlined in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
RHW loan amount is subject to an overall maximum of $2.5 million per project unless waived by the Department
Applicant must complete CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funding request
Development or site plan approval is not required at application stage

For prepayment in full, borrower must provide written notice to each tenant, provide notice to CDA and local political subdivision, offer right of first purchase to CDA and other specified parties, provide lease extension for at least one year to assisted unit tenants, make relocation assistance payments as determined by CDA, and provide three-year lease extensions or three months rent-equivalent payments to 20% of qualifying elderly, disabled, or families with minor children tenants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Application Submission Package in conjunction with a Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits application using the Department's standard Application Submission Package. Complete the RHW application checklist and provide: completed CDA Form 202 with RHW funding clearly identified; written documentation of required zoning for use and density from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution; completed FTE Job Calculator estimating full-time equivalent jobs; and certification to RHW Application Submission Package. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed alongside Multifamily Bond Program applications. Projects passing threshold are scored using evaluation criteria in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring is complete. Projects must proceed according to agreed-upon timelines and are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis. The Department processes applications through the multifamily pipeline on a first-ready-to-proceed basis with estimated closing dates projected in the annual funding status report.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides 100% grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to cover costs associated with preparing federal funding applications for broadband projects. The Office of Statewide Broadband will offer assistance in preparing and reviewing federal funding applications to ensure applications are complete and competitive, and will coordinate with other State Agencies on the use of State assets where they will feasibly benefit the project. Eligible expenses include market studies, engineering, legal, financial, and other approved services from outside consultants needed to prepare federal funding applications.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The OSB will reimburse for properly contracted services required for the federal funding application, such as engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other costs that may be considered on a case-by-case basis. A maximum funding amount of $125,000 will be provided to the applicant for these costs. Costs will only be considered for projects that submit a completed application for the federal funding program and that meet the terms and conditions of the federal funding program. Partnerships are offered on a rolling basis depending on the federal funding opportunity and available state funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No application window; partnerships offered on a rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding. Interested applicants should contact the office to discuss.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners seeking to develop broadband expansion projects that serve unserved rural residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with preparing federal funding applications, including engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other properly contracted consulting services. Maximum reimbursement of $125,000 per project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must target unserved areas as defined by the federal funding program or, if the federal program does not define unserved areas, areas without internet service at 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up. Projects must comply with federal program requirements regarding areas that have not received other federal investments.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction or internet service provider partner of a local jurisdiction
Project must be for broadband service to unserved rural residents and businesses
Project must target areas meeting federal program definition of unserved areas (or 25 Mbps down/3 Mbps up minimum if federal program does not define unserved)

Applicant must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (or comply with more restrictive federal program requirements)
Project must submit a completed application for the federal funding program
Project must meet the terms and conditions of the federal funding program
Costs must be for properly contracted services from outside consultants
Applicant must complete the Grant Application Form and submit responses to all RFP requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one electronic copy of RFP response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in subject line. Response must include: cover letter with local jurisdiction and partner contact information, completed and signed Grant Application Form, business model summary, statement of team experience, network design and construction description, customer profile description, and proposed implementation schedule. Questions should be submitted in writing to OSB.MD@maryland.gov. OSB will evaluate responses to guide determination of partnerships and funding allocations. Evaluation is based on qualifications, evaluation of submittals, and possible interview. No reimbursement is made by OSB for costs incurred in responding to the RFP. Partnerships are offered on a rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program exclusively for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to access capital for relending to small businesses. The program focuses on businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses, and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas. CDFIs receive loans that they then relend to eligible small businesses, with a required private capital match. The program is part of the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD issues loans (SSBCI Loans) to CDFIs at interest rates as low as 0%-2% with loan terms up to 7 years with annual renewal options thereafter. SSBCI Loans can range from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 and must be matched with private capital at a minimum 1:1 ratio. Initial proposal structures each small business loan (SBL) with 20% SSBCI funds and 80% private match capital for non-SEDI and non-VSB businesses, and 30% SSBCI funds and 70% private match capital for SEDI and VSB businesses. CDFIs then relend these funds to small businesses in loans up to $250,000 (unless prior written approval is given), at interest rates not exceeding 18%, with terms up to 5 years. Small business borrowers pay combined origination fees and points not to exceed 1%, with application fees capped at $100. Risk of loss on each SBL is shared between DHCD and Lender on a loan-by-loan basis with the SSBCI-funded portion in a top loss position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications; funding subject to SSBCI fund availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) with demonstrated financial stability, experience in small business lending, access to private capital match, and commitment to serving very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees), socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led businesses, and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDFIs use funds to relend to small businesses for: working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payment, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential/transient living businesses, multifamily/single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Eligible small business locations include retail businesses, manufacturing businesses, goods and services related businesses, home-based businesses, and non-profit organizations, with priority given to those in CDFI Investment Areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) certified with the CDFI Fund
Must demonstrate financial stability and good standing with the State and Internal Revenue Service

Must have experience in administering small business loan programs including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management, and compliance with reporting requirements
Must demonstrate ability to leverage eligible required private capital as match to SSBCI funding (minimum 1:1 ratio)
Must have capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations, and Policies and DHCD requirements
Must demonstrate readiness to begin making SBLs within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan
Must have ability to provide technical assistance to SBL Borrowers
Must have outreach capabilities to very small businesses and socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led businesses or businesses in CDFI Investment Areas
Must provide financial documentation including most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) organizational documents, and last 3 years of organizational tax returns
Must certify no outstanding liabilities with Maryland (income taxes, sales taxes, payroll withholding taxes, unemployment taxes, or other penalties and fines)
Combined origination fee and points for SBLs cannot exceed 1%
Application fee to borrowers capped at $100 maximum
No prepayment penalties allowed on SBLs
Small business loans cannot exceed $250,000 unless DHCD gives prior written approval
Interest rates on SBLs cannot exceed 18%
Must maintain separation: Lender cannot act as participant, have security interest, or be stakeholder in SBL Borrowers
Must meet federal SSBCI requirements including minimum 20% lender capital at risk and SSBCI funding only for small businesses with fewer than 500 employees
Total financing per transaction cannot exceed $20,000,000
Must allocate 34.46% of SSBCI funds for very small businesses and SEDI businesses combined to meet Treasury incentive fund targets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs interested in participating should submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application (Appendix A) to DHCD. The application should include: organization information and CDFI certification details; explanation of capacity and experience in small business lending with 6-year projected loan production; explanation of leverage strategy with private capital terms and conditions; verification of financial stability and resources; details on lending program including demographic, geographic, and industry targets; description of outreach to very small businesses and SEDI-led businesses; loan product details including size, interest rates, terms, and fees; capabilities for reporting and audit activity; explanation of technical assistance and training resources; and confirmation of no outstanding state liabilities. Applicants must attach organizational documents including Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) documents, and last 3 years of tax returns. Upon approval, the CDFI receives a commitment letter from DHCD specifying the SSBCI Loan amount, required private capital match, and proposed SBL funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with documentation provided by the Maryland Office of the Attorney General. The Lender is then responsible for origination, credit and compliance underwriting, closing, servicing, and asset management of all SBLs. Monthly, quarterly, and annual reports must be submitted to DHCD in Treasury's reporting format. Quarterly reports are due 30 days after every quarter, and annual reports are due by February 28 to allow consolidation for Treasury submission by March 31.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. The program provides bridge financing — in the form of venture debt or convertible notes — to help companies that have already raised equity from early-stage investors reach their next equity raise and scale their operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Venture debt or convertible notes ranging from $500,000 to $2,500,000 per company, for aggregate funding rounds under $20,000,000. Typical bridge rounds are over $2,000,000. SSBCI funds must be on at least a pari passu basis (equal footing) with private capital match, and must cause and result in the private capital match. Repayment in principal and interest or convertible note terms available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking bridge financing to achieve milestones and reach their next equity raise. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own and operate businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to help early-stage businesses achieve milestones and reach their next equity raise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fewer than 500 employees
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing Paid-In-Capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
Companies typically positioned to scale and bridge financing needed to achieve milestones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov to inquire and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan Participation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan participation program that helps small businesses acquire or expand their owner-occupied real estate or working capital needs. The program offers below-market interest rates and can lend up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. Priority is given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or Junior Debt ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000. The SSBCI portion covers up to 30% of the total loan. Interest rates are based on underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms available up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. A prepayment lockout period may apply. Private capital match required: 4:1 target (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB businesses or 2.3:1 target (70-30) for SEDI/VSB, with minimum 1:1 match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses in the same building, machinery and equipment, working capital, and certain other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fewer than 500 employees
Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area
Must be Maryland-based
Local governments are not eligible
Proof of private capital match: 4:1 target for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 target for SEDI/VSB with minimum 1:1 match
Business viability and potential impact on the neighborhood
Readiness to proceed
Acceptable cash flow and collateral
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package and submit through the online application system at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Upon loan approval, applicants receive a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires that applicants meet underwriting guidelines. Applicants must have executed necessary legal documents prior to disbursement of loan proceeds. Application fee is $250 and closing fee is $250.

structured_extraction.program_description: This federally funded program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. Adults with disabilities between 18 and 61 years old who receive Medicaid and have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income are eligible. The program is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health, and helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Section 811 provides project-based rental assistance that subsidizes the contract rent of eligible participants with disabilities. Funds are awarded to eligible rental projects that receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds. Eligible properties receive assistance to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities. The program does not provide loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing projects (for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments) and low-income adults with disabilities aged 18 to 61 who receive Medicaid and have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants with disabilities in approved rental housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. The program is available statewide. Funding has been distributed to support units in Baltimore, Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Areas, the Eastern Shore, and Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be adults aged 18 to 61
Applicants must have a qualifying disability and receive Medicaid
Applicants must have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Applicants must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
Housing must be a rental property
Housing must receive financing from DHCD
Housing must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee including representatives from the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to review and select projects that align with program goals. Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming the property is eligible for funding to support unit subsidies. Eligible residents are referred by MDOD and selected according to tenant selection plans.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions (colleges, universities, hospitals, and cultural organizations) for community development projects that generate jobs, strengthen partnerships between institutions and the state, and create safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Projects are anchored by institutions that serve as catalysts for neighborhood revitalization, including adaptive reuse of vacant schools and other buildings for community centers, health care facilities, day care facilities, and other community amenities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans for capital improvement projects. Anchor institutions must provide matching funds equal to 100 percent of the financial assistance received from the fund (1:1 match requirement). Capital funding may be used for adaptive reuse of vacant buildings and other community development capital projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period closed July 2, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions defined as institutions of higher education in Maryland or hospital institutions in Maryland with organized medical staff, diagnostic and treatment facilities, and overnight care capacity. Also includes Maryland hospital and higher education institution departments, foundations, and other related entities. Nonprofit organizations seeking to catalyze neighborhood revitalization through community development are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects at anchor institutions in eligible geographic areas, including adaptive reuse of vacant schools and other buildings for community centers, health care facilities, day care facilities, and other community amenities. Projects must generate jobs, strengthen community partnerships, and lead to safer, healthier, and more attractive communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible anchor institution
Project must be located in a Sustainable Community or underinvested area of the state
Applicant must provide matching funds equal to 100 percent of the assistance amount requested
Project must be anchored by an anchor institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through Project Portal after registering as a new user. Registration must be completed by June 11, 2025. For additional application instructions and information, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to nonprofits and local governments to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters, including supportive services for residents experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. The program provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Eligible uses include acquiring land and buildings, site preparation, labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation, acquisition of necessary machinery and equipment installed at the project (including HVAC systems and household furnishings), architectural and engineering services, and fees and premiums for real estate development including bonds, insurance, and other costs acceptable to the Department. Grant funds may cover up to one-half of total project costs generally, or up to 75 percent under certain conditions. Recipients must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or the grant becomes repayable. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, financing building portions that do not provide homeless housing, financial transaction costs, replacing furnishings in existing facilities, and providing operating assistance. Equipment and furnishings must have a life expectancy of at least 15 years, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, and not be elaborate or extravagant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments seeking to create or improve transitional housing and emergency shelters for homeless individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Funds may be used for acquiring land and buildings, necessary studies and surveys, site preparation, labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation, acquisition of machinery and equipment installed at the project, and fees and premiums for real estate development. Funds may not be used for refinancing existing debt, financing non-housing portions of buildings, financial transaction costs, replacing furnishings in existing facilities, or providing operating assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All projects involving any new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City with some exceptions), all areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits and the Washington DC beltway and boundary, all Sustainable Communities areas, Federal and State enterprise zones, areas designated by county governments as PFAs including rural villages designated in county comprehensive plans, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Local government letters of support are required for all projects, and applications for new construction projects must include a letter from local government certifying the project is located in a PFA.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Project must provide transitional housing or emergency shelter with supportive services
Residents must be homeless households and individuals (defined as households without permanent housing and lacking resources to obtain permanent housing and in imminent danger of homelessness)
Recipient must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years
Local government letter of support required for all projects
Grant funds may not exceed one-half of total project costs generally, or 75 percent under certain conditions
Applicants must identify the homeless target population they expect to serve and continue serving throughout the 15-year funding term
Supportive services must be specifically oriented to meeting the needs of the homeless target population and service providers must be identified
Applicants must submit copies of commitment letters, agreements or documents identifying sources of funding for services and a plan outlining funding sources for services and operating expenses
Eligible projects include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family detached homes, single room occupancy facilities and group or shared housing
Projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation are subject to thorough review of construction-related items by Department's Construction Management staff
All applications for new construction projects must include a letter from local government certifying the project is located in a Priority Funding Area
Nonprofit organizations receiving Low-Income Housing Tax Credits must be the sole managing general partner responsible for project management

Compliance with State policies including Minority Business Requirements (29% MBE goal), LEED building encouragement, Maryland Historical Trust requirements, 20-year roof warranties, prohibition on religious purposes funding, forest conservation requirements, and debarred business requirements
Maryland Historical Trust must complete review before funds are disbursed

Equipment and furnishings must have a life expectancy of at least 15 years, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, be heavy enough to prevent easy removal, not be intended to replace adequate items already on hand, be necessary to accommodate intended functions, and not be elaborate or extravagant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office at the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for application instructions and deadlines. The application must include identification of the homeless target population to be served, description of supportive services, evidence of local government support via letter, certification of Priority Funding Area location for new construction projects, and documentation of funding sources for services and operating expenses. Applications undergo threshold requirements review for acceptance and are subject to underwriting and construction review processes. Viability review and commitment review are conducted as part of the evaluation process. The Department may enlist assistance from the Maryland Department of Human Resources' Office of Transitional Services or the Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality for review of proposed supportive services. The Department will consider applicant's experience operating facilities for the homeless, previous success in providing services, and ability to secure funding for services. Processing time and specific deadlines should be obtained by contacting the Department directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides loans to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or minimum housing quality standards. The Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program helps homeowners address critical health and safety issues in owner-occupied single-family homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent to six percent interest loans based on applicant's ability to pay. Loans are fully deferred for families with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Maximum loan is generally $50,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans are processed directly by local governments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household incomes at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Priority consideration for families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs to owner-occupied single-family homes including: mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair, chimney repair, foundation and waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well systems, septic and sewer systems, windows and doors for health/safety or water intrusion, structural repair, accessibility modifications, fall prevention measures, pest treatments, and incipient failure of critical infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, or Montgomery County. Available in other Maryland jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Owner must occupy the single-family home as primary residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (50 percent for fully deferred loans)
Property must be a single-family home, duplex, townhome, condo, or manufactured home
Repairs must address critical health and safety issues or bring property to code compliance
Maximum loan request is $50,000
Property must have homeowners insurance
Applicants must provide bids from licensed and insured Maryland contractors or trade professionals
Bids should not be more than 60 days old
Applicants must meet eligibility criteria set by local governments processing the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application and submit it with required documentation including: proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill), homeowners insurance declaration page, income verification documents (recent paystubs, tax returns, or award letters), personal identification, and contractor bids with photos documenting critical repairs. Contractor must provide current MHIC or trade license, certificate of liability insurance (minimum $1 million per occurrence), letter of good standing, and completed W-9 form. Applications can be submitted by email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loan requests are processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides funding to accelerate economic development and job production in existing Maryland communities by supporting grey field development projects that face more barriers than sprawling development. The fund focuses on demolition of vacant and underutilized structures and supports projects with high economic and revitalization impact as part of community revitalization efforts statewide. It helps make development on previously used land more financially possible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants (and loans) to fund demolition of derelict non-contributing structures and vacant/underutilized buildings, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels for solicitation or planned development, site development, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed (application period closed July 2, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City on projects in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones; communities and organizations seeking to remove vacant and underutilized structures.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: demolishing old/derelict non-contributing structures and vacant/underutilized buildings; buying and combining land for new development (site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels); site development; and creating construction-level architectural and engineering plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City or Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Applicants must use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Lead applicants must be local governments or nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City
Projects must be located in eligible geographic areas
Project must be located in a Sustainable Community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the Project Portal after registering as a new user. Registration must be completed by June 11, 2025. Application period closed July 2, 2025. For more information and application instructions, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designation program that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation and housing and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that qualifies communities for access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives. Communities receive the Sustainable Community designation for five years, which allows them to access state revitalization funding and programs including: Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership, commercial revitalization); Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap financing for small businesses and nonprofits); Strategic Demolition Fund (grants for demolition and land assembly); Operating Assistance Grants (grants for operating and technical assistance costs); National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (financing for grey field development); Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants and loans for anchor institutions); Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance and training); Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (additional place-based revitalization investment); Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements); Job Creation Tax Credit (enhanced credits up to $5,000 per job with lower job creation threshold of 25 jobs); Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing Authority (expanded eligible uses); Low Income Housing Tax Credit (additional points for LIHTC applications); Water Quality Financing Administration Programs (below-market loans and grants); State Highway Administration Programs (preference for transportation projects); Sidewalk Retrofit Program (sidewalk construction funding with preference for Sustainable Communities); Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program (additional points for bicycle access projects); and Sustainable Maryland Certified program (20 points toward certification). The designation itself does not provide direct financial assistance but unlocks eligibility for other state funding programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to designate specific geographic areas for revitalization and sustainability efforts. Community development organizations and anchor institutions may also benefit from related programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Once designated, the Sustainable Community designation qualifies communities to apply for certain state programs that support historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, streetscape improvements, commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, demolition and land assembly, water quality and environmental projects, and other revitalization initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All proposed Sustainable Communities areas must be located within a Priority Funding Area and show a targeted approach. The area should be within or near a town center or transportation center. Communities must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization. Some programs have additional geographic preferences (e.g., National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund focuses on areas between the District of Columbia and Interstate 495; Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative serves inner beltway Sustainable Communities within and surrounding Baltimore City).
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Must be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization
Must have a defined geographic area with existing built environment
Must have a Sustainable Community Action Plan that is consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
Must have a local government resolution supporting both the boundary designation and Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request an application template by emailing Tynan Stevenson with details about the inquiry. For new designations, a meeting with program staff is required. 2. Submit an application including a defined geographic area, a Sustainable Community Action Plan, and a local government resolution. 3. An interagency panel reviews the application. 4. The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 5. Once approved, the designation is valid for five years.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT is a public-private partnership program designed to increase homeownership opportunities and property values in historically redlined and underserved communities by closing the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to develop or renovate a property and its market sale price. The program provides funding to cover this gap, enabling qualified nonprofit and for-profit development teams to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted low-income neighborhoods. It aims to increase property values, create homeownership opportunities, and build wealth for families in historically disinvested areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: UPLIFT provides funding to qualified development teams to cover the appraisal gap—the difference between the total cost to develop a property and the price it can sell for on the market. The State covers this gap through a combination of public and private financing, structured as both grant and loan components. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loan (via Maryland Mortgage Program or other source), other acceptable subsidy support, and a soft promissory note with the Department. Developer loans are made during construction, with repayment upon approved sales. Loan terms vary based on location (ENOUGH Act Grantees and Just Communities areas may have modified terms). The program charges a one-time non-refundable application fee of $1,000 per project. Additional fees may include origination and closing fees as projects progress.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders working with local jurisdictions and community-based organizations to develop affordable housing in historically redlined and low-income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to cover the difference between the cost to construct or renovate quality affordable housing and the price the property can sell for on the market. This enables development teams to build or rehabilitate homes in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities affected by historic redlining and disinvestment. Projects may use funds for acquisition, construction, professional fees, developer fees, neighborhood engagement, marketing and sales activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in low-income census tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% of AMI or have poverty rate of 25% or more) and designated Sustainable Communities. Applicants should refer to the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map for eligible locations. New construction projects are not to be located in FEMA Flood Zone A or AE areas. Projects in Zone C may submit waiver requests with engineer documentation. Projects in Zone X require waiver requests with flood mitigation plans or engineering risk documentation.
requirements_list: Project must be located in qualified low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities
Development team must consist of qualified nonprofit or for-profit developers and builders with minimum comparable project experience
Projects must align with UPLIFT design and construction standards for quality, safety, and environmental performance
Applicants must complete pre-application meeting process before formal application submission
Non-refundable $1,000 application fee per project required
Both electronic (via Dropbox) and hard copy application submissions required
Project must consist of newly constructed or formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated
Development team must demonstrate acceptable financial capacity and credit history
Neighborhood engagement and community coordination required
Site must have proper control (ownership, option, or land contract)
All environmental assessments must be current (typically less than 12 months old)

Projects must meet all threshold criteria including project location, development team requirements, development costs, neighborhood engagement, quality thresholds, marketing/sales plan, and financing commitments
Homebuyer affirmative fair housing marketing required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review the UPLIFT Program Guide and schedule a Pre-Application Meeting by submitting the Pre-Application Meeting Request Form at least two business days in advance. Step 1: After the pre-application meeting, submit the Electronic Application Submission Request Form to receive a private Dropbox link. Step 2: Download the Application Documents Package from the UPLIFT website, complete all sections using the Detailed Application Instructions, and prepare two complete copies (one electronic via Dropbox, one hard copy). Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable application fee by ACH transfer or check and upload proof of payment. Step 4: Upload all application files to the Dropbox in correct subfolders, sign and upload the Final Submission Checklist, and deliver the hard copy to DHCD's Operations & Administration Office at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Step 5: DHCD reviews applications for Threshold Criteria compliance and scores eligible projects against Evaluative Criteria covering: Development Team Capacity, Project Impact, Leveraging and Cost Effectiveness, Readiness to Proceed, and Development Quality. Step 6: The UPLIFT Loan Committee makes a recommendation to the Secretary for resource approval. Step 7: Approved applicants receive a Commitment Letter. Step 8: Projects entering underwriting pipeline undergo Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) process, typically with Project Kick-off Meeting held 45-60 days after complete application submission. Step 9: Following underwriting approval, initial financing closing occurs with Secretary determination and Attorney General review. Step 10: Shortly after closing, Construction Kick-off Meeting coordinates construction phase, marketing, and occupancy requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by the American Rescue Plan Act that provides stabilization funding to eligible child care providers to help keep their doors open and support early childhood educators. The program addresses the hardships faced by child care providers and instability in the child care market caused by COVID-19, supporting operational stability and continuity of care during the pandemic recovery period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a base award of $10,000 plus additional per-slot funding of $126 for licensed child care slots serving infants, toddlers, or children in the Child Care Scholarship program, as well as additional funding for providers participating in Maryland EXCELS (rating 1-5) and providers located in census tracts with a Social Vulnerability Index greater than 0.6. Any unutilized funds from non-participating providers are distributed evenly to grant-awarded providers per licensed slot. Funding does not need to be repaid if recipients meet all required certifications. Eligible expenses include: personnel costs (owner and employee pay, benefits, premium pay, bonuses, vaccine-related costs, professional development); facility costs (mortgage, rent, utilities, phone, internet, maintenance, COVID-related facility improvements); PPE and cleaning supplies (masks, gloves, hand sanitizer, disinfecting materials, cleaning services, health and safety training); equipment and supplies (accounting software, payroll software, health monitoring equipment, computers and devices); goods and services (food, diapers, toys, books, craft materials, licensing fees); behavioral health supports; and past expenses incurred during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 23, 2022 by 6:00pm (EST) CLOSED
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible child care providers including family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs under a Letter of Compliance operating in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: personnel costs including owner and employee wages, benefits, premium pay, bonuses, and vaccine-related costs; rent or mortgage payments, utilities, phone and internet, facilities maintenance and improvements, or insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, or training related to health and safety; equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19 including accounting and payroll software, health monitoring equipment, and computers or devices for remote communication or distance learning support; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services including food, diapers, toys, books, craft materials, and licensing fees; behavioral health supports for children and employees; and past expenses incurred during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an operating child care provider (family child care home, large family child care home, child care center, or education program under a Letter of Compliance)
Must meet one criteria from each eligibility column as specified in the program eligibility chart
Must have been licensed as a child care provider in Maryland
Must comply with all required certifications throughout the grant term
Head Start and Early Head Start programs are not eligible
Providers who own or operate more than one child care location must submit separate applications for each site
Must implement policies in line with Maryland guidance and CDC guidance to the greatest extent possible when open and providing services

Must maintain at least the same weekly wages and benefits for all employees (including lead teachers, aides, and staff in transportation and food preparation) from the date of application submission through the duration of the grant period
Must not furlough employees from the date of application submission through the duration of the grant period
Must provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing relief for families struggling to make payments
Must keep and maintain all required documentation including health and safety protocols, employee payment and benefit records, hours worked records, and records of tuition relief provided to families
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted online only through a survey link. Providers cannot submit scanned copies, faxes, or written applications. Applicants can access the application via computer or mobile device. The MSDE provides virtual customer service support sessions including documentation needed webinars, application form walkthroughs, and Q&A sessions. All session recordings are posted on the website. Providers with questions can contact MSDE staff via email or inquiry form, with responses provided within 24 hours or the next business day. Applicants should use the provided expense tracking tool to organize and document all expenses by category (personnel, facility costs, PPE and cleaning, equipment and supplies, goods and services, mental health services, and past expenses) to support their application and grant management.
