structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course required by state and federal law for all child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program. The training covers health, safety, and nutrition topics required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant regulations, as well as recommended best practices related to health and safety in child care settings and connects to Maryland regulations for child care. Participants must complete four modules, pass with a minimum score of 80%, and receive a certificate of completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training consisting of four modules (Introduction to Basic Health and Safety, plus three additional topic modules) covering health, safety, and nutrition. Training is hosted on Canvas at https://msde.instructure.com. Training takes approximately three hours to complete. Participants must score at least 80% on all topic reviews and a final review and survey to receive a certificate of completion. Participants are allowed up to two attempts to achieve the passing score on the Final Assessment. The training is offered in monthly cohorts with recurring registration and course dates. Training must be completed within a 21-day course window. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance. Modules must be completed in sequential order (Introduction first), after which other topics become available and may be completed in any order.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens one week per month. May cohort registration closes April 23 at 12:00 pm, training completed by May 22; June cohort registration closes May 23 at 12:00 pm, training completed by June 22. Ongoing monthly cohorts. Check the Basic Health and Safety Training web page for current registration dates. New employees must complete within 90 days of hire. Annual updates must be completed by December 31 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program in Maryland. This includes newly approved family child care providers and newly hired staff. Newly hired staff have 90 days from hire date to complete. Child care staff and family providers must complete annual updates.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a training program, not a financial assistance program. The training covers health and safety topics required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant to maintain compliance with state and federal regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Training is available online through the Canvas learning management system at https://msde.instructure.com. Face-to-face training is also available through approved trainers throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program
Must have a valid email address to register (one name per email address only)
Must have basic technical skills including mouse use, typing, email, viewing videos, internet navigation, and printing
Must complete the Introduction module first; other modules become available upon completion
Must complete all remaining modules in any order within the course period
Must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the final review and survey to receive a certificate
Must complete the final review and survey in one sitting without exiting
Must print certificate of completion prior to course end date; MSDE does not retain or send copies
Allowed maximum of two attempts to pass the Final Assessment; grade at end of course is final
Must complete the training within the 21-day course window; accounts expire at end of course period
Child care staff and family providers must complete the annual update by December 31 each year (or by December 31, 2025 for staff employed before October 2025)

Newly hired staff or approved family child care providers hired October through December must complete training by March 31 of the following year (e.g., by March 31, 2026 for newly hired or approved staff)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register during the one-week monthly registration window by completing the online registration form at the Basic Health and Safety Training web page with a valid email address. 2. Upon successful registration, receive login instructions via email to the registered email address. Check spam/junk folders if not received. 3. Log into the course platform at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas using the registered email address as username and the password you created. 4. Select and complete the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module first (other modules are locked until completion). 5. Exit the course properly using the EXIT COURSE button in the upper right corner to save progress. System remembers where you left off. 6. After completing the Introduction, other topic modules become available and may be completed in any order at your own pace (does not need to be completed in one sitting). 7. Once all topic modules are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. 8. Complete the Final Review and Survey in one sitting without exiting. 9. Submit the final assessment to receive an immediate score. 10. If score is 80% or higher, a Certificate of Completion immediately appears in the Modules section and the Save and Print Your Certificate module unlocks. 11. Print and save the certificate before the course end date (MSDE does not retain copies). If below 80%, retake the Final Assessment up to one additional time (two attempts total) while the course is open. After two attempts, you cannot register for the same cohort again; you must register for a future cohort if you have not completed any course sections in the previous cohort.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to eligible students who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and want to attend a participating nonpublic school. Priority is given to students who received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year and their siblings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided to cover tuition costs at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts depend on household income, academic level of the student, and any financial assistance the school provides. The award is paid by check sent to the school, which the parent or guardian must sign. The scholarship award is reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. Around 2,500 scholarship awards are estimated to be distributed from approximately $9,000,000 in available funding for the 2026-2027 school year. Awards are made by the BOOST Advisory Board based on ranking of eligible students by household income as a percentage of federal poverty levels. The scholarship is for tuition and required fees only; funds may not be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 9 - May 8, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who qualify for free and reduced-price school meals (FARMS) and are entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees at participating nonpublic schools. Funds may not be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland for nonpublic schools registered to operate in the state. Participating nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education, be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program, and provide more than only prekindergarten and kindergarten programs.
requirements_list: Qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMS) based on household income compared to federal poverty guidelines
Be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade for the 2026-2027 school year (Pre-K students not eligible)
Upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size
Provide child's full name as it appears on birth certificate
Indicate whether child received a BOOST scholarship in previous year or is sibling of previous recipient
Indicate whether child has learning disability and receives special education services (to be confirmed by school)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable portal. Application period opens March 9, 2026 and closes May 8, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT. As part of the application, parents upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns and provide household information. The BOOST program uses FARMS income guidelines established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture each year. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis but are not awarded on a first-come, first-serve basis. After May 30, 2026, all application data is collected and shared with the BOOST Advisory Board. The BOOST Advisory Board meets in Summer 2026 (June/July) to determine award amounts based on available funding and priority rankings. Students are ranked by household income as a percentage of federal poverty levels according to priority tiers: (1st) Renewals and their siblings; (2nd) New applicants from public schools qualifying for free meals; (3rd) New applicants from public schools qualifying for reduced meals; (4th) Existing nonpublic school students qualifying for free meals; (5th) Existing nonpublic school students qualifying for reduced meals. Parents receive award notification via email in August 2026 and must accept or decline by deadline. Participating schools must confirm student enrollment and, for special education students, upload IEP, IFSP or 504 Plan. Scholarship checks are printed and mailed via FedEx to schools between September-December 2026. No new awards will be offered after December 11, 2026. MSDE holds customer service support sessions on: Tuesday, March 10, 2026 at 12:00-1:00 p.m.; Thursday, March 12, 2026 at 12:00-1:00 p.m. (with certified interpreter); and weekly Wednesdays March 18 through May 6 at 12:00-1:00 p.m. (with certified interpreter available).

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance (scholarship) program that helps child care providers and staff participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program earn a college degree in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education at participating accredited colleges and universities in Maryland. Funding is paid directly to the college or university on behalf of approved applicants rather than reimbursing participants. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis for first-time applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance/scholarship funding for college education paid directly to the accredited institution on an annual basis. Funding covers associate or bachelor's degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at participating Maryland colleges and universities. Awards cover tuition, fees, and required textbooks only; funds cannot be used for costs previously incurred. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis for first-time applicants, with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit. Continuation funding is available if funds remain available and recipients maintain a 2.50 GPA. Recipients must reapply annually with updated documentation of employment and credential participation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications due by March 1st each year; Continuation and Transfer applications due by June 30th each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff who work in licensed child care centers or are registered family child care providers in Maryland, enrolled in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher, with at least one year of experience working with groups of children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at accredited Maryland colleges and universities. Funds can only be used toward the completion of a college degree in an approved field and cannot be used to pay fees or costs, including tuition, previously incurred for college enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to child care providers working in Maryland at licensed child care centers or as registered family child care providers. Degree must be pursued at a participating accredited Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Must participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher
Must be a child care provider or staff member working in a licensed child care center or as a registered family child care provider in Maryland and work at least 10 hours per week
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of your choice
Must pursue a degree from an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Eligible degree fields: Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
Maintain employment in child care in Maryland while participating in the program
Participate in professional development
Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative grade point average from the point of first entering the program

Agree to complete the child care service requirement in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week after completion of the degree: 2 years for associate degree, 4 years for bachelor's degree, 2.5 years for master's degree
If withdrawing from the fund without good cause, must repay the State of Maryland the amount paid on their behalf for college tuition, fees, and textbooks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Be accepted to a participating college or university offering a degree in an eligible field. Contact the CCCPDF Coordinator at the participating college of your choice using the list of Participating Colleges. Step 2: Once accepted into the college, meet with the CCCPDF Coordinator at the college who must review and sign the application checklist before submission to MSDE. Step 3: Submit a completed CCCPDF application with all required documentation to the Office of Child Care by the deadline. Required documentation includes: completed and signed application; proof of at least one year of child care experience with signed letter from current and previous employers on letterhead (or current Family Child Care license); copy of current Maryland Child Care Credential certificate (Level Two or higher); letter of acceptance or documentation from a CCCPDF participating college/university including declared major; and professional development plan with courses and timeline to complete degree. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. MSDE will notify applicants of whether they have received fund approval. Continuation applications require updated employment letter, current credential certificate, current college transcript, and revised professional development plan if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports child care providers in improving the professionalism and quality of their care services and children's school readiness. It awards grant funds to incentivize child care providers to enhance the quality of care, and helps them acquire supplies, materials, equipment, and training to create stimulating learning environments aligned with early learning standards and Kindergarten Readiness guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded as an incentive for child care providers to enhance quality. Funds can be used to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments and implement knowledge gained through professional training and education. Grant amounts are based on the number of children in care: up to $1,000 for facilities with fewer than 10 children, up to $1,500 for facilities with up to 29 children, and up to $2,500 for facilities with more than 30 children. Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October. Providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted quarterly; grants awarded in January, April, July, and October. Check after December 1, 2022 for updated FY23 information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care homes in Maryland committed to improving quality and children's school readiness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments, implement knowledge gained through professional training and education, and improve or enhance the quality of care for children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must possess a current license or letter of compliance
Must currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Must implement a curriculum that aligns with the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines
Each child care facility must submit a separate application if providers operate or own multiple sites
Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Social Security Number (SSN) identification must be provided per site to qualify for multiple awards
All statements on the application must be completed; when a statement does not apply, applicants must answer Yes, No, or Does Not Apply (N/A)
Applicants must itemize all proposed purchases with individual costs and descriptions of how each item will improve or enhance care quality
Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years
Additional requirements vary by whether applicant is a child care center or family child care home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete a grant application form and submit it to the Credentialing Branch. The application must include responses to every statement, itemized lists of all proposed purchases with costs, and descriptions of how each item will improve or enhance care quality. Applicants will be notified in writing whether their application has been approved or disapproved. Application details and the revised Grant Information Guide are announced through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program helps eligible low-income families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. The program provides payment scholarships that cover part of child care costs at participating licensed child care centers, registered family homes, and informal care providers (relative or non-relative care in the child's home). Families receive a temporary 60-day scholarship while their full application is processed; if fully eligible, they may receive a 52-week scholarship. As of May 1, 2025, the program implemented a temporary enrollment freeze for new families due to funding capacity. Applications continue to be accepted and processed, and approved applicants are placed on a Frozen Status List (waitlist) to receive scholarships when funding becomes available. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the freeze. Currently enrolled families continue to receive benefits without interruption if they meet eligibility requirements and complete recertification on time. The program is managed through a centralized vendor called CCS Central 2.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state pays a scholarship amount toward the cost of child care at a participating provider. Families pay a state-assigned co-payment (the amount the family pays), with the scholarship rate covering the remaining portion. Co-payments are based on the unit of care and range from $0 to $3 per week per scholarship. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) pay a $0 co-payment. Co-payments also vary based on other factors: families receiving SNAP, housing assistance, WIC, WAG, GBI, or with children in Head Start or State-funded Pre-K may be eligible for $0 co-payment with proof. Multiple children enrolled result in reduced co-payments ($3 per week per 3-unit scholarship, $2 per week per 2-unit scholarship, $1 per week per 1-unit scholarship). Three scholarship types are available: (1) temporary 60-day scholarships for registered family homes or licensed child care centers issued upon fast-track approval; (2) full 52-week formal scholarships for the same providers upon complete eligibility verification; and (3) informal scholarships for relative care or non-relative care in the child's home. Child care providers receive advance payments from the state based on enrolled children twice per month (on the 15th and 30th of each month; payment dates visible in General Accounting Division are two semi-monthly payments with true-up reconciliation occurring monthly). Payment continues through up to 60 days of child absences per calendar year. During the enrollment freeze (effective May 1, 2025), newly approved families are placed on a Frozen Status List and receive scholarships when funding becomes available. The application process can take up to 30 calendar days with incomplete documentation or up to 5 business days after all required documentation is received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis; as of May 1, 2025, a temporary enrollment freeze is in effect for new families (approved applicants are waitlisted). Fast-Track applications will not be processed during the freeze; full applications must be submitted to be determined eligible for the Frozen Status List.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-877-227-0125 (Office Hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 am–5:00 pm); 1-855-435-7410 (After Hours: Tuesday–Thursday 5:00 pm–9:00 pm, Saturday 9:00 am–12:00 pm)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible low-income Maryland families with children younger than 13 (or ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability) who are employed, in an approved training program, or attending school. Also serves licensed child care centers, registered family homes, and informal child care providers participating in the program. Families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care and early education at Maryland registered family homes, licensed child care centers, and informal child care by relatives or non-relatives in the child's home, including before and after school child care and extended hours care (evenings, weekends, or summer).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland (all counties).
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
Be employed, in an approved training program, or attending school (both parents in same household must meet all requirements)

Be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), OR have family income below the CCS income guidelines (based on family size and income scale; initial income scale for new applications and continuation income scale for redeterminations)

Child must be younger than 13 years old, or age 13–19 with a qualifying disability (a child who has been diagnosed as being physically or mentally incapable of self-care appropriate to the age of the child, as verified by the State based on determination by a physician, licensed or certified psychologist, or licensed social worker)
Child must be immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation supporting immunization exemption (non-school-age children in informal care only)
Provide proof that each child is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien (birth certificate or citizenship documentation); parents are NOT required to be citizens
Provide proof of identity for all household members (government-issued document for adults; birth certificate for children)
Head of household must provide a Photo ID
Provide proof of residency (utility bill, lease agreement, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license with current address)

For full 52-week scholarship: submit additional verification within 15 days of fast-track approval, including 4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs, proof of approved activity, proof of all other income, and proof of address
Provide most recent 30 days of continuous income documentation for standard employment; 90 days for self-employment
Self-employed applicants must provide tax return (if after April 15) or profit and loss statements (if before April 15 or business is new) and completed Self-Employment Attestation Statement
Child care providers must be Maryland EXCELS participants to enroll children with scholarships (for formal care)
Providers must register and use the Child Care Provider Portal and submit timely and accurate attendance records
Families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness are eligible (referral letter on agency letterhead required)
Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the May 2025 enrollment freeze

Income fluctuations (overtime, seasonal work): caseworker must consider irregular income and calculate year-to-date gross income to determine eligibility; if irregular income exists, use YTD gross divided by weeks worked to calculate income

For informal child care providers: must complete fingerprinting, notarized child protective services consent form, health and safety standards agreement, emergency preparedness plan, emergency care and medication authorization form, proof of residency, proof of identity, SSN/ITIN card, immunization and blood-lead testing certificates (if applicable), proof of relatedness (if relative care), health and safety training certificates (3-hour basic plus 1.5-hour annual update), CPR and First Aid certification, and pass care location inspection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for an account in the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org. Step 2: Submit a Fast-Track application (available only when enrollment freeze is not in effect) or full application with required documentation: proof of employment/training/school enrollment, proof of residency, proof of income (4 weeks consecutive pay stubs or equivalent), proof of identity for all household members, and child citizenship documentation. Step 3: CCS Central 2 processes the application: Fast-Track within 3 business days (temporary 60-day scholarship issued if eligible); Full application within 30 calendar days from submission or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation (52-week scholarship issued if fully eligible). Step 4: If eligible, temporary 60-day scholarship is issued while full application is being reviewed. Step 5: Within 15 days of fast-track approval, submit additional documentation for full 52-week scholarship consideration (4 weeks consecutive pay stubs, proof of approved activity, proof of all income sources, proof of address). Step 6: Upon approval of full application, 52-week scholarship is issued (or 2-year scholarship for new/returning customers). Step 7: Select a child care provider in the portal and provider must approve the scholarship within 5 business days. Step 8: Child care begins and provider submits attendance records and invoices for payment. During enrollment freeze (effective May 1, 2025): approved applicants are placed on Frozen Status List (waitlist) and receive scholarships when funding becomes available; Fast-Track applications are not processed; full applications must be submitted; families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from freeze. For redetermination: 45 days before scholarship end date, families are prompted to submit redetermination application to continue receiving benefits; if denied or not submitted, scholarships end. For informal child care provider applications: contact CCS Central 2 at 1-877-227-0125; provider must complete Initial or Renewal application packet including background clearances, health and safety forms, emergency preparedness plan, training certificates, and pass care location inspection (60 days for approval). Families needing language assistance can call CCS Central 2 to request a translator. For providers: register with Maryland EXCELS and use the Child Care Provider Portal to manage enrollment, attendance, and invoicing; submit attendance sheets within 14 days when selected for attendance verification audit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Scholarship Advance Payments (Provider Payment System)
structured_extraction.program_description: A payment system where the Maryland State Department of Education provides advance payments to eligible child care providers based on enrollment of children with child care scholarships. Providers receive two payments per month instead of retroactive payments, and payment amounts are based on the number of children appearing on the provider's invoice by the last Saturday of each month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides advance payments to child care providers for children enrolled in the Child Care Scholarship program. Payments are issued in two equal installments per month: one on the 15th of the month and another on the last day of the month. The advance payment amount is based on the number of children with active receipted scholarship vouchers assigned to the provider as of the last Saturday of the previous month (the snapshot date). Payments are calculated using a daily rate multiplied by the number of payable days in each month to ensure accurate reimbursement regardless of the number of days in the month. Providers receive payment for full enrollment regardless of attendance unless a child's absences exceed 60 days within a calendar year or the child is an informal provider participant (who are not paid for absences and holidays). The program includes a True-Up reconciliation process that occurs one month after the advance payment to account for changes in enrollment status, voucher end dates, license status, Maryland EXCELS status, and other adjustments. True-Up reconciliation now consolidates adjustments across three months, with calculations provided in the monthly Invoice Detail Report. Registered Family Home Providers who are SEIU members continue to have union dues deducted from advance payments. Maryland EXCELS Tier Payments are added to advance payments based on the provider's quality rating. Registration fees, union dues, and recoupments are reconciled separately. For timely and accurate payments, providers must submit invoices within 15 calendar days of the end of a service period, customers must validate attendance within 15 calendar days of receiving alerts, and providers must upload Sign-In/Sign-Out sheets within 10 business days of receiving an attendance dispute notification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed and regulated child care providers, informal child care providers, and family child care home providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care services provided to children with child care scholarships. Providers submit invoices for each monthly service period for program integrity audits and attendance verification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Child care provider must have enrolled children with active child care scholarships
Provider must be licensed, regulated, or an approved informal child care provider
Provider must maintain current license, registration, or informal provider eligibility status
Children must appear on the provider's invoice as of the last Saturday of each month to be included in the advance payment calculation
Providers must submit invoices within 15 calendar days of the end of each monthly service period
Providers must pass MSDE Program Integrity Audits by submitting required documentation
Providers must validate attendance within 15 calendar days of receiving validation alerts
Providers must upload Sign-In/Sign-Out sheets within 10 business days of receiving attendance dispute notifications
For informal providers: children must have immunization records or exemption documentation; documentation proving relationship to child(ren) must be provided
Provider must maintain Maryland EXCELS participation as a requirement for CCS program participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Child care providers submit invoices for each monthly service period through the Child Care Provider Portal (https://provider.childcareportals.org/). Providers must register for a portal account with required information and set up a secure password. MSDE calculates advance payments based on enrollment as of the last Saturday of each month (the snapshot date). Two equal advance payments are processed on the 15th and last day of each month, viewable in the General Accounting Division system within specified payment dates. Providers receive payment invoices and detailed Invoice Detail Reports through the portal showing the enrollment count, unadjusted monthly amount, additional amounts from late-receipted vouchers, and offsets for scholarship changes. The True-Up reconciliation process occurs one month after the advance payment and consolidates adjustments across three months. True-Up calculations account for voucher end dates, EXCELS tier adjustments, changes in enrollment status, and ineligibility determinations. Invoices are reviewed as part of Program Integrity Audits. For questions or disputes, providers contact CCS Central 2 through the Provider Inquiry Link (for advance payment disputes) or Provider Portal (for informal appeals regarding repayment or audit results). Providers may submit informal appeals within 90 days of receiving payment or notification. Customer service support is available through multiple channels including the provider service request form, email at CCS2review.msde@maryland.gov, or phone at 877-227-0125. Extended hours are available (Tuesday-Thursday 5pm-9pm, Saturday 9am-12pm) for families and providers needing additional case management support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal special education program that requires local education agencies identified as having racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B funds to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of over-identification. The program funds educational and behavioral evaluations, services, professional development, and systemic changes to increase equity and decrease disproportionate representation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LEAs identified by the state as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement CCEIS. Funds must be used to supplement, not supplant, state and local funds. Reserved funds support: (1) educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; (2) professional development for staff to deliver scientifically-based interventions; (3) systemic awareness and leadership support; (4) self-assessment and data review processes; (5) development of comprehensive evaluation systems; and (6) organizational change initiatives. An LEA is identified if it has one or more subgroups of students with a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years, or if the risk ratio declines by less than the defined amount (.15 if less than 4.0 and .5 if over 4.0) from one year to the next. Allowable costs include: staff salaries and fringe benefits (RTI/MTSS coordinators, general education teachers, school psychologists, school social workers, guidance counselors, special education teachers providing Tier 2/3 interventions); extended contracts/hours for intervention delivery; coaches and mentors; tutors; substitute teachers; professional development services; computing devices for intervention delivery; instructional materials for struggling students; and software exclusively for interventions. Unallowable costs include: core curriculum/universal programming; bus or student transportation; furniture or office equipment; rent/occupancy costs; special education eligibility evaluations; OT/PT services; universal screening; Child Find activities; and alternative programming that replaces core instruction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Interim Progress Report #1: January 31, 2025; Interim Progress Report #2: January 31, 2026; Grant Amendment Requests: August 15, 2026; Final Progress Report: November 30, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA, Branch Chief; Demetria White, Interagency Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies in Maryland that have been identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development for staff; systemic awareness and leadership support; self-assessment and data review processes; development of comprehensive evaluation systems for plan outcomes; alignment of expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root causes of disproportionality; staff salaries for intervention coordination and delivery; extended contracts/hours; coaching and mentoring services; tutoring services; computing devices and instructional software for intervention delivery; and organizational change initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. LEAs are identified by the Maryland Department of Education based on special education data analysis of identification, placement, and disciplinary removal patterns by race/ethnicity across two or more years.
requirements_list: Local Education Agency Implementation Team must be established and meet regularly to co-develop, analyze data, co-implement, and co-evaluate the CCEIS Plan
Address factors contributing to significant disproportionality
Address and review policies, practices, or procedures contributing to over-identification

Convene a diverse local stakeholder group including external and internal partners, school/student support representatives, general and special education coordinators, school-based administrators, staff, and parents/community members
Engage in self-assessment and data review using one of three MSDE-recommended tools to determine root cause factors
Consider implementation drivers including staffing, training, coaching, staff evaluation, and data systems
Develop job-embedded professional learning experiences for personnel
Create a comprehensive evaluation system for plan outcomes emphasizing implementation fidelity and measurable student outcomes
Align projected expenditures with specific actions to meet CCEIS Plan outcomes
Complete CCEIS Plan using SFY 2025 template with budget detail forms (C-1-25)
Submit programmatic and fiscal amendments as needed
Submit interim progress reports (January 31, 2025 and January 31, 2026) and final progress reports (November 30, 2026)
Meet non-supplant requirement: funds must supplement, not replace, state, local, and other federal funds
Ensure compliance with 34 CFR §300.646 and IDEA Part B requirements

For each category of disproportionality identified, include at least one Planned Response Action (PRA) addressing review/adjustment of policies, procedures, and practices; at least one academic or behavioral intervention; and professional learning for capacity-building
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. LEAs identified as having significant disproportionality receive notification from Maryland Department of Education with specific data on identification, placement, and/or disciplinary removal categories. 2. Local Education Agency Implementation Team is established with diverse representation. 3. LEA conducts comprehensive self-assessment and root cause analysis using a MSDE-recommended tool (IDEA Data Center Equity Rubric, Safe and Supportive Learning Guide, or WestEd Program Review Tool). 4. Team completes SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan template including: Categories of Analysis table, self-assessment findings, root cause analysis, Planned Response Actions (PRAs) for each area of disproportionality, and measurable goals/benchmarks with data sources. 5. For each PRA, develop: policy/procedure reviews and adjustments, specific academic or behavioral interventions, and professional learning activities aligned to root causes. 6. Submit required fiscal documents: MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 (separate form if combining 611 and 619 allocations differently from state calculation) and detailed Budget Detail Forms showing category, object, description, unit costs, and quantities. 7. Obtain signatures from Local Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, and Superintendent. 8. Submit complete plan to MSDE for review by DEI/SES Equity Specialist, Programmatic Liaison, Fiscal Liaison, and RMMB Chief. 9. Upon approval, implement planned activities and monitor progress quarterly. 10. Submit Interim Progress Report #1 by January 31, 2025 (covering July 1, 2024–December 31, 2024); Interim Progress Report #2 by January 31, 2026 (covering January 1, 2025–December 31, 2025); request grant amendments by August 15, 2026 if needed; and submit Final Progress Report by November 30, 2026 (covering July 1, 2024–September 30, 2026). 11. Progress reports include Cumulative Variance Reports, intervening supports provided, disability determination data, PRA progress monitoring, and budget expenditure variances.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to eligible schools and residential child care institutions to help them comply with meal pattern rules established by the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010. structured_extraction.program_description: A quality improvement program that allows licensed child care centers and public pre-K programs to demonstrate their commitment to providing high-quality early learning and school-age services. Programs work through a 24-month process to meet Maryland Accreditation Standards, submit self-appraisals, develop improvement plans, receive technical assistance, and undergo validation visits. Once awarded, accreditation status is valid for five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive optional support through Virtual Technical Assistance (phone sessions with validators) and Onsite Technical Assistance (on-site validator observations). Virtual TA addresses questions about Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships indicators. Onsite TA includes observations of indoor and outdoor environments for Program Operations indicators. Both types of TA result in written feedback within three business days. Programs also have access to Accreditation Support Funds to assist with accreditation expenses, particularly for purchasing instructional materials. TA sessions must be satisfied (scheduled and completed or declined) before submitting Final Self-Appraisal and requesting validation visit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No set deadline; programs can apply year-round and work through the 24-month accreditation process at their own pace.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, public pre-K programs, and school-age only programs seeking to demonstrate commitment to high-quality early learning and school-age services. Family child care programs are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation Support Funds can be used for purchasing instructional materials to support accreditation efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, available to all Maryland licensed child care centers, public pre-K programs, and school-age only programs.
requirements_list: Program must be a licensed child care center, public pre-K program, or school-age only program
Family child care programs are not eligible
Program must complete self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation
Program must create a user account in the Maryland EXCELS/Maryland Accreditation online system at excels.marylandexcels.org
Program must complete a Program Application within the online system
Program must meet Maryland Accreditation Standards for early childhood or school-age programs
Program must form a Self-Appraisal Team with staff and family input
Program must complete Initial Self-Appraisals and submit comments and required documentation
Program must develop a Program Improvement Plan addressing indicators rated Partially Met or Not Met
Program must request or decline Virtual and/or Onsite Technical Assistance
Program must complete Final Self-Appraisal with comments and required documentation
Program must request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expires
Program must host Validation Visit at least 30 days before accreditation expires
Program must upload comments, required evidence, and pictures within 3 days of binder re-opening in response to validator ratings
Program must receive Accreditation Decision from MSDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Complete the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation. Step 2: Within 12 months of finishing orientation, access the Maryland EXCELS/Maryland Accreditation online system at excels.marylandexcels.org to create a user account. Step 3: Submit a Program Application providing your program's License Number, Registration Number, or School ID. Step 4: Form a Self-Appraisal Team. Step 5: Complete Initial Self-Appraisals for all indicators and submit documentation. Step 6: Apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds. Step 7: Develop a Program Improvement Plan for indicators rated Partially Met or Not Met. Step 8: Request or decline Virtual Technical Assistance (phone sessions addressing Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships) and/or Onsite Technical Assistance (validator observations of environments). Step 9: Complete Final Self-Appraisal and submit all comments and required documentation. Step 10: Request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expires. Step 11: Host the Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration. Step 12: Within 3 days of binder re-opening, upload comments, required evidence, and pictures in response to validator's ratings. Step 13: Receive Accreditation Decision from MSDE (date of receipt becomes anniversary date). After accreditation is awarded for five years: Years 1-3 submit Annual Updates up to 60 days before the due date; Years 4-5 begin re-accreditation process by completing orientation again.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development system that recognizes and rewards child care professionals (staff and administrators) who exceed state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience. Participants progress through seven credential levels for staff or four levels for administrators. The program helps develop a professional workforce, improve provider compensation, recognize professional learning and ongoing education, and provide a structure for career growth. Incentives include achievement bonuses, training vouchers and reimbursements, and access to tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund. Training Vouchers and Reimbursements provide eligible providers (Level 2 credential or higher) up to $400 annually to cover approved training, conferences, and college coursework—either as advance vouchers or post-training reimbursements submitted via the Maryland OneStop platform.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon achieving a credential level, with staff bonuses of $200-$1,000 (paid one-time at Levels 2, 3, and 4, and annually at Levels 4+, 5, and 6) and administrator bonuses of $600-$1,500 (paid one-time at Level 1, and annually at Levels 2, 3, and 4). Participants with credential Level 2 or higher receive up to $400 per year in training vouchers and reimbursements (as funds are available) for approved Core of Knowledge training, pre-service training, conference registration, and approved college coursework. Applicants may request advance training vouchers by submitting an application at least 60 days before the training; recipients download the signed voucher from Maryland OneStop and forward it to the trainer. Alternatively, participants may submit reimbursement applications within 180 days of training completion with documentation of successful completion (transcript, grade slip, or certificate). All participants are also eligible to receive tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund for pursuing Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degrees. All applications must be submitted via the Maryland OneStop platform.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Training voucher applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training. Training reimbursement applications must be submitted within 180 days of training completion. Applications accepted beginning December 29, 2025. Applicants will receive approval or denial notification via email within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, infant/toddler/preschool/school-age teachers, and assistants and aides working part-time or full-time in licensed child care centers or Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland who want to advance their professional development beyond state licensing requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-service training (45-hour Child Growth and Development, Methods and Materials, Directors/Administrator courses), approved Core of Knowledge training in six key areas (Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, Community), national and state conferences, college coursework, and approved professional development activities. Ineligible uses include training not approved by MSDE, training fees, association membership fees, CDA credential or CDA renewal fees, and activities serving only marketing purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; program is available in all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider or an operator, director, teacher, assistant teacher, or aide in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Must work directly with children on a daily basis (child care center employees in regional/district management, administrative, maintenance, food service, or transportation roles are ineligible)
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Must exceed state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience
Must complete approved training for the applicable credential level according to specific clock-hour requirements
Must participate in professional activities related to the child care profession for the applicable level (Professional Activity Units or PAUs)
Must continue working in a registered or licensed child care program for at least one year after acceptance and maintain participation
Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and may be renewed annually if you continue working in a registered or licensed child care program by submitting training, PAUs, and proof of employment
Training must be MSDE-approved according to COMAR 13A.14.09 and COMAR regulations
For training vouchers: must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential Level 2 or higher, OR have held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
For training vouchers: application must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training
For training reimbursement: application must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
Documentation of training completion (transcript, grade slip, or certificate of successful completion) is required for reimbursement claims
All applications must be submitted via Maryland OneStop platform
If a training voucher is not used without good cause, the provider must repay the voucher amount and becomes ineligible for additional vouchers until repayment is made
Professional activities not listed on the PAU Matrix require submission of a Professional Activities Approval Form for evaluation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For credential levels: Interested providers should watch the program website and email for updates on application availability. Work with the Credentialing Program to ensure that training is approved and applicable toward credential goals. Professional activities not listed on the PAU Matrix require submission of a Professional Activities Approval Form to credentialocc.msde@maryland.gov; requests will be reviewed within 60 days and assigned 1-3 PAUs if approved. For training vouchers and reimbursements: Submit a completed application via the Maryland OneStop platform beginning December 29, 2025. Log in to Maryland OneStop, complete the training voucher or reimbursement application, and submit required documentation. For advance vouchers: Submit at least 60 days before training; applicants will receive approval/denial notification via email within 30 days; approved applicants download the signed voucher from their Maryland OneStop dashboard and forward it to the trainer. For reimbursement: Submit within 180 days of training completion with certificate of completion; log into Maryland OneStop, navigate to My Dashboard, select the application, scroll to 'Verification of Training Completion' section, upload the certificate, and submit. Contact the Office of Child Care-Workforce Advancement Branch at credentialocc.msde@maryland.gov or (410) 767-7852 for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5 stars based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. The program helps early childhood and school-age care programs improve their services, with the goal of increasing the number of high-quality care options in Maryland. Participating providers receive guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training opportunities, and incentives to improve their practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating child care and early education providers receive quality ratings (1-5 stars), guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training opportunities, and incentives to improve their practices. Providers show evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards through an online system and receive ratings for each standard area as well as an overall rating. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants and Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities. Local Lead Agencies aggregate information from partner agencies to complete grant applications and required submissions, enabling the creation and operation of early intervention services in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and state funds awarded to local jurisdictions through Local Lead Agencies to support local early intervention programs. The grant period covers fiscal year 2026 (SFY 2026) and includes both federal and state general funds. Grantees receive access to secure accounts on the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) for submission of grant-related documents including pdf-formatted applications, reports, and amendment requests. The MMSFTW enables secure outbound submission of documents 365 days per year with designated ToMSDE and FromMSDE folders for document exchange. Formula and project grants are provided to local jurisdictions to support early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing with multiple submission deadlines throughout the grant period; applications submitted annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Brian Morrison; Daniele Redivo, Management Associate; Glenn Graymen, Lead Fiscal Grants Liaison; Nancy Vorobey, Fiscal Liaison
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITPs), local governments, and non-profit organizations that implement early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities in Maryland jurisdictions.

Funds may be used for grant-related expenses as specified in the SFY 2026 budget submissions workbook.

requirements_list: Must be designated Local Lead Agency of a Local Infants & Toddlers Program
Must aggregate information from LITP partner agencies
Must complete grant application using current SFY 2026 forms
Must submit all budget and post-application submissions as specified
Must upload all submissions to MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/
Must follow file naming conventions: FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_APP.pdf for applications and FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_Grant#_TypeCode.pdf for amendments and reports
Must send email notification to assigned fiscal grants liaison upon document upload, specifying document name(s)
Each Program Director/Project Manager must be designated as Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) with Entity Code and log-on credentials
Must ensure only authorized individuals have access to MMSFTW and immediately notify fiscal grants liaison to deactivate access for departing employees
Must immediately download and save documents received from MSDE in FromMSDE folder as files are subject to deletion 30 days from posting date
Must file reports by specified deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies download current forms from the MSDE website. They complete the SFY 2026 CLIG Application, SFY 2026 CLIG Budget Submissions Workbook, and required assurances and certifications. The designated Grants Submission Coordinator logs into the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ using Entity Code and credentials. All submissions are uploaded to the program's designated shared folder in the ToMSDE folder following file naming conventions (INTG_EntityID_SFY_CLIG_APP.pdf for applications). After uploading, grantees must send an email notification to their assigned fiscal grants liaison specifying the document name(s) and save a screenshot as proof of submission. Budget and post-application submissions (including amendments, program reports, and financial reports) follow instructions in the CLIG Grant Information Guide and use forms from designated Excel workbooks, using appropriate Type Codes (AMD for amendments, SEMIPRO for semi-annual reports, ANNUPRO for annual reports, ICVR for interim cumulative variance reports, FCVR for final cumulative variance reports, 400 for Form 400, 500 for Form 500, AFR for annual financial reports, FFR for final financial reports).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services include adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, and therapeutic integration. Participants also receive service coordination and full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver covers nine community-based therapeutic services provided by approved Medicaid provider agencies. Services include: Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance for self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills); Therapeutic Integration-Regular or Intensive (structured programs outside school hours with therapeutic and expressive therapies); Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living); Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for home modifications to ensure health, welfare, and safety); Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training); Adult Life Planning (family-centered support for accessing adult community services); and Residential Habilitation-Regular or Intensive (community-based residential placement for children requiring highly supervised environments). Participants receive full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, mental health services, and service coordination through their local education agency. Over 60 provider agencies statewide are approved to deliver services. Enrollment is based on chronological order from placement on the waitlist. Participants must use at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month to maintain eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of the application letter from Maryland Department of Health to complete financial eligibility application
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of Health Autism Waiver Helpline and Local Education Agency Autism Waiver Contacts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old with Autism Spectrum Disorder who reside in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services including adult life planning, environmental home adaptations for safety and independence, family consultation and training, one-on-one support services, residential habilitation for community-based living, respite care, and structured therapeutic integration programs. Funds also cover full Medical Assistance benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Children and youth must reside in Maryland.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Are ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Reside in Maryland

Receive early intervention or special education services through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 or more hours of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit
Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs

Military Exception: Dependents of U.S. Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
Maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in services must call the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register. The Maryland Department of Health vendor conducts an initial screening during the intake call based on parent self-report to verify technical eligibility criteria (Maryland resident, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, and IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education and health-related services). If the child meets technical eligibility criteria, MSDE is notified and a letter is sent to the family confirming the name has been added to the Autism Waiver Registry. Children are then added to a waitlist in chronological order. When a vacancy occurs, the Maryland Department of Health sends an application letter inviting the family to apply. Families have 45 days from the application letter date to: (1) contact the local education agency or early intervention program to speak with the Autism Waiver contact, (2) work with the assigned Service Coordinator to complete the financial eligibility application, (3) contribute to the Level of Care assessment process for medical eligibility determination, and (4) complete the technical eligibility checklist and submit required documentation. The family works with the Autism Waiver contact to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. Once eligible, the State sends a notification letter including a start date to begin services. The family then attends a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care before services begin.
