structured_extraction.program_name: Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and additional services designed to complement their regular academic program. Community learning centers offer families literacy instruction and related educational development programs. The program targets students and families at schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Programs occur before school, after school, during the summer, and on Saturdays to keep students safe, assist working families, and improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to local education agencies (LEAs), interagency organizations, community and faith-based organizations, private or public organizations, and consortiums of two or more agencies to provide academic enrichment and educational services to students and families at Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students. Total funds available: $22.6 million (FY25). Grant awards are three-year grants (36 months) with funding at 100% for year one and year two, contingent on satisfactory performance and compliance. Programs selected for funding will be level funded the same amount for all three years unless reduced based on performance or funding availability. Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance. Grant funds must be expended in the grant year they were awarded; MSDE does not allow carryover of funds. Final expenditure reports are due 60 days after the end of the grant period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, schools, non-profit agencies, community and faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, and for-profit corporations serving students and families primarily attending Title I eligible schools or schools with high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities, services complementing regular academic programs, and literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. Allowable expenses include: intervention strategies and curriculum purchases meeting ESSA evidence criteria; salaries and fringe benefits for 21st CCLC OST staff; professional development and 21st CCLC trainings; consultants, subcontractors, and evaluators; classroom materials and supplies; remedial educational activities and academic enrichment learning programs; core academic subject educational activities; arts and music education activities; entrepreneurial education and college and career readiness programs; tutoring services and mentoring programs; programs for limited English proficient students; recreational activities; telecommunications and technology education programs; expanded library service hours; drug and violence prevention programs; counseling programs; and character education programs. Unallowable expenses include proposal preparation costs, pre-award costs, entertainment and refreshments, unapproved field trips, incentives, promotional items, vehicles or facilities purchases, capital improvements, supplanting funds, and any costs not allowable under federal programs per 2 CFR 200.400.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided to students and families who primarily attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Title I schools that serve at least 40% of students from low-income families, high schools with graduation rates less than 67%, and other schools determined by the LEA to need intervention and support are eligible service sites.
requirements_list: Participants must provide services to students and families of students who primarily attend Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of low-income students
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance
Proposed activities must target students and families from low-income backgrounds
Demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served
Attend required out-of-school (OST) national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings

Submit required documentation in a timely manner during the project year including monitoring components (Start-Up, Interim, Grant Renewal Application, End of Year Reports, and Critical Elements Monitoring), corrective actions, monthly reimbursement expenditure reports, and detailed local narrative evaluation reports

Maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to the United States Department of Education 21 Annual Performance Report database by established deadlines including: academic achievement measures (reading/language arts and math growth for grades 4-8), grade point average improvements (grades 7-8 and 10-12 with prior-year GPA less than 3.0), school day attendance rate improvements (grades 1-12 with prior-year attendance at or below 90%), behavior measures (decrease in in-school suspensions for grades 1-12), and student engagement in learning improvements (grades 1-5)
Participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements
Provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes, and safety standards

Non-LEA subrecipients operating in non-public school facilities must submit copies of all required licenses and certifications for health and safety including Use and Occupancy (U&O) permit and current Fire Inspection report per operating site
Provide description of how grant provides comparable opportunities for public and private school student participation with evidence of consultation with private school officials
Describe efforts to provide timely notice of intent to apply and information dissemination methods

Meet minimum programming hours: School Year Programs (no less than 12 hours per week for 25 weeks or 4 hours on Saturdays for 25 weeks, with at least 4 hours academic programming per week or 1 hour per Saturday); School Year and Summer Programs (same school year requirements plus minimum 80 hours summer with at least 32 hours onsite academic and enrichment); Summer Only Programs (minimum 80 hours with at least 32 hours onsite academic and enrichment)
Implement programs aligned with Maryland College and Career Readiness Standards
Identify at least one Maryland Leads Strategy, Maryland Strategic Plan, or Blueprint for Maryland's Future Priority area as focus of proposed 21st CCLC programming

Address and improve measurable state data goals including reading/language arts growth, math growth, GPA improvement, 80% attendance rate achievement, decreased in-school suspensions, and improved teacher-reported engagement in learning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a grant application through the Qualtrics application system by the deadline of Friday, August 29, 2025. The renewal application was released on Friday, July 25, 2025. Customer Service Support Sessions are available to assist applicants with the application process. For renewal applications, subgrantees must submit grant renewal applications providing programmatic and fiscal outcome data for the prior grant award period and a grants management plan for the next year for review. Applications must include required exhibits: Performance Goals and Indicators, Management Plan, Partner Plan, and Evaluation Plan. Final documents must be uploaded into the Critical Elements Monitoring folder by the deadline. MSDE reviews applications and evaluates compliance with all grant requirements. Upon submission and review of grant renewal applications and performance data (including Start-up report, Critical Elements Monitoring Stages I, II and III, timely reimbursement invoice submissions, and number of amendments), MSDE will approve subgrantees for continuation funding and assign a risk assessment level (1-5) reflected on the Notification of Grant Award (NOGA). Eligible organizations become grantees upon approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state aid program that reimburses the cost of tuition for students with special education needs who are placed in nonpublic special education schools through their Individualized Education Program (IEP). The state covers a portion of the tuition cost as calculated under Maryland Education Article §8-415. The program covers both day and residential placements, including MSDE-approved programs and individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State reimburses a share of nonpublic special education tuition costs through a per diem rate structure. Students placed in MSDE-approved nonpublic special education schools are included in the September 30th enrollment count and receive state aid through a tuition reimbursement process rather than Foundation calculations. Reimbursement covers standard educational and related services, extended school year services when applicable, and residential services if deemed necessary by the IEP team. Related services and supplemental aides beyond standard services are itemized on cost sheets with billable units specified. The program accepts both approved day/residential program placements and individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Submission timelines vary: ESY or Entry dates occurring during July/August submit by September 30; Entry dates September 1 to June 2 submit within 30 calendar days of Entry Date; Entry dates June 3-30 submit by July 7; Discharge applications submit within 30 calendar days of Discharge Date; Service Revision applications submit within 30 calendar days of Service Revision Date
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD, Section Chief, Nonpublic Special Education; Jeffrey Miller, Data Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school districts placing students with special education needs in nonpublic special education schools, including both MSDE-approved programs and non-approved or out-of-state placements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nonpublic special education tuition costs for students placed through the IEP process, including standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services when applicable, and supplemental services and program modifications outlined in the IEP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for students in MSDE-approved nonpublic special education schools in Maryland, as well as non-approved or out-of-state special education programs when placement is determined necessary through the IEP process.
requirements_list: Student must have an Individualized Education Program (IEP) that documents placement in a nonpublic special education school
School must be MSDE-approved for approved day/residential program placements
Student must be included in the September 30th enrollment count with a code 09 attached to indicate nonpublic placement
For non-approved or out-of-state placements, IEP team must document reason for school placement

For new/renewal individual placements, applicant must submit approved cost sheet, IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from service provider stating they can implement FAPE in least restrictive environment, and copy of agreement/decision for mediated or due process cases if applicable
All information on NTAP application must be typed or printed legibly
LSS Special Education Supervisor/Director or Designee must sign and verify accuracy of cost sheet
Student information must include complete demographic data, disability code, unique ID, and medical assistance number when available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit either the MSDE Approved Day and Residential Program Application or an Individual Placement application to request approval of funding. For approved programs: applications include directions, definitions, explanations, and examples to guide completion of student information, IEP placement information, requested reimbursement for services, and verification/assurance sections. An approved cost sheet must accompany each application. Submission timelines vary by entry/discharge date: ESY or July/August entries submit by September 30; September 1 to June 2 entries submit within 30 calendar days of entry date; June 3-30 entries submit by July 7; discharge applications submit within 30 days of discharge; service revision applications submit within 30 days of revision. For individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, new/renewal applications must include approved cost sheet, IEP team minutes, provider letter regarding FAPE implementation, and mediation/due process documentation if applicable. All applications require LSS Special Education Supervisor/Director sign-off. Written notice must be provided if unable to meet submission timeline. MSDE may audit applications and supporting documentation; discrepancies or noncompliance may result in refund requirements.
