structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to local education agencies and private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families earning up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level at no cost to families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided to local education agencies (LEAs/public school systems) and qualified private providers (including Head Start programs and licensed or registered child care centers and family child care homes) to administer and deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten programming and school readiness services. Funding amount available: $26,644,000 with an estimated average grant award of $400,000 (approximately 50 grants estimated). Funding per full-day slot: $19,950 for three-year-olds and four-year-olds. Grant period: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Instructional year minimum: 180 days. Programs must offer full-day instruction (at least 6.5 hours) at no cost to eligible families. Grant funds enable providers to offer services at no cost to eligible families earning at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level. For nonprofit organizations, indirect costs may not exceed 15% of total funding request. For all other grantees, indirect costs may not exceed 10%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT (Amended March 6, 2026)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (public school systems) and private child care providers (including Head Start programs, center-based programs, and family child care homes) that are licensed or registered and can deliver high-quality prekindergarten services to three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services aligned with the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. Eligible uses include: salaries, wages, and fringe benefits for teaching staff (commensurate with local school system salaries); equipment, materials, and supplies (classroom furniture, instructional materials including MSDE-approved curriculum resources aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards); reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated based on square footage); technology costs (not to exceed 10% of total fund request); costs associated with maintaining Maryland or national accreditation status or Maryland EXCELS rating; costs for contracts to administer screening and intervention services; costs associated with evaluation and monitoring (not to exceed 5% of total fund request); indirect costs (not to exceed 15% for nonprofits, 10% for others); costs for at least one meal per day meeting CACFP meal pattern requirements; costs for academic field trips; costs for approved professional learning activities for instructional staff. Grant funds may not be used for: supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, costs incurred prior to grant approval, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. All counties are eligible. Priority will be given to programs in areas with unmet need for prekindergarten services.
requirements_list: Applicants must hold a valid license or registration issued by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) (if applicable)
Applicants must currently meet the Maryland EXCELS rating requirement (Level 3 or higher for private providers, Level 4 or higher for public providers)
Programs must deliver high-quality prekindergarten services in alignment with the Blueprint for Maryland's Future
Children served must be ages three or four
Families served must have household incomes at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Programs must participate in Maryland EXCELS program
Applicants must provide measurable SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes
Programs must describe procedures for income verification and family document collection to determine eligibility based on FY 2026 Federal Poverty Levels
Programs must describe methods for identifying and appropriately serving students with disabilities, students experiencing homelessness, and students who speak a home language other than English
Programs must demonstrate high-quality prekindergarten programming with qualified teaching staff
Lead teachers must meet Blueprint for Maryland's Future requirements
For classrooms with more than 10 students, an Assistant Teacher meeting Blueprint requirements must be present
Lead teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026
Private providers must have a valid child care license
Head Start programs must submit a letter of support from the funded grantee if applicant is not the funded grantee
All grant requirements must be met prior to start of grant year and before invoices or advance requests can be paid
Programs must provide description of community need for high-quality Pre-K education
Programs must include family engagement strategies
Programs must demonstrate plan to build long-term sustainability and community/business partnerships
Programs must provide professional learning activities for instructional staff consisting of at least 20 hours supporting school readiness and aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards
Programs must use valid and reliable child assessment tools to monitor progress
Programs must provide health screenings and referrals for vision, hearing/speech/language, general health, and physical development
Applicants receiving Blueprint funding must increase number of three and four-year-old children served in full-day Pre-K as reported in September 30, 2025 enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically through Qualtrics by 5:00 p.m. EDT on March 11, 2026. Applicants must first answer initial eligibility questions to confirm program meets basic eligibility requirements. Based on responses, applicants will be directed to either a Full Application (for new applicants and existing grantees without track record of success) or Modified Short Form Application (for programs seeking renewal/expansion with demonstrated track record of success). The Full Application consists of 10 sections: (1) Program Eligibility - Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation, (2) Evidence of Need/Market Analysis, (3) Measurable Goals, (4) Program Quality and Curriculum, (5) Plan of Operation, (6) Staffing, Key Personnel, and Management Plan, (7) Project Timeline/Implementation Plan, (8) Collaboration and Sustainability, (9) Fiscal Systems and Controls, and (10) Budget and Budget Narrative. Modified Short Form includes only required sections marked in application. Applicants can complete application in multiple sittings using same device and browser, with progress saved. Before final submission, applicants have opportunity to review all answers and download responses for their records. MSDE offers customer service support sessions and office hours to assist applicants with understanding requirements and completing applications. Paper application is available for reference only; all submissions must be electronic. Grant Information Guides and supporting documents are available on MSDE website. Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between MSDE, LEA, and any private providers must be submitted no later than September 30, 2026. A 20% payment advance may be requested at time of application (15% will be issued upon meeting all grant requirements).

structured_extraction.program_name: Project SELECT (Student Education, Lunchroom Environment, and Culinary Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA Team Nutrition training grant that targeted middle schools to increase students' selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits through culinary training, food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A USDA Team Nutrition grant implemented from 2016 through 2019 providing training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. Also included development of a family engagement wellness toolkit to support wellness policy implementation involving families and parents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in targeted school systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary training, food service operations training, Smarter Lunchrooms implementation, food tasting events, nutrition education, and family engagement wellness toolkit development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Middle schools in Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico County school systems
requirements_list: Middle school enrollment in targeted school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This was a time-limited grant program implemented from 2016 through 2019 and is no longer accepting new applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding by providing guidance through the grant application process and connecting providers with Pre-K Specialists who walk them through every step.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to state prekindergarten funding through grants and offers technical assistance through Pre-K Specialist s who guide child care provider s through the application process and requirement s for obtaining Pre-K grant s. Provider s receive support in understanding eligibility criteria, organizational capacity, and stakeholder readiness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care provider s seeking to expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To expand child care service s and meet requirement s for state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Organization must be eligible to apply based on Grant Information Guide eligibility criteria
Organization must have the technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to successfully provide service s as described in the Grant Information Guide
All organizational stakeholder s must be supportive of applying for the grant
Organization must have read and understood the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Provider s should complete the Grant Consideration Checklist to determine if they meet all prerequisite s before beginning the application. Pre-K Specialist s provide guidance through every step of the process. Applicant s should refer to the Pre-K Grant s resource and complete the eligibility checklist to determine if the grant is appropriate for their program. Provider s must answer 'yes' to all questions on the Grant Consideration Checklist before proceeding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides nutritious breakfast meals to students in Maryland public schools, private nonprofit schools, and residential childcare institutions. The program reimburses participating schools with federal dollars for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards, helping schools and residential child care facilities cover the cost of providing breakfast to school-age children. Students may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income. All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students daily.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive reimbursement (direct payments) from the federal government for nutritious breakfasts served to students that meet USDA nutrition standards. Students may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income. Funds help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools and residential child care institutions, including Maryland public school systems, private nonprofit schools, and residential childcare institutions; ultimately serving students who may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help cover the costs of producing nutritious breakfast meals for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions throughout the state
requirements_list: Must be a participating public school, private nonprofit school, or residential childcare institution
Meals must meet USDA nutrition standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides milk to children in schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate. The program reimburses eligible institutions for milk served to children, helping to lower the cost of milk provided to children at these sites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for milk served to children in eligible schools, childcare centers, and camps. The program provides direct payments to offset the cost of milk served to children who are not covered by other federal child nutrition meal service programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private nonprofit schools, childcare centers, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit organizations that serve milk to children and do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs; schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children lack access to school meal programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for milk served to children; funds must be used to lower the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a school, childcare center, or eligible camp not participating in other federal child nutrition meal service programs
Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences aligned with the State's curricular and educational priorities that cannot be replicated in the classroom, emphasizing experiential learning and one-on-one support services including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants provided to qualified non-profit organizations to support educational programs. Funds must be used for direct services to students and teachers within the fiscal year. Funds may be used for: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs (property repair, maintenance, property taxes, insurance, furniture, administrative salaries, office supplies, rent), or food. Approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded. Grant period is July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Currently, there are 57 organizations in the SAI program. In fiscal year 2024, approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers were served through this program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports educational programs including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development opportunities for teachers that connect SAI programs to classroom curriculum. Funds may be used for salaries, wages, stipends, supplies, materials, outreach and marketing tools, and equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers. Funds may NOT be used for construction, capital improvements, transportation, utilities, operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. For fiscal year 2026, fifty-six programs are funded across the State.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing
Non-profit must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers
Programs must provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities
Programs must offer educational opportunities that cannot be replicated in the classroom
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Applicants must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement describing the educational program, amount of funds requested, populations to be served, educational goals and objectives, and anticipated outcomes
Applicants must provide names of independent governing board members
Applicants must submit proof of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Applicants must provide evidence of current independent annual audit or most recent internally generated financial statement
Applicants must provide evidence of active liability insurance coverage
Applicants must provide detailed operating budget showing less than 50% of budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo), with all sources of income and expenditures specified

Applicants must provide evidence of provision of direct service to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including data on student age levels and projected numbers of students and teachers to be served statewide and by jurisdiction
Applicants must provide plans to align educational programs with MSDE's educational and curricular priorities
New applicants must provide evidence that the educational program is not new and can show a track record of success
Applicants must set programmatic goals that are specific, measurable, ambitious yet attainable, realistic, and time-bound with clear evaluation methods
Applicants must provide detailed educational programming descriptions including grade levels, areas of educational focus, and related curricular standards
Applicants must have an outreach plan to advertise programs, including steps to provide outreach to historically underserved populations
Applicants must provide a project timeline with key activities and implementation dates
Applicants must identify key personnel with titles, responsibilities, and tasks

Applicants must submit detailed budget narrative with itemized line-item expenses grouped by category (Salaries & Wages, Contracted Services, Supplies & Materials, Other Charges, Equipment, Transfers)
Applicants must submit completed C-1-25 MSDE grant budget form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application period opens Thursday, May 1, 2025. MSDE will hold virtual customer service support sessions on May 5 and May 23, 2025 to review program requirements and assist applicants in understanding the application process. Applicants must download the electronic SAI application from the MSDE SAI webpage, complete it with all attachments, and save it as one PDF file. All grant applications must be submitted by email to sai.applications@maryland.gov no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on Friday, June 13, 2025. MSDE reviews applications on a rolling basis. Submitted applications undergo pre-screening for submission requirements and inclusion of all required sections. Applications not meeting pre-screen requirements may be returned for revisions. A review committee established by MSDE evaluates applications using a scoring rubric. For any application section scored as Level 1 (does not meet criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. MSDE communicates evaluation results to the State Superintendent of Schools in July 2025. Data is then sent to the State Board of Education for review and discussion in August 2025. Final approval for awards is determined in legislation as authorized by the budget bill for fiscal year 2027, with the Governor releasing the draft budget bill in January 2026 and final voting around April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program that provides free nutritious meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas during the summer months when school is not in session. The program reimburses providers (sponsors) who serve meals through community organizations at designated summer meal sites across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses organizations that serve free meals to children and teens. Meals are provided at designated summer meal sites in low-income areas. Two types of meal service are available: SUN Meals (where meals are consumed on-site with activities provided) and SUN Meals To-Go (where multi-day meal boxes are provided for pickup, requiring registration). Program sponsors apply to operate summer food service sites through the Maryland State Department of Education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas during summer months when school is not in session
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing free nutritious meals to eligible children and teens during summer
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; program operates through county-based sponsoring organizations listed for each of Maryland's 24 counties, serving economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must apply through the sponsoring organization in their county
Sites must serve free meals in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas
Meals must meet federal nutrition requirements and meal patterns by age and grade
For SUN Meals To-Go sites, beneficiaries must register to receive multi-day meal boxes
Must serve children 18 and under
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in becoming a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization in their county. Baltimore City has an online application available. Other counties require phone contact with their county public schools or designated sponsoring agency. Program sponsors apply to operate summer food service sites through the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) Annual Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Required annual training for participating agencies providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development for the Summer Food Service Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free required annual training providing updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development for participating Summer Food Service Program agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agencies participating in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual training on SFSP regulations, updates, and professional development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Participation in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at 410-767-0199 for dates and locations of annual training meetings.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to Local Education Agencies (school districts) that participate in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option to support recipe development using local agricultural products. The grant funds staff training, recipe tasting events, and supplies to develop high-quality recipes that appeal to students and can realistically be implemented in school kitchens. MSDE works with chefs from Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality to develop standardized recipes using local agricultural products.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides grant funding to Local Education Agencies to support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events during the grant period (May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023). Funds may be used for: salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow attendance at training; stipends for staff time attending training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, utensils) with total equipment value not exceeding 5% of subgrant total; food costs for training and taste tests not exceeding 20% of subgrant total, purchased in accordance with Buy American Provision; and consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests. MSDE anticipates awarding approximately ten (10) grants with possibility of additional grants if funds available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 22, 2022, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 that commit participation of up to three schools and ensure schools are registered as Team Nutrition Schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time for training and recipe tasting events; food and supplies for tasting events; development of training and nutrition education resources; salaries/wages for substitute staff; stipends for training attendance; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (limited to 5% of total); food costs for training and taste tests (limited to 20% of total). Funds cannot be used for child nutrition program costs outside grant scope, purchasing meals for training, foods for reimbursable meals, foods as prizes/incentives, foods for home preparation, foods unrelated to standardized recipes, prizes or incentive items, gardening tools or materials, or clothing items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Schools participating must be located in Maryland and may receive priority consideration if located in rural zones as defined by USDA map or in Internal Revenue Service (IRS) designated Qualified Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during 2021-2022 and in good standing
Must commit participation of up to three schools; if more than one school selected, at least two schools must serve different grade levels
Must select schools enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools; schools must be registered prior to application submission
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities implemented at all participating schools
School nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Schools must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
Grant Coordinator must collect feedback from students and school nutrition staff and submit after each tasting event
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
Schools must serve at least one of final new recipes in a reimbursable meal by end of grant period
LEA and schools must submit quarterly reports on grant activities and utilization of funds
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must: (1) Identify up to three participating schools that participate in NSLP or SSO and are registered as Team Nutrition Schools; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member; (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application including all components (school listing, recipe selection from four available recipes - Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, or Entrée Salad - budget, and school agreements); (4) Submit required attachments including signed MSDE Assurances Page, signed LEA and School Agreement Forms, and Team Nutrition Budget (Excel file). Applications must be submitted electronically to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov by the deadline. MSDE will review applications for eligibility and completeness, score applications using selection criteria based on Free and Reduced-Price enrollment percentages and school location in rural zones or Qualified Opportunity Zones, and notify approximately ten LEAs of award status. Award notification sent by email in spring with official Notice of Grant Awards processing beginning May 1, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program (Judy Center Early Learning Hubs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant-funded early learning hubs located in elementary schools across Maryland, formally established under the Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program. This program helps at-risk children from birth to age six (prenatal through age 5) and their families prepare for school. Judy Centers serve as comprehensive support centers for families using a multigenerational approach to prepare children for success in school and life. They provide developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, and case management with families and service coordination with community partners. Grants are also provided to child care providers for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. Professional development for early childhood educators is offered. As of FY2024, there are 86 Judy Center sites serving every local school system in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers provide grants to child care providers for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. Comprehensive family support and early care and education services are also provided including: full-day/full-year services (7-12 hours per day, year-round), meals for children and families during school days, school breaks, weekends, and after-school hours, case management and service coordination with community partners, integration of early education services across Prekindergarten, Kindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, and child care programs, family engagement through parent and child playgroups (minimum 2 per week; average of 3 per week statewide), early identification and intervention for children birth through five years, full inclusion of children with disabilities under IEP and IFSP, health-related services including referrals for dental, vision, hearing and mental health screenings, professional learning opportunities for early childhood educators, adult education and career services connections, support for accreditation of partner early care programs, and active community partnerships. In FY2024, Judy Centers served 17,681 children and 14,750 families across 86 sites, made 80,367 referrals to community partners and agencies, and supported 2,202 children with IEP/IFSP and 512 housing-insecure children.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually (approximately June).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance); Judy Walker
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 who live within the school zone where a Judy Center is located, particularly targeting low-income families in Title I school districts. Also supports early childhood educators and child care providers who serve at-risk children. Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, full-day/full-year care and education, home visiting, case management, health screenings and referrals, professional development for early childhood educators, support for program accreditation, and grants to child care providers for accreditation and staff professional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are located in elementary schools across all 24 Maryland counties plus Baltimore City, serving every local school system. Children must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. As of FY2024, 86 Judy Centers are operating with planned expansion of nine sites annually until 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030 as part of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. Sites are particularly concentrated in Title I school districts.
requirements_list: Child must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 are eligible
Children will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located

Families and children are considered served if they engage with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year or are enrolled in formal partner programs (Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or child care centers)
All early care and education programs in partnership with the Judy Center must be accredited or actively pursuing accreditation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in Judy Center services should contact their local Judy Center directly. Judy Centers operate within elementary school catchment areas and families do not submit formal applications. Instead, families engage with their local Judy Center for enrollment in services. A comprehensive contact list with coordinator names, emails, and phone numbers for all 86 Judy Center sites across Maryland is available, organized by county. Information about each Judy Center location and services is available at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/. Once families connect with their local Judy Center coordinator, services including family engagement activities, case management, and referrals to community partners are coordinated. Child care providers seeking grants should contact the program annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded nutrition program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides reimbursement to childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities for serving nutritionally balanced meals and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards. The program helps licensed daycare providers pay for nutritious meals and snacks for children, older adults, and people with disabilities in their care, supporting healthy growth and development of young children and the health and wellness of older adults and people with disabilities. Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate in CACFP.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CACFP sponsors receive federal cash reimbursement for meals and snacks served to eligible children and adults that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Participating facilities receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Emergency shelters receive the highest reimbursement rates with minimal paperwork requirements. Child care centers can receive maximum annual reimbursement based on the number of free-eligible participants served breakfast, lunch, and snacks 5 days per week. Family child care homes receive separate reimbursement rates based on Tier I participants served.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters serving children 18 years and younger, adult day care facilities serving adults over 60 or living with a disability, and licensed child care providers and programs, including public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers. Family child care homes can also participate through sponsoring organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal reimbursement for providing nutritionally balanced meals and snacks to enrolled children, older adults, and people with disabilities that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; statewide. Family child care homes are supported through sponsoring organizations located in specific regions including Cecil County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Kent County, Frederick County, Carroll County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and through The Planning Council for all counties.
requirements_list: Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services.
Participating facilities must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Children 18 years and younger in emergency shelters are automatically eligible for free meals
Must be a participating childcare center, daycare home, afterschool program, emergency shelter, or adult daycare facility
Centers must complete CACFP Basics Training
Centers must complete three-part online application
Facilities are subject to MSDE pre-approval visit before approval to claim reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Child and Adult Care Centers: 1) Call MSDE at (410) 767-0199 to begin the CACFP Interest Process. 2) Complete the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet. 3) MSDE determines center eligibility. 4) Complete CACFP Basics Training and three-part online application. 5) MSDE conducts a pre-approval visit. 6) MSDE approves the center to participate; center can begin claiming reimbursement for meals served. For Family Child Care Homes: Contact your county's sponsoring organization to begin enrollment. Sponsoring organizations include Cecil County Government (410-996-0253), Frederick County Community Action Agency (301-600-6263), Montgomery County Public Schools (301-284-4937), Prince George's County Public Schools (301-817-0535), and The Planning Council (757-657-0716). Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious lunches and snacks to students in Maryland public and private schools and residential childcare institutions. The program provides reimbursement and direct payments to help offset the cost of producing meals for students, serving over 900,000 students daily across all 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive reimbursement from the federal government for nutritious lunches and snacks served to students. The program provides direct payments to help offset the cost of producing meals for students. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 900,000 students daily.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions, as well as the schools and residential child care institutions themselves.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help cover the cost of producing nutritious lunches and snacks for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems participate, plus 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must be a participating public or private nonprofit school, residential childcare facility, or eligible institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland offers this gap financing loan program to help small businesses locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. The program partners with banks and other lenders to fund the part of a project that a primary lender cannot cover, with the primary goal of creating or retaining jobs in the region. Funded by federal and state grants, repaid loan funds are returned to the revolving loan fund to make additional loans. The program has been operating since 1980.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides gap financing loans from $10,000 to $400,000. A bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate. Funds are returned to the revolving loan fund upon repayment to finance additional loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses — including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships — seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County that cannot obtain all needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, machinery and equipment, start-up costs, and working capital for location and expansion projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in or planning to locate in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County in the Appalachian region of Maryland.
requirements_list: Small business seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington county
A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with participating banks and lenders to apply for gap financing. Steps include: (1) Create a business plan and determine funding needs. (2) Apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. (3) Complete the program's application form and submit it with required documents and the application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance to agricultural operations in Washington County for innovation and equipment purchases to enhance farm operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases for farms operating in Washington County. Farmers and agricultural operations may also have access to additional financing and grant programs through MARBIDCO, USDA Rural Development, and other state and federal programs for equipment, working capital, renewable energy, conservation measures, and value-added agricultural projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural operations and farmers in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation projects and equipment purchases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to enter into a ten-year agreement restricting their land from development. In exchange, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), and receive a property tax credit on their agricultural real property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who voluntarily enter the program agree not to develop their land for ten years, with the agreement recorded in the County Land Records and binding even if the property is sold or transferred. In exchange, they receive: (1) County property tax credits for the farmland, farm buildings, and partial tax credit for the home; (2) protection from nuisance complaints under the Right to Farm Ordinance through official County acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use; (3) eligibility to apply to sell development rights easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF); and (4) security that the land and nearby districts and easements are protected from development. The program does not provide direct financial assistance but offers tax credits and protections. After ten years, landowners may terminate the agreement at any time for any reason.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Planning & Zoning / Land Preservation Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land restriction and preservation; program does not provide direct financial assistance but offers tax credits and protections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Landowner must own agricultural land
Property must contain a minimum of 50 acres as a stand-alone parcel or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Property must have a minimum of 50% of soil classes I, II and III
Property must be outside water and sewer service areas
Property must be outside of growth areas
Must voluntarily agree to a ten-year development restriction on the land
Land may not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial or residential use except as permitted by County Regulations
Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within a soil conservation plan approved by the local soil conservation district must be implemented within 10 years
Property must comply with all terms and conditions of the County's Ordinance and Regulations for the Establishment of Agricultural Preservation Districts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning / Land Preservation Office. Landowners complete the Agricultural District Intake Form providing information about the property, ownership, acreage, soil types, and farming operation. The County reviews the application to verify eligibility requirements are met. If eligible, the County prepares an Agricultural Preservation District Agreement, which is a notarized legal document that runs with the land. The agreement must be signed by all current titled landowners and authorized representatives, notarized, and recorded in the Washington County Land Records. The agreement becomes effective upon recording. After ten years, landowners may request termination by submitting a Release and Termination document signed by all current titled owners, which must be recorded in the Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive program providing loans, grants, and financial assistance to agricultural businesses, operations, farmers, and rural enterprises in Washington County through MARBIDCO, USDA, and other funding sources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple financing and grant programs available: MARBIDCO Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund offers low-interest loans (2.25% initially) up to $250,000-$750,000 depending on project type; Rural Business Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund provides moderate-cost loans (5.25%) up to $100,000; Maryland Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Fruit Planting Loan Fund offers 4.50% loans up to $100,000; Forestry Equipment loans up to $150,000; Rural Business Energy Efficiency loans (4.50%) from $2,500-$30,000. Grant programs include Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (up to $10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Grant (competitive grants $2,500-$10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Matching Grant (up to $11,250-$25,000 matching support), Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program for down payments, Small Acreage Next Generation Program for 10-49 acre farms, and Maryland Market Money Program providing dollar-for-dollar match for SNAP/EBT/WIC/Senior FNMP purchases at farmers markets. USDA programs include Farmers Market Promotion Program ($50,000-$500,000 with 25% match), Local Food Promotion Program ($25,000-$500,000 with 25% match), Rural Development Grants ($10,000-$500,000), Value Added Producer Grants ($75,000-$250,000), Regional Food System Partnership Program ($100,000-$1,000,000 with 25% match), Community Food Projects ($35,000-$400,000 with 100% match), and Rural Energy for America Program for renewable energy and efficiency. Maryland Agriculture Water Quality Cost Share Program covers up to 87.5% of BMP installation costs ($50,000-$300,000). Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF) offers up to $40,000 for rural nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; USDA Community Food Projects applications available in April with June deadline; USDA VAPG offered annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses and operations, farmers, beginning/young farmers, rural enterprises, food processors, livestock producers, timber products processors, urban farmers, rural small businesses, nonprofits serving rural areas, and community colleges in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural business support including land and equipment purchases, construction, working capital, energy efficiency improvements, water quality best management practices, farmland acquisition, value-added product development, processing and marketing, farmers market expansion, rural transportation, business training, technical assistance, and agricultural education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County; some USDA programs apply to rural areas defined as territory not within 50,000+ population city boundaries and adjacent urbanized areas
requirements_list: Operate an agricultural business or operation in Washington County
MARBIDCO MRBIFF: Ag/RBI-industry enterprises for land acquisition or capital equipment
MARBIDCO Rural Business Loan Fund: Ag/RBI firms and producers (farmers)
MARBIDCO Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Fund: Landowners wanting to plant fruit-bearing vines/trees
MARBIDCO Forestry Fund: Forest products businesses
MARBIDCO Energy Efficiency Fund: Food and fiber producers/processors with third-party energy audit
MUACLIG: Urban farmers with commercial lender participation (bank, Farm Credit, or FSA)

MVAPG-CAO: Crop producer, agricultural cooperative, seafood/livestock processor, or timber processor in business minimum 2 years; must produce 'value-added' product with useful life 7+ years; hemp fiber processors eligible if in business before June 30, 2020
MVAPMG: Must be eligible under USDA VAPG Program
Next Gen Program: Beginning farmers purchasing farmland
SANG: Young/beginning farmers purchasing 10-49 acre farms
Maryland Market Money: SNAP/EBT/WIC/Senior FNMP benefit users at participating farmers markets
USDA FMPP: Develop direct producer-to-consumer markets
USDA LFPP: Develop local/regional food business enterprises as intermediaries
USDA RBDG: Small and emerging businesses in rural areas with 50 or fewer new employees and less than $1,000,000 projected annual revenues
USDA VAPG: Value-added agricultural product producers/processors
USDA RFSP: Partnerships connecting public/private resources for local/regional food systems
USDA CFP: Address food needs of low-income people or increase community self-reliance
USDA REAP: Agricultural producers and rural small businesses
MD Water Quality Cost Share: Farmers installing BMPs for water quality protection
MAERDAF: Rural-serving nonprofits promoting planning, economic development, agricultural/forestry education serving 2+ counties; community colleges supporting small/agricultural businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business Development at 240-313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net for details on specific programs. For MARBIDCO programs, contact MARBIDCO or county agricultural land preservation office. For USDA programs, visit program websites: FMPP (ams.usda.gov/services/grants/fmpp), LFPP (ams.usda.gov), RBDG (rd.usda.gov), VAPG (rd.usda.gov/programs-services/value-added-producer-grants/md), RFSP (ams.usda.gov/services/grants/rfsp), CFP (nifa.usda.gov). Maryland Market Money Program administered through Tri-County Council of Southern Maryland (TCCSMD) Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission. Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org) is a resource for funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program that provides funding to eligible entities for projects supporting economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity in the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to eligible entities for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development, supporting businesses and international exports), Ready Workforce (education, skills, health, and employment supports), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater, energy, and business development sites), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development, heritage tourism, outdoor recreation), and Leadership and Community Capacity (organizational skills, leadership development, and collaborative partnerships). Grants require a 50% match from other sources that must be identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Limited funding available; review committee may reduce funding amounts to allow maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded. Applicants should identify minimum ARC funding needed for project to move forward.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 for preliminary project submission; November 15 for formal grant application to Appalachian Regional Commission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities seeking to advance community and economic development in Washington County and the Appalachian region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Priority consideration given to projects in technology development, broadband, education and workforce development, tourism, energy, recovery ecosystems, and traditional infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; part of the Appalachian region
requirements_list: 50% project match from other funding sources required
Matching funds must be identified and committed at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
Project proposals must be submitted through Washington County Office of Grant Management
Projects should be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement and Maryland's State Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with numeric values and defined in the context of project activities
Projects should reference any plan and/or economic documents showing the project is part of overall plan for economic development
Commitment letters required for all matching funds with committed status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. The PPD should include project description, organizational capacity to administer federal grant, ARC investment goal, state objective and strategy alignment, performance measures with quantifiable outputs and outcomes with timeframes, and proposed funding sources. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners, then submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early fall inviting submission of a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with final application due by November 15. Review committee may reduce funding amounts to allow maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based on addressing specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners determines the annual allocation to be set aside for the Community Organization Fund, which for Fiscal Year 2027 is $1,200,000 distributed across priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive grants to support their charitable work and community services. Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter), and all funds must be expended within one fiscal year (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027). Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total request amount. Funding can support both operating and capital expenses/projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director, Office of Grant Management; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations within Washington County that are included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Public Local Laws § 1-108). Organizations must have an office located in Washington County and provide services within the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports programs and services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Funds may be used for operating expenses and/or capital projects. Endowments and funding for the benefit of individuals are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in and provide services to Washington County. Service priority areas align with countywide community needs: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Arts & Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, and Other.
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Organization must be a charitable organization recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with a 'Valid' status
Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be 'In Good Standing' at the time of application (proof required)
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must submit a recent audit (preferably) or a detailed financial statement
Organization must not have unpaid liens or judgments against the corporation or association
Organization must not have unpaid or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Organization must have submitted Grant Reports as required for any prior funding and have no outstanding obligations to the County
Application must be submitted during the published application window by the deadline
Organizations must demonstrate efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested
For capital projects, organization must be able to complete the project and expend all funds within one fiscal year given the quarterly disbursement schedule
Application must be complete, signed by an authorized representative, and include all required attachments
Organization must be in good standing at the time of submission with evidence included
If requesting multiple programs, a separate complete application must be submitted for each program
Hard copies and electronic submission must both be submitted by the due date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) annually during the budgeting process. The NOFA contains application procedures and opening and closing dates. Applications are available online on or about December 1, 2025. Applicants must complete the Community Organization Funding application packet including: Overview/Statement of Need (1 page), Past Performance (1 page), Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan (2 pages), Program Plan (4 pages), Collaborating Partnerships and Coordination of Services (1 page), Letters of Support, Budget Spreadsheet (FY27 Excel format), IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT Proof of Organization In Good Standing, most recent Audit or Financial Statement, copy of most recent IRS Form 990, and W-9 & Vendor Remittance Form (if applicable). Applicants must submit six hard paper copies (unsecured, no binders or tab dividers) and one electronic copy (combined PDF) by the published deadline. Hard copies should be placed in a manila envelope and may be mailed to the Office of Grant Management (100 W. Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740, Attn: Julie Mackereth, Senior Office Associate) or dropped off. Electronic copies must be emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net with the organization name as the PDF title. Applications received after the deadline will not be accepted regardless of postmark date. OGM staff will not check applications for accuracy or completeness at submission; applicants are responsible for verifying completeness using the submittal checklist. The COF Committee, consisting of OGM representatives and five BOCC-appointed members, reviews and ranks applications using a scoring rubric with criteria: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points) for a maximum of 100 points. Additional factors considered include total funding allocation, funding per priority area, geographic distribution, service duplication, and previous performance. The Board of County Commissioners determines final awards during the budget approval process (May-June 2026). Applicants will be notified in writing upon completion of the budgetary process. Technical assistance workshops are offered before the deadline, and OGM staff are available to answer questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund that reinvests cannabis sales tax revenue and business conversion fees into communities that were disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement prior to July 1, 2022. The fund supports community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from cannabis sales tax revenue and one-time cannabis business conversion fees to support community-based initiatives. Funds are maintained in a separate special revenue fund as restricted cash reserves and must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and programs serving low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in Washington County ZIP code 21740, which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities including mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, and housing assistance and homelessness prevention. Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted CRRF cannabis sales tax funds in Washington County may only be used for initiatives serving ZIP code 21740, which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas of the County.
requirements_list: Funds must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services
Programs must serve low-income communities or disproportionately impacted areas as defined in § 36–101
Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Washington County is developing application procedures and guidelines for eligible organizations. The County is continuing to gather community input and holding public hearings to establish the funding plan. Applicants should contact Grant Management for current application procedures and guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus. Established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation with $8 million in state Relief Act funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $8 million in state Relief Act funding distributed as grants to commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief for continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that works with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program to make conservation agreements permanent through state-funded conservation easements. Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts can add up to ten times the acreage of their contract to maximize land preservation and easement value. The program has protected 1,926 acres with $4,835,547 invested in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded conservation easements that make existing Federal Farm Service Agency CREP Contracts permanent. Landowners can extend their easement to include additional acreage up to ten times the original contract amount to maximize preservation and easement value. The program has protected 1,926 acres with $4,835,547 invested in Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners with existing Federal Farm Service Agency (FSA) CREP Contracts in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of permanent conservation easements on land enrolled in CREP contracts to protect agricultural and conservation lands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Must have an existing FSA CREP Contract in place
Landowner must be willing to sell easement
Easement remains effective in perpetuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts apply through the County's Land Preservation Office. The easement is processed and becomes permanent upon completion, remaining effective in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in the designated Enterprise Zones.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credits for job creation: $1,000 one-time maximum for most new jobs; $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees (as certified by Maryland Department of Labor). Local real property tax credits: 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for first five years, declining 10% per year for years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Credits apply to real property only. Exemption from commercial building excise tax on new construction within Enterprise Zones. Employees must work at least 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, spend at least 50% of work time in the Zone, and work at least six consecutive months before credit is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying businesses (proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations) that make job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones. Eligible business categories include: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, offices for corporate or regional headquarters, service industries, and mercantile or retail businesses (with special conditions).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for businesses investing in Enterprise Zones through job creation and capital improvements (construction of new buildings, building additions, renovations).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three state-designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: (1) City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, designated December 15, 1982, includes Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres, designated December 15, 1995, stretches from Pennsylvania border to Potomac River). Minimum qualifications vary by zone and district.
requirements_list: Business must be located in designated Enterprise Zone on designation date, relocated after designation, or started construction/expansion after designation
For income tax credits: minimum job creation requirements - Central Business District: 1 new job; Outside Central Business District: 5 new jobs; Hancock Zone: 1 new job
For real property tax credits: minimum capital investment requirements - Central Business District: $5,000+; Outside Central Business District: $50,000+; Hancock Zone: $5,000+
New employees must be hired after Zone designation date
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must be employed for at least six consecutive months
Employees must spend at least 50% of work time in Enterprise Zone or in activities directly related to the Zone
New jobs must not be replacement positions
Property improvements must be submitted for qualification before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits

Business activities must fall within eligible categories: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, offices for corporate or regional headquarters, service industries, or mercantile/retail (with restrictions)
Mercantile or retail businesses only eligible if located in Hancock Enterprise Zone or Central Business District of Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Determine property is located in a designated Enterprise Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2) For property tax credits: Submit completed Enterprise Zone Certification application (Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form) prior to project completion date. 3) For income tax credits: Submit completed application after hiring new employees, including 'New Jobs Created' form listing employees meeting requirements. 4) For income tax credits: Local Maryland Department of Labor Job Service Office reviews employee list to determine individual eligibility as 'disadvantaged' or 'non-disadvantaged.' 5) Washington County Department of Business Development sends approval letter or explanation of non-approval. 6) For property tax credits: Credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher to submit with payment. 7) For income tax credits: Claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR 'Enterprise Zone Tax Credit' with a copy of approval letter. To claim disadvantaged employee credits, contact Maryland Job Service Office (301-393-8200) before hiring to have employees referred and screened, or contact Job Service to screen employees already hired.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 in reimbursement for expenses associated with an international marketing project.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Gaming Commission distributes funds from the Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible 501(c)(3) charitable organizations. The fund is generated from tip jar gaming revenue, with 50% allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association and the remaining funds distributed to local charitable organizations. The Commission reviews applications and awards grants to support community initiatives in health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic and recreational activities, and educational and cultural activities in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are distributed from the Washington County Gaming Fund to qualified 501(c)(3) organizations. Maximum distribution per application is $100,000. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund. Award announcements are made during the Board of County Commissioners meeting in August, with funds disbursed several weeks after announcement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, May 6, 2020 by 3:00 P.M.
