structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Applications are released each April and submitted to the Office of Grant Management. (2) Download application packet from https://www.washco-md.net/grant-management/charitable-gaming-program/ (3) Complete all required forms including the Request for Funding application, financial statement, Gaming Fund Grant Report, and supporting documentation. (4) Submit complete electronic application via email to jmackereth@washco-md.net copying slapole@washco-md.net by 3:00 P.M. on May 6, 2020. No hard copies accepted. (5) Applications must include: REQUEST (signed application), FINANCIALS (most recent annual financial statement), GRPT (2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report with evidence of fund expenditure), DOC (supporting documentation if applicable), NORP (Notice of Responsible Person if applicable), and W-9 (completed IRS form and Washington County vendor forms). (6) Organizations may schedule a public hearing time with the Office of Grant Management on submission day or any day after submission up to June 12, 2020. (7) A Public Funding Hearing is held in June (June 23, 2020). (8) Gaming Commission reviews all applications and makes funding recommendations after public hearing and workshop. (9) Final awards announced during Board of County Commissioners meeting in August. (10) Award letters sent and funds disbursed several weeks after announcement. (11) Grant performance period is one year from award announcement. Organizations unable to spend funds as indicated should contact the Office of Grant Management for budget modification.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to organizations operating in Washington County for one-time projects or events that were not anticipated or budgeted. It helps address current financial issues or situations requiring prompt response and resolution. The funding is designed to assist organizations with projects or events that would not otherwise qualify for general fund Community Organization Funding or Hotel Rental Tax Funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000. The total cost of the event or project may exceed this amount, but no amount greater than the maximum award can be approved. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors for products or services. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of the completion of the event. The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. This portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating within Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events that require prompt response and resolution
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County only
requirements_list: Have an unexpected circumstance requiring prompt resolution
Have provided evidence that the request meets a critical need in the community
Do not have an alternative source of funding
Have proven to be a valuable community resource
Requests that benefit individuals are not eligible (does not exclude individuals participating in a group event, activity, or project)
Normal and routine operating and administrative expenses are not eligible
Organizations that support political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation are not eligible
For-profit ventures are not eligible
Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000
All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation within 60 days of the completion of the event or project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Submit the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application via the County's website at www.washco-md.net, or print and mail or email the application. All applications will be received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). Upon receipt, the OGM will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners; (4) Approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) Notify the applicant in writing as to the approval or denial of their request. All organizations receiving grant funding will be required to complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation to the OGM within 60 days of the completion of the event or project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake qualified historic preservation work on eligible historic properties. The program offers stackable credits at the county (25%), state (20%), and federal (20%) levels, with an additional 5% credit available for new construction attached to historic structures, totaling up to 70% in possible credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 25% county property tax credit available to property owners who complete qualified historic preservation work (rehabilitation, restoration, or renovation) on eligible historic properties within Washington County. The credit offsets costs associated with rehabilitation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has thoughtful, sympathetic design. An additional 5% credit is available for new construction attached to existing historic structures. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. The credit is stackable with state (20%) and federal (20%) tax credits, providing up to 70% in total possible credits. Qualified Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted before work starts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners with historic properties in Washington County historic districts or qualifying areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified historic preservation work on eligible historic properties, including roof repair and/or replacement, chimney repair and/or replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Structures must be within the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district, or be a contributing structure to a surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Village (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmantown). Properties with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay applied through rezoning qualify. Contributing structures located within Towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines also qualify. Properties must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a qualifying geographic area: Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district, a contributing structure to a surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Village, have the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoning designation, or be a contributing structure within a Town listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines
Property must be residential or commercial and documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must be rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has thoughtful and sympathetic design
Work must be consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Application must be submitted before work starts; any work started and/or completed prior to approval may not be eligible for the tax credit

Property owner must comply with all Federal, State and local laws applicable to the project, including zoning, building, and safety codes; review by easement holders such as Maryland Historical Trust; and applicable Federal, State and local licensing, permitting, and environmental requirements
For structures under Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Easement, a copy of the easement document must be included with the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts, all requiring signatures. Part I (Evaluation of Significance) is submitted first to determine if the structure qualifies for the tax credit. Properties with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay do not need to complete Part I unless there is a question about overlay inclusion. Part I must be reviewed and approved by staff for qualifying area and by the Historic District Commission (HDC) for project appropriateness. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) evaluates whether proposed work meets rehabilitation standards and must be approved BEFORE rehabilitation work begins. Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work) is submitted after project completion to certify that rehabilitation was completed as approved and to verify expenses. The application process timeline: (1) Initial Application - review by staff for qualifying area and by HDC for project appropriateness; (2) Work Begins - owner/contractor records progress with photos and maintains expense and receipt records; (3) Project Completion - owner notifies HDC of completion and supplies photos of completed work, staff conducts site visit if needed, and owner provides final documentation of expenses; (4) Credit Review - owner is notified of HDC meeting where documentation is reviewed and owner attendance is encouraged, HDC reviews all information to determine eligible expenses; (5) Credit Applied - credit amount is forwarded to Treasurer's Office for property bill updates. Completed applications and supporting documents should be mailed to: Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or emailed to askplanning@washco-md.net. For Part III, a written accounting of ALL project expenses (including ineligible expenses) must be completed on the provided spreadsheet with copies of invoices/receipts and proof of payment (with sensitive information redacted).

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to help Washington County organizations, agencies, and businesses develop tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects. The program is designed to assist organizations and agencies in undertaking activities that would not be possible without special funding and that have the potential to eventually succeed without continued financial assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county generates funds from a 6% hotel rental tax. These funds are invested back into the community through grants to support tourism, economic development, cultural, and recreational projects. Grants are paid directly to applicants, not to vendors. For requests of $25,000 or less, applications are approved by the Office of Grant Management with concurrence of the County Administrator. For requests exceeding $25,000, applications are forwarded to the County Commissioners for final approval. Any changes to approved line items exceeding 10% require approval from the Office of Grant Management. Unused funds must be returned to the County within 30 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects in Washington County. Projects may include tourism advertising, facility development, job creation initiatives, cultural and historical projects, and recreational activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Activities must have merit that can eventually succeed without financial assistance from this funding
Projects that generate overnight stays in the County are prioritized
Projects must encourage support of County businesses, restaurants and attractions
Projects must reach a broad segment of the community
Applicants should seek multiple sources of support rather than rely solely on Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Projects must yield benefits to the community for resources invested
Projects that promote cooperation among event organizers to reduce costs are prioritized
Individuals are not eligible applicants

Organizations with budget deficits prior to application are not eligible
Funding cannot be used for normal and routine operating and administrative expenses
Funding cannot be used for political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation
Funding cannot be used for endowments
Grant recipients must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation within 60 days of project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. The application can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed. Upon receipt, the Office of Grant Management will determine if the applicant and project are qualified and if the request meets funding goals. For requests of $25,000 and below, the Office of Grant Management will approve or deny the request with concurrence of the County Administrator. For requests exceeding $25,000, the application is processed and forwarded to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review, the County Commissioners will hear the request and may take action at their discretion. Applicants will be notified in writing of approval or denial. All grant recipients must submit a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county program designed to accelerate land preservation easement purchases by providing an alternative to upfront payment. Agricultural landowners sell their development rights to the County through installment purchase agreements with fixed interest rates paid over ten years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural preservation easements and pays landowners through installment agreements. Payment is made through an Installment Purchase Agreement over 10 years, with 10% of the principal paid at settlement plus interest, and 10% of the principal paid annually for the remaining 9 years at a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County with qualifying properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of agricultural preservation easements on contiguous agricultural land for permanent preservation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Must own agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Must agree to preserve all contiguous acreage except for one acre per existing dwelling
Easement covers entire contiguous acreage minus one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners meeting minimum qualifications apply to sell development rights easements to the County. The County makes an offer to purchase, and if accepted, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written specifying total payment amount and terms.

The program prioritizes non-emergency medical transportation, expansion of existing transportation networks, and last-mile solutions for underserved areas.

Washington County intends to award 1 to 3 grants with individual awards ranging from $10,000 to $40,000. Performance period: May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026. Funding can support non-emergency medical transportation services (direct transport for patients to and from primary care, dialysis, mental health services, or pharmacy pickups), expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services, and last-mile solutions for residents in underserved areas not reached by public transit.

Properties are ranked based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Easement restrictions remain permanent and effective in perpetuity. As of the data provided, the program has spent $49,855,542 to preserve 17,008 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county purchases development rights easements on agricultural land. Landowners receive payment for permanently restricting development on their property. As of the data provided, the program has spent $49,855,542 to preserve 17,008 acres in Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state financing program that provides loans, grants, and other financial assistance to businesses and local jurisdictions for economic development projects located in priority funding areas and eligible industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDAAF offers six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities—loans up to the lesser of $10 million or 20 percent of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity—loans up to $5 million or conditional loans and grants up to $2 million with local jurisdiction participation; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions—up to $3 million (or more for qualified distressed counties) for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development planning; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund—grants of up to $250,000 annually to capitalize local revolving loan funds; (5) Special Purposes Loan—funding for critical initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care Centers; (6) Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund)—financing for extraordinary opportunities with minimum applicant capital investment of five times the assistance amount. Assistance generally cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in priority funding areas and eligible industries, and local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, economic development planning, and project-specific financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located within a priority funding area. Projects in qualified distressed counties may receive higher maximum assistance.
requirements_list: Located in a priority funding area
Operating in an eligible industry sector (with some exceptions)
Project must meet program-specific eligibility criteria
Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs (with limited exceptions)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DBED for application procedures specific to the financing capability sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that facilitates private sector financing for economic development projects in priority funding areas by issuing revenue bonds and providing credit insurance.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA offers industrial revenue bonds and credit insurance. Taxable bonds provide long-term capital for fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds provide long-term capital at tax-exempt rates for 501(c)(3) non-profits, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects. Credit insurance includes a Conventional Program insuring up to 80 percent (not to exceed $2.5 million) or 90 percent for export transactions; a Bond Program insuring bonds up to 100 percent (not to exceed $7.5 million); and Linked Deposits providing certificates of deposit in certain rural high-unemployment areas to enable below-market-rate loans to eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations for fixed asset financing, and small businesses in rural high-unemployment areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fixed asset financing and long-term capital needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Linked Deposits available in certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment.
requirements_list: Located in a priority funding area
For tax-exempt bonds: must be 501(c)(3) non-profit, manufacturing facility, or certain solid waste project
For conventional credit insurance: transaction through a financial institution
For linked deposits: located in rural area with qualifying high unemployment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with financial institutions and MIDFA to structure appropriate financing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition (Next Gen) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program provided by the Maryland Agricultural Resource-Based Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that offers down payment assistance to young and beginning farmers purchasing agricultural properties that qualify for the County's Agricultural District program. The program provides 51% of a land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property (capped at $500,000) to assist buyers with purchase. After settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program within seven years, or the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Down payment assistance equal to 51% of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property, capped at $500,000, to assist buyers in purchasing qualifying agricultural properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers seeking to purchase agricultural properties that qualify for the County's Agricultural District program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for purchase of agricultural farmland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County; properties must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program
requirements_list: Buyer must be a young or beginning farmer
Property must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program
Buyer must provide a signed sales contract for the farm
After settlement, landowner must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program
Landowner must enroll in the County's Agricultural District program
If no permanent easement is procured within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers must provide a signed sales contract and complete an application in conjunction with the County's Land Preservation Office. The application is submitted to MARBIDCO. The process takes roughly six months to complete.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that helps elderly people and individuals with disabilities meet their transportation needs by providing general purpose transportation through vouchers that can be used with registered taxi providers at a reduced rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate that provide at least 50% savings compared to regular taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and are used to pay drivers directly. A set number of vouchers can be purchased each month. Vouchers expire on June 30 of each year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General purpose transportation via registered taxi providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or over OR have a disability
Must be unable to utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
If applicant is under age 60, application must be certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging the disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Application expires June 30 of every year and must be renewed annually to continue using the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Washington County Transit office at 240-313-2750 to request an application by mail, or visit the office at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD to pick one up in person. If under age 60, have a healthcare professional certify your disability on the application. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes are not accepted). You will be notified by mail of your eligibility. Once approved, purchase vouchers at the WCT office or by mail using business checks, money orders, or credit cards. Call registered service providers to schedule rides and pay the driver with your vouchers.

Properties are ranked based on property size, number of development rights, proximity to other easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics. Easement restrictions remain permanent. The program has protected 9,421 acres with $28,499,083 invested in Washington County.

Unlike the Next Gen program, there is no seven-year requirement to pursue a permanent easement — properties are permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of real estate settlement, eliminating the need for additional easement pursuits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Business Incentives Program (General Overview Booklet)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive tax incentives and business development assistance programs offered by Washington County and the City of Hagerstown to support business development, expansion, job creation, workforce training, and economic growth. Includes tax credits, revolving loan funds, grants, and access to workforce development resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentive programs available: (1) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program - 6 to 15 years of tax credits on County portion of real estate taxes based on job creation and capital investment; (2) New Jobs Tax Credit Program - 6-year tax credit (52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6) for businesses expanding/relocating with minimum 10,000 sq ft and 25 new jobs; (3) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program - 3-year tax credit of 0.4% of construction costs; (4) Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption - exempts R&D equipment from County Business Personal Property Tax; (5) Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption - exempts manufacturing equipment from County Business Personal Property Tax; (6) Business Inventory Tax Exemption - exempts inventory from County Business Personal Property Tax; (7) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) - real property tax credits of 50-70% of increased site value for 5 years (up to 10 years in Enterprise Zones); (8) C-PACE Program - commercial loans for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects with up to 100% fixed-rate financing and 20-year payback; (9) City of Hagerstown CDBG Microenterprise Grant Program - grants for microenterprises (5 or fewer employees); (10) Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund (HRLF) - loans up to $200,000 (80% of project cost) at LIBOR plus 1% (minimum 3%) for growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance; (11) Invest Hagerstown Grant Programs - City Center Redevelopment Grants ($150,000-$250,000), City-Wide Redevelopment Grants ($5,000-$25,000), Down Payment and Rehabilitation Grants ($7,500), Rental Property Rehabilitation Grants ($7,500); (12) Enterprise Zone Tax Credits - State income tax credits and local real property tax credits for job creation and capital investment; (13) Workforce Training & Development - training grants, apprenticeship programs, and custom training through multiple providers; (14) Partnership for Workforce Quality - matching training grants for manufacturing and technology companies; (15) Western Maryland Consortium - training reimbursement up to $4,500 per worker; (16) Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program - tax credits and financial incentives for hiring apprentices.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development; City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development Department
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located or planning to locate in Washington County and City of Hagerstown; existing businesses seeking to expand; job creators; manufacturers; technology companies; microenterprises; developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business operations and development, expansion, capital improvements, workforce training, manufacturing machinery and equipment, research and development, energy efficiency and renewable energy projects, building renovation and construction, façade enhancement, employee recruitment and retention, code compliance, working capital, land improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; specific incentives available in Enterprise Zones (Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone covering approximately 5,000 acres including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park and downtown Hagerstown; Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone covering 1,500 acres); Priority Funding Areas designated in Title 5, Subtitle 7B of the State Finance and Procurement Article; Foreign Trade Zone #255 (approximately 1,700 acres at Hagerstown Regional Airport, Williamsport, Hopewell Valley, Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade, and Hancock). City of Hagerstown programs require location within corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown.
requirements_list: New Jobs Tax Credit: minimum 10,000 square feet expansion/new construction; minimum 25 new permanent full-time employees at new/expanded premises; 50% of new jobs must pay at least 135% of average weekly wage per Washington County worker; location in Priority Funding Area

Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credit Section 4(a): existing business must obtain at least 1,500 square feet of new or expanded premises; must employ at least one new permanent full-time employee during 12-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credit Section 4(b): must obtain at least 2,500 square feet; must employ at least five additional new permanent full-time employees during 24-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credit Section 4(c): must invest $10,000,000 in capital improvements; must create 100 new permanent full-time employees

Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund: business sales must be less than $5 million annually for each of the last two years; minimum loan amount $10,000; maximum loan amount $200,000 or 80% of project cost whichever is less; for each $35,000 borrowed, one full-time job must be created or retained within two years

CDBG Microenterprise Grant Program: business must be located in corporate boundaries of City of Hagerstown or have at least two-thirds of business occur in Hagerstown for roving businesses; must have five or fewer total employees including owner(s); must be private for-profit business; must be in good standing with City and State; must be in compliance with all City regulations; must be established and operating for at least 12 months at time of application (or provide business plan and business counseling documentation)
Enterprise Zone businesses: eligible for State income tax credits and local real property tax credits for job creation and capital investments
BRIP: site must be located in participating jurisdiction; must be owned by inculpable person; real property tax credit of 50-70% of increased value for 5 years (up to 10 years in Enterprise Zones)
C-PACE Program: for commercial businesses and nonprofits; must invest in energy efficiency, renewable energy, or water conservation projects
Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program: qualifying projects must be approved parcels; entitled to priority plan review and deferral of County Site Plan application and review fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development at (240) 313-2280 or www.washco-md.net/business-development for information on specific tax incentive programs and Enterprise Zone benefits. For City of Hagerstown programs, contact the City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development Department. CDBG Microenterprise Grant Program applicants should download complete guidelines and application forms from the program website. Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund applicants must submit application with credit check and non-refundable application fee based on requested loan amount; download complete guidelines and application forms from program website. Invest Hagerstown Grant Program applicants download complete guidelines and application forms from program website. C-PACE Program loans administered through Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) agent Abacus Property Solutions; apply at www.md-pace.com/. Workforce training and development assistance available through multiple providers including Hagerstown Community College (240-500-2476), Pittsburgh Institute of Aeronautics (240-347-4805), Associated Builders & Contractors (301-739-1190), University System of Maryland-Hagerstown (240-527-2727), Washington County American Job Center (301-393-8200), Maryland Department of Labor Apprenticeship program (443-615-4758), Partnership for Workforce Quality (443-447-4999), and Western Maryland Consortium (301-791-3164).

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides up to a fifteen year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program includes three tiers based on investment and job creation levels, offering meaningful tax relief to businesses that demonstrate a commitment to economic development. It helps attract new companies and supports existing companies that expand in Washington County.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to fifteen years of tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program offers three tiers: TIER ONE (existing business, expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft., create at least 5 new FTEs within 12 months) receives 3 years of credits at 55%, 40%, 25%; TIER TWO (new business, at least 2,500 sq. ft., create at least 25 new FTEs within 24 months) receives 6 years at 55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25%; TIER THREE (new or existing business, invest at least $20M in capital improvements, create at least 200 new FTEs within 24 months with 80% paid at 200% of Maryland State minimum wage) receives 15 years at 75% for the first five years, then reduced by 5% annually until reaching 25%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete or before occupying space or hiring employees
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation requirements. Businesses located in Enterprise Zones are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate tax credit on the increased assessed property value for newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied eligible properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible for this program.
requirements_list: Must be located in Washington County (Priority Funding Area)
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone
Apply before occupying space, hiring employees, or completing construction
Newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied property that is owned or leased
Tier 1 (Existing Business): Expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 5 new full-time jobs within 12 months
Tier 2 (New Business): Obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of space and create at least 25 new full-time jobs within 24 months

Tier 3 (New or Existing Business): Invest at least $20,000,000 in capital improvements and create at least 200 new full-time jobs within 24 months, with 80% paid at 200% of Maryland State minimum wage
Upon construction completion, notify DBED with square footage documentation

Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1st each year with employee information including name, last four digits of SSN or ID number, home city/state, start and end dates, annual salary, hours worked, and benefits information
Continue to meet all applicable program requirements for each year receiving the tax credit
If leased, lessor must reduce taxes by the amount of credit for which business qualifies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Submit a letter of intent and official application before completing construction or acquiring space/hiring employees. 2) Provide a detailed description of the project, including square footage and location. 3) Specify number of full-time jobs to be created and anticipated occupation date. 4) Upon construction completion, notify DBED with square footage documentation. 5) Create required full-time employees within specified timeframe (12 months for Tier 1, 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3). 6) Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1st each year. 7) Receive certification from Washington County DBED.
